**Pattern 401: `page.route()` + `route.fulfill({ json })` Fault-Injection Oracle for Error-State Exploration** [official]
Intercept specific API endpoints and return controlled error responses (500, 429, 404, empty arrays, malformed JSON) to systematically explore the application's error handling, empty-state rendering, and retry logic — without needing a backend test harness or feature flags.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const faultScenarios = [
  { status: 500, body: { error: 'Internal Server Error' }, label: 'server-error' },
  { status: 429, body: { error: 'Rate limit exceeded' }, label: 'rate-limited' },
  { status: 200, body: [], label: 'empty-list' },
  { status: 200, body: null, label: 'null-body' },
] as const;

for (const scenario of faultScenarios) {
  test(`dashboard handles ${scenario.label} from /api/widgets`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.route('**/api/widgets**', route =>
      route.fulfill({ status: scenario.status, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify(scenario.body) })
    );

    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    // Oracle: no raw JSON or stack traces should ever reach the user
    const bodyText = await page.locator('body').innerText();
    expect(bodyText).not.toMatch(/\{"error":/);
    expect(bodyText).not.toMatch(/at\s+\w+\s+\(/); // stack trace pattern

    await page.screenshot({ path: `fault-${scenario.label}.png` });
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: `route.fulfill()` with `json` option bypasses real network latency and authentication checks — the fault scenario tests the client's rendering logic but cannot reveal server-side error-propagation bugs; complement with contract tests that verify the real API actually returns well-formed error envelopes.

**Pattern 402: `page.waitForRequest()` Predicate Charter for Verifying Request Payload Integrity** [official]
Use `page.waitForRequest()` with a predicate function to assert that user interactions produce the correct HTTP request bodies — catching cases where UI state drift, optimistic update bugs, or multi-step form data loss causes a silent wrong-payload submission.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('profile save sends correct payload including optional fields', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile/edit');

  // Set up the request watcher before triggering the action
  const saveRequestPromise = page.waitForRequest(req =>
    req.url().includes('/api/profile') &&
    req.method() === 'PUT'
  );

  await page.getByLabel('Display Name').fill('Alice Explorer');
  await page.getByLabel('Bio').fill('QA engineer');
  await page.getByLabel('Website').fill('https://alice.dev');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save Profile' }).click();

  const saveRequest = await saveRequestPromise;
  const payload = saveRequest.postDataJSON();

  expect(payload).toMatchObject({
    displayName: 'Alice Explorer',
    bio: 'QA engineer',
    website: 'https://alice.dev',
  });
  // Assert optional field is not stripped
  expect(payload).toHaveProperty('website');
  expect(payload.website).not.toBe('');
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.waitForRequest()` with a predicate times out (default 30 s) if the matching request never fires — always pair it with `Promise.race([saveRequestPromise, page.waitForTimeout(5000)])` in exploratory harnesses where the button may be unexpectedly disabled, or use `{ timeout: 10000 }` to fail fast; also note that Playwright matches against the initial request URL, so redirect chains require a predicate on `.url().includes(...)` rather than an exact URL string.

**Pattern 403: `devices` Registry + `isMobile` Context Flag Layered Emulation Charter** [official]
Combine Playwright's built-in device descriptors with per-test overrides to create a layered emulation matrix — testing both preset device profiles and edge-case combinations that no real device perfectly represents (e.g., tablet UA with phone viewport, or phone UA with no touch support disabled).
```typescript
import { test, expect, devices } from '@playwright/test';

const emulationMatrix = [
  { ...devices['iPhone 14'], label: 'iphone14-preset' },
  { ...devices['Pixel 7'], label: 'pixel7-preset' },
  // Edge case: tablet UA but constrained viewport
  {
    ...devices['iPad Pro 11'],
    viewport: { width: 375, height: 667 },
    label: 'ipad-ua-phone-viewport',
  },
  // Edge case: desktop UA but touch enabled
  {
    userAgent: devices['Desktop Chrome'].userAgent,
    viewport: { width: 390, height: 844 },
    isMobile: true,
    hasTouch: true,
    label: 'desktop-ua-touch-enabled',
  },
];

for (const config of emulationMatrix) {
  test(`navigation renders correctly on ${config.label}`, async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext(config);
    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/');
    await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeVisible();
    const hamburger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /menu/i });
    const isNarrow = config.viewport!.width < 768;
    if (isNarrow) {
      await expect(hamburger).toBeVisible();
    } else {
      await expect(hamburger).not.toBeVisible();
    }
    await context.close();
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Playwright's device descriptors are versioned snapshots — the `userAgent` strings in `devices['iPhone 14']` may lag behind real Safari releases by one or two minor versions, causing UA-sniffing code to classify the emulated device incorrectly; always cross-check `navigator.userAgent` via `page.evaluate()` against the actual UA your production analytics show for the target device.

**Pattern 404: `context.setOffline(true)` + `context.setOffline(false)` Network Oscillation Oracle for Resilience Exploration** [official]
Toggle network connectivity programmatically mid-session to explore how the application handles flapping connections — revealing missing loading states, broken retry logic, data loss on reconnect, and offline indicator UI bugs that only surface during transient rather than permanent offline conditions.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('form data is preserved across a network outage during submission', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await page.goto('/feedback');
  await page.getByLabel('Subject').fill('Network resilience test');
  await page.getByLabel('Message').fill('This was typed before the network dropped.');
  await page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Subscribe to updates' }).check();

  // Cut network just before submission
  await context.setOffline(true);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click();

  // Oracle: offline indicator should appear
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /offline|no connection/i })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 })
    .catch(() => console.warn('No offline indicator found — potential UX gap'));

  // Restore network after 2 seconds
  await page.waitForTimeout(2000);
  await context.setOffline(false);

  // Oracle: form data should not be lost on reconnect
  await expect(page.getByLabel('Subject')).toHaveValue('Network resilience test');
  await expect(page.getByLabel('Message')).toHaveValue('This was typed before the network dropped.');
  await expect(page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: 'Subscribe to updates' })).toBeChecked();
});
```
Tradeoff: `context.setOffline(true)` blocks all TCP connections at the browser level, simulating a complete network loss rather than a slow or intermittent connection — it does not test partial failure scenarios (e.g., only the API endpoint is unreachable while the CDN is available); for partial failures use `page.route()` to abort specific URL patterns while leaving others unaffected.

**Pattern 405: `page.evaluate()` + `localStorage` Seeded-State Charter for Deep-Feature Exploration** [official]
Pre-seed `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` with controlled state (feature flags, onboarding completion markers, cached API responses, user preferences) before navigating, allowing an exploratory session to begin in a specific application state without navigating through the onboarding flow or waiting for real data to load.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore dashboard with seeded user preferences and cached data', async ({ page }) => {
  // Seed state before navigation so it is available on first load
  await page.goto('about:blank');
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    localStorage.setItem('user_prefs', JSON.stringify({
      theme: 'dark',
      dashboardLayout: 'compact',
      dismissedTours: ['welcome', 'analytics', 'export'],
    }));
    localStorage.setItem('feature_flags', JSON.stringify({
      newExportDialog: true,
      betaAnalytics: false,
    }));
    sessionStorage.setItem('last_viewed_report', 'report-42');
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Oracle: seeded preferences should be reflected immediately
  await expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('dashboard-layout')).toHaveAttribute('data-layout', 'compact');

  // Oracle: dismissed tours should not re-appear
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /welcome tour/i })).not.toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: Seeding `localStorage` via `page.evaluate()` on `about:blank` before the real navigation is effective only for keys that the application reads on boot — state that is read lazily (e.g., after a user interaction triggers a module load) can be seeded more safely via `page.addInitScript()` which runs before every navigation, ensuring the seed is present regardless of when the application reads it.

---

**Pattern 406: `page.ariaSnapshot()` Structural Regression Oracle for Accessibility-Critical Flows** [official]
Capture the ARIA accessibility tree as a YAML snapshot at key interaction points during an exploratory session to detect structural regressions — missing `aria-label` attributes, role changes after re-renders, focus-trap breakdowns, and landmark restructuring that visual screenshots miss.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore modal open/close cycle and verify ARIA structure', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile');

  // Baseline ARIA snapshot before modal opens
  await expect(page.locator('body')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - main:
      - heading "Profile Settings" [level=1]
      - button "Edit Profile"
  `);

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Edit Profile' }).click();

  // After open: dialog must be present with correct structure
  await expect(page.locator('body')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - main:
      - heading "Profile Settings" [level=1]
    - dialog "Edit Profile":
      - heading "Edit Profile" [level=2]
      - textbox "Display Name"
      - textbox "Bio"
      - button "Save"
      - button "Cancel"
  `);

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Cancel' }).click();

  // After close: dialog must be gone and focus must return to trigger
  await expect(page.locator('body')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - main:
      - heading "Profile Settings" [level=1]
      - button "Edit Profile"
  `);
  // Verify focus returned to trigger button
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Edit Profile' })).toBeFocused();
});
```
Tradeoff: `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` performs an exact structural match by default — even a cosmetically innocuous change like adding an `aria-describedby` attribute to the dialog will cause a snapshot mismatch; use the `{ message }` option and re-generate snapshots deliberately with `--update-snapshots`, and treat every snapshot diff as a deliberate accessibility review rather than a routine update.

---

**Pattern 407: `page.emulate({ colorScheme: 'dark' })` + `toHaveScreenshot()` Dark-Mode Contrast Oracle** [official]
Combine color scheme emulation with visual screenshot comparison to systematically explore dark-mode rendering quality — catching insufficient text contrast, missing dark-mode asset variants, hardcoded light-mode color leaks, and focus-ring invisibility issues.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const colorSchemes = ['light', 'dark'] as const;
const criticalPages = ['/login', '/dashboard', '/settings', '/checkout'];

for (const scheme of colorSchemes) {
  for (const path of criticalPages) {
    test(`${scheme} mode visual oracle: ${path}`, async ({ browser }) => {
      const context = await browser.newContext({
        colorScheme: scheme,
        viewport: { width: 1280, height: 800 },
      });
      const page = await context.newPage();
      await page.goto(path);

      // Wait for fonts and layout paint to settle
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

      // Capture full-page screenshot for visual diff
      await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot(`${scheme}-${path.replace(/\//g, '_')}.png`, {
        fullPage: true,
        threshold: 0.02, // 2% pixel diff tolerance for anti-aliasing
      });

      // Programmatic contrast check via evaluate
      const lowContrastElements = await page.evaluate(() => {
        const results: string[] = [];
        document.querySelectorAll('p, h1, h2, h3, label, button, a').forEach(el => {
          const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
          const color = style.color;
          const bg = style.backgroundColor;
          // Flag elements with both color and bg as rgba(0,0,0,0) (transparent on transparent)
          if (color === bg && color !== 'rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)') {
            results.push(el.tagName + ': ' + el.textContent?.slice(0, 40));
          }
        });
        return results;
      });
      expect(lowContrastElements, 'Potential same-color text/bg pairs').toHaveLength(0);
      await context.close();
    });
  }
}
```
Tradeoff: `toHaveScreenshot()` diffs are pixel-based and font rendering varies across OS and GPU — running dark-mode visual oracles on Linux CI while developing on macOS will produce consistent failures due to sub-pixel rendering differences; always generate baseline screenshots on the same CI environment that will run the comparisons, and use `--update-snapshots` on a dedicated baseline run rather than locally.

---

**Pattern 408: `page.route()` + `route.continue({ headers })` Auth-Header Mutation Charter for Permission-Boundary Exploration** [official]
Intercept outbound API requests and mutate the `Authorization` header mid-session to explore permission boundaries — swapping tokens between roles, stripping auth entirely, inserting expired or malformed tokens — without re-authenticating through the UI, enabling rapid systematic exploration of authorization logic.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const authScenarios = [
  { label: 'no-auth', header: undefined },
  { label: 'expired-token', header: 'Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJleHAiOjF9.invalid' },
  { label: 'viewer-role-token', header: 'Bearer VIEWER_STATIC_TEST_TOKEN' },
  { label: 'wrong-tenant', header: 'Bearer CROSS_TENANT_TEST_TOKEN' },
] as const;

for (const scenario of authScenarios) {
  test(`admin endpoint rejects ${scenario.label}`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.route('**/api/admin/**', async route => {
      const headers = { ...route.request().headers() };
      if (scenario.header === undefined) {
        delete headers['authorization'];
      } else {
        headers['authorization'] = scenario.header;
      }
      await route.continue({ headers });
    });

    await page.goto('/admin/users');

    // Oracle: unauthorized access must not render sensitive data
    await expect(page.getByRole('table')).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 })
      .catch(() => {});
    const body = await page.locator('body').innerText();
    expect(body).not.toMatch(/user@example\.com/);
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Auth-header mutation via `route.continue()` tests the API layer's authorization enforcement, but it does not test the UI's own permission-gating logic (e.g., whether the "Admin Users" nav item is hidden for viewer-role users) — always complement network-layer auth mutation with separate UI-layer role-switch tests using `storageState` seeded with role-specific auth sessions.

**Pattern 409: `page.keyboard.press('Tab')` Focus-Chain Recorder for Keyboard Navigation Exploration** [official]
Programmatically walk the focus chain by pressing `Tab` repeatedly and recording the focused element at each step — generating a focus-order map that surfaces missing `tabindex`, focus-trap failures, skip-link effectiveness, and focus-sink bugs (elements that receive focus but are not visually focused).
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore focus chain on login form', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  // Move focus to the page body to start from the top
  await page.locator('body').press('Tab');

  const focusChain: Array<{ tag: string; role: string | null; label: string | null; index: number }> = [];
  const MAX_TABS = 30;

  for (let i = 0; i < MAX_TABS; i++) {
    const focused = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
      return {
        tag: el.tagName,
        role: el.getAttribute('role'),
        label: el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 40) ?? null,
        id: el.id,
      };
    });
    if (!focused) break;
    focusChain.push({ ...focused, index: i });
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  }

  console.log('Focus chain:', JSON.stringify(focusChain, null, 2));

  // Oracle: interactive elements must appear in a logical sequence
  const labels = focusChain.map(f => f.label);
  const emailIdx = labels.findIndex(l => l?.match(/email/i));
  const passwordIdx = labels.findIndex(l => l?.match(/password/i));
  const submitIdx = labels.findIndex(l => l?.match(/sign in|log in|submit/i));

  expect(emailIdx, 'Email field must be in focus chain').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0);
  expect(passwordIdx, 'Password field must follow email in focus chain').toBeGreaterThan(emailIdx);
  expect(submitIdx, 'Submit button must follow password in focus chain').toBeGreaterThan(passwordIdx);
});
```
Tradeoff: Tab-walking via `page.keyboard.press('Tab')` is synchronous-sequential and will stall on focus-trap dialogs that have not been opened — if an interactive element triggers an overlay on focus (e.g., a tooltip-powered help icon), the chain recorder will spin on the same overlay; add a guard that detects repeated focus on the same element (same `id` twice consecutively) and breaks the loop or logs a "focus-sink detected" warning.

---

**Pattern 410: `page.on('request')` + `page.on('response')` Paired Streaming Request Log for Full-Session Network Audit** [official]
Register both `request` and `response` event listeners before the session begins to build a complete chronological request log — capturing URL, method, status, timing, and request size — which serves as a post-session oracle for detecting unexpected third-party calls, tracking pixel fires, unintended data exfiltration, and N+1 API call patterns.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface RequestEntry {
  url: string;
  method: string;
  status: number | null;
  durationMs: number | null;
  requestBodySize: number;
}

test('audit network activity during checkout session', async ({ page }) => {
  const requestLog: RequestEntry[] = [];
  const pending = new Map<string, { startTime: number; bodySize: number }>();

  page.on('request', req => {
    pending.set(req.url(), {
      startTime: Date.now(),
      bodySize: (req.postData() ?? '').length,
    });
  });

  page.on('response', async res => {
    const entry = pending.get(res.url());
    pending.delete(res.url());
    requestLog.push({
      url: res.url(),
      method: res.request().method(),
      status: res.status(),
      durationMs: entry ? Date.now() - entry.startTime : null,
      requestBodySize: entry?.bodySize ?? 0,
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Checkout' }).click();
  await page.getByLabel('Card Number').fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place Order' }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/order-confirmation**');

  // Oracle: no third-party analytics calls should carry PII
  const thirdPartyWithPII = requestLog.filter(r =>
    !r.url.includes('example.com') &&
    r.requestBodySize > 0
  );
  console.log('Third-party requests with body payload:', thirdPartyWithPII);

  // Oracle: no 5xx errors during checkout
  const serverErrors = requestLog.filter(r => r.status !== null && r.status >= 500);
  expect(serverErrors, '5xx errors during checkout').toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Streaming all requests via `page.on()` introduces a small memory cost per entry in long sessions and does not capture requests initiated by Service Workers unless `serviceWorkers: 'block'` is set or the browser is Chromium with Service Worker routing enabled; for sessions requiring Service Worker request visibility, use `context.on('request')` in combination with `context.route('**', route => { ... route.continue() })` which forces all requests through the routing layer and makes them visible.

---

**Pattern 411: `page.screenshot({ clip })` Region-Focused Evidence Capture for Defect Documentation** [official]
Capture clipped screenshots of specific UI regions rather than full-page screenshots to produce precise, low-noise defect evidence — isolating the exact element cluster that exhibits the bug without including unrelated page content that confuses triage readers.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

async function captureDefectEvidence(
  page: import('@playwright/test').Page,
  locator: import('@playwright/test').Locator,
  label: string,
  paddingPx = 16
) {
  const box = await locator.boundingBox();
  if (!box) throw new Error(`Element not found for defect evidence: ${label}`);
  await page.screenshot({
    path: `evidence/${label}.png`,
    clip: {
      x: Math.max(0, box.x - paddingPx),
      y: Math.max(0, box.y - paddingPx),
      width: box.width + paddingPx * 2,
      height: box.height + paddingPx * 2,
    },
  });
}

test('explore error state rendering and capture defect evidence', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/api/profile', route =>
    route.fulfill({ status: 500, body: JSON.stringify({ error: 'Server error' }) })
  );

  await page.goto('/profile');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Load Profile' }).click();

  const errorAlert = page.getByRole('alert');
  await errorAlert.waitFor({ state: 'visible' });

  // Capture a tight clip around just the error message region
  await captureDefectEvidence(page, errorAlert, 'profile-load-error-state');

  // Also capture the full action area for context
  const actionArea = page.getByTestId('profile-action-area');
  if (await actionArea.isVisible()) {
    await captureDefectEvidence(page, actionArea, 'profile-action-area-error-context', 32);
  }

  expect(errorAlert).toBeDefined(); // placeholder; real oracle checks message quality
});
```
Tradeoff: Clipped screenshots depend on `locator.boundingBox()` which returns `null` for elements with `display: contents` or zero-dimension flex/grid children — always add a `null` guard and fall back to a full-page screenshot with an annotation overlay rather than silently producing no evidence; also note that `clip` coordinates are in CSS pixels which differ from physical pixels on high-DPI screens, so add `page.viewportSize()` context to defect reports.

---

**Pattern 412: `expect.poll()` Async Convergence Oracle for Eventually-Consistent State Exploration** [official]
Use `expect.poll()` to repeatedly evaluate a condition until it converges or times out — ideal for exploring eventually-consistent state (search index staleness, async job completion, WebSocket push updates, optimistic UI rollback) where the expected state is not immediately observable after the triggering action.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore search index freshness after content creation', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/articles/new');
  await page.getByLabel('Title').fill('Exploratory Testing Convergence ' + Date.now());
  await page.getByLabel('Content').fill('Testing async convergence patterns.');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Publish' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toContainText(/published/i);

  const articleTitle = await page.getByLabel('Title').inputValue();

  // Navigate to search and poll until the new article appears in results
  await page.goto('/search');
  await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill(articleTitle);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Search' }).click();

  // Oracle: article must appear in search results within 15 seconds
  await expect.poll(
    async () => {
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Search' }).click();
      await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
      return page.getByRole('article').filter({ hasText: articleTitle }).count();
    },
    {
      message: `Article "${articleTitle}" did not appear in search results within 15s`,
      timeout: 15_000,
      intervals: [1000, 2000, 3000],
    }
  ).toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `expect.poll()` retries the entire async function including page actions (clicks, navigation) — if the polled function has side effects (e.g., submitting a form on each call) the retries will replay those effects multiple times; always make the poll function purely observational (read-only assertions, no writes) and separate the triggering action into a one-shot step before the poll block.

---

**Pattern 413: `browser.newContext({ storageState })` Parallel Multi-Role Session Charter for Cross-Role Interaction Exploration** [official]
Create multiple browser contexts from pre-seeded storage states representing different user roles, then run parallel exploratory actions across those contexts to discover cross-role interaction bugs — data leakage between roles, notification visibility mismatches, and shared-resource conflict conditions that single-role sessions never surface.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore shared document with concurrent admin and viewer sessions', async ({ browser }) => {
  // Load pre-seeded auth states (generated by setup scripts)
  const adminContext = await browser.newContext({ storageState: 'playwright/.auth/admin.json' });
  const viewerContext = await browser.newContext({ storageState: 'playwright/.auth/viewer.json' });

  const adminPage = await adminContext.newPage();
  const viewerPage = await viewerContext.newPage();

  // Both navigate to the same shared document
  await Promise.all([
    adminPage.goto('/docs/shared-charter-001'),
    viewerPage.goto('/docs/shared-charter-001'),
  ]);

  // Admin edits the document title
  await adminPage.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 }).dblclick();
  await adminPage.keyboard.selectAll();
  await adminPage.keyboard.type('Updated by Admin');
  await adminPage.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }).click();

  // Oracle: viewer should see the updated title (real-time sync)
  await expect
    .poll(() => viewerPage.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 }).textContent(), { timeout: 8000 })
    .toMatch(/Updated by Admin/);

  // Oracle: viewer must not see the admin's edit toolbar
  await expect(viewerPage.getByRole('toolbar', { name: /edit/i })).not.toBeVisible();

  // Admin deletes the document
  await adminPage.getByRole('button', { name: /delete document/i }).click();
  await adminPage.getByRole('button', { name: 'Confirm Delete' }).click();

  // Oracle: viewer's page must show a graceful "document deleted" state, not an error
  await expect
    .poll(() => viewerPage.locator('body').innerText(), { timeout: 6000 })
    .toMatch(/deleted|no longer available/i);

  await adminContext.close();
  await viewerContext.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: Running multiple browser contexts in a single test body increases memory consumption linearly — on memory-constrained CI runners (< 4 GB RAM), allocating 3+ contexts with full page state can exhaust available memory and cause flaky OOM failures; prefer using Playwright's `test.describe.parallel()` with `storageState` in the project config to distribute multi-role sessions across worker processes rather than instantiating all contexts in a single test body.

### Community Gotchas

**G50. Registering `page.on('console', handler)` after `await page.goto()` silently drops all console messages that fired during page boot — including React/Vue hydration errors, missing polyfill warnings, and failed initial API fetches that run before `DOMContentLoaded` completes.**
A team building an error oracle for a Next.js application registered `page.on('console', ...)` immediately after `page.goto('/')` resolved and observed zero console errors across all sessions, even though browser DevTools showed four hydration errors per page load. Investigation revealed that Next.js fires `console.error()` for hydration mismatches during the synchronous React render phase, which completes before Playwright's post-`goto()` listener attachment. The team added `page.addInitScript(() => { const orig = console.error; console.error = (...args) => { orig(...args); window.__earlyErrors = window.__earlyErrors || []; window.__earlyErrors.push(args.join(' ')); }; })` before `goto()` to intercept early errors and drain `window.__earlyErrors` after navigation. WHY: Playwright's `page.on('console')` listener is attached asynchronously after the `goto()` promise resolves, meaning any synchronous console calls that complete during the navigation phase are never delivered to the Node.js handler; always register console and pageerror listeners before the first navigation call.
Fix: Register all `page.on()` listeners immediately after `await browser.newPage()` and before any `page.goto()` call; supplement with `page.addInitScript()` shims for synchronous boot-time errors.

---

**G51. `page.route()` with `route.fulfill()` does not intercept requests that originate from a Service Worker — SW-initiated fetches bypass the Playwright routing layer entirely on Chromium unless `serviceWorkers: 'block'` is set in the browser context options.**
A team mocking API responses for a PWA found that their `page.route('**/api/**', ...)` handlers were being called for desktop browser requests but silently bypassed for the same URLs when the Service Worker was active and serving cached responses. The `page.on('request')` log showed no matching requests because the SW intercepted them at the browser network layer before they reached Playwright's routing interception point. The fix was either to set `{ serviceWorkers: 'block' }` in `browser.newContext()` to prevent SW registration entirely during testing, or to add a SW bypass header (`X-Playwright-Route: bypass`) that the SW was instructed to pass through via a `sw.js` test hook. WHY: Playwright's network routing intercepts at the CDP `Fetch.enable` / `Network.enable` level, which sits above the SW fetch handler in Chromium's network stack — Service Worker fetch events are handled before requests leave the renderer and therefore never reach Playwright's interception layer.
Fix: Set `serviceWorkers: 'block'` in `browser.newContext()` for tests that rely on `page.route()` mocking, or instrument the Service Worker with a passthrough header that it checks before intercepting requests.

---

**G52. `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' })` will match multiple elements and throw an "strict mode violation" error if two visually distinct buttons share the same accessible name — a common situation in item lists where each row has its own "Save" button, or in multi-step forms where a "Save Draft" and "Save and Continue" button are abbreviated to "Save" in their `aria-label`.**
A team exploring a settings page with three sections each containing a "Save" button found that `page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' })` threw `Error: strict mode violation — getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' }) resolved to 3 elements`. The buttons were structurally identical from an ARIA standpoint despite being in visually separate card sections. The fix was to scope the locator using `page.getByRole('region', { name: 'Notifications' }).getByRole('button', { name: 'Save' })` to narrow the scope to the specific section under exploration. WHY: Playwright's `getByRole()` searches the entire accessibility tree by default and enforces strict mode (exactly one match) for actions — duplicate accessible names across sibling regions are an accessibility defect (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name) as well as a test authoring trap; treat the strict mode error as both a test fix signal and an accessibility defect to file.
Fix: Scope role-based locators to their nearest landmark or region using chained locators (`.getByRole('region', { name: '...' }).getByRole('button', { name: '...' })`), and file an accessibility defect for duplicate accessible names on interactive controls.

---

**G53. `context.clearCookies()` + `page.reload()` does not fully simulate a logged-out state for applications that store session tokens in `localStorage` or `sessionStorage` — clearing cookies alone leaves storage-based tokens in place, and the application's auth check on reload reads from storage first, short-circuiting the cookie check.**
A team testing session expiry behavior called `context.clearCookies()` followed by `page.reload()` expecting the application to redirect to the login page, but the application remained authenticated. Investigation showed the auth token was stored in `localStorage` under the key `auth_token` as a JWT, with cookies used only as a fallback for server-side rendering. Clearing cookies did not touch `localStorage`, so the SPA re-authenticated silently on reload. The fix was to add `await page.evaluate(() => { localStorage.clear(); sessionStorage.clear(); })` before `page.reload()` to ensure all client-side auth state was wiped. WHY: Modern SPAs increasingly use `localStorage` as the primary token store for performance and cross-tab sharing reasons, demoting cookies to an SSR-only concern — exploratory tests that assume cookie clearing equals full session reset will produce false-green auth bypass results for this architecture.
Fix: Always combine `context.clearCookies()` with `page.evaluate(() => { localStorage.clear(); sessionStorage.clear(); })` for a complete client-side auth state reset, and verify the reset by asserting `page.evaluate(() => localStorage.getItem('auth_token'))` returns `null` before reloading.

---

**G54. `page.dragAndDrop(source, target)` silently succeeds (returns without error) even when the drop is rejected by the application — the method resolves as soon as the pointer-up event fires, not when the application's `drop` event handler resolves its async business logic, meaning a rejected drag (e.g., dragging a file type that is not accepted) appears identical to a successful drag in the Playwright API.**
A team exploring a Kanban board's drag-and-drop restrictions found that `page.dragAndDrop('[data-card="blocked-item"]', '[data-column="done"]')` returned without error even though the application's business rule prevented "blocked" items from being moved to "done". The `drop` event handler dispatched an async API call and then visually rolled back the item on failure, but by the time the rollback completed, `page.dragAndDrop()` had already resolved. The fix was to add an explicit state oracle after the drag: `await expect(page.locator('[data-card="blocked-item"]').locator('..')).toHaveAttribute('data-column', 'in-progress')` which asserts the card remained in its original column, catching the visual rollback as the intended behavior. WHY: Playwright's drag-and-drop API resolves at the browser pointer-event level (mousedown → mousemove → mouseup), not at the application's async business-logic level — any post-drop validation, animation, or API call that determines the final state occurs after the method returns; always add an explicit post-drag state assertion rather than treating a non-error return as success.
Fix: After every `page.dragAndDrop()` call, explicitly assert the final expected state of both the dragged element (it moved to the correct location, or remained in place if the drop was expected to be rejected) rather than relying on the absence of a thrown error as a success oracle.

## Cycle 56 — 2026-05-14

### New Patterns

**Pattern 414: `page.addLocatorHandler()` Proactive Overlay Auto-Dismissal** [official]
Overlay elements (cookie banners, chat bubbles, survey modals, permission prompts) appear at unpredictable points during exploratory sessions and cause "element is obscured" failures on otherwise valid interactions. `page.addLocatorHandler()` registers a handler that fires automatically whenever the matching element becomes visible, dismissing the overlay before Playwright retries the blocked action — without requiring the tester to predict when the overlay appears.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore checkout flow with unpredictable overlays', async ({ page }) => {
  // Register overlay handlers before navigation — they persist for the session lifetime
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('button', { name: /accept cookies/i }),
    async (btn) => { await btn.click(); },
  );
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /rate your experience/i }),
    async (dialog) => {
      await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: /dismiss/i }).click();
    },
  );

  await page.goto('/shop');
  // All subsequent interactions proceed without manual overlay handling
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Laptop Pro 15' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to Cart' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Checkout' }).click();

  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order summary/i })).toBeVisible();
  console.log('Overlay handlers fired:', await page.evaluate(() => window.__overlayDismissals ?? 0));
});
```
Tradeoff: Handlers registered with `addLocatorHandler()` are checked on every actionability retry — in pages with many `MutationObserver`-driven DOM updates, the check polling can measurably slow down session wall time; scope the locator predicate as tightly as possible (e.g., `getByRole('button', { name: /exact text/i })` rather than `locator('.modal button')`) to reduce false-positive handler triggers during DOM-heavy sessions.

---

**Pattern 415: `page.route()` + `route.fetch()` Response-Body Mutation Oracle** [official]
Modifying API response bodies in-flight lets exploratory sessions verify UI resilience to malformed, truncated, or semantically unexpected server payloads without requiring backend changes. `route.fetch()` retrieves the real response and `route.fulfill()` delivers the mutated version, keeping the session anchored to real network paths while injecting targeted data anomalies.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore dashboard resilience to partial user profile response', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.route('**/api/v1/user/profile', async (route) => {
    const response = await route.fetch();
    const body = await response.json();

    // Simulate a backend returning a profile with missing required fields
    const mutated = { ...body, displayName: undefined, avatarUrl: null, roles: [] };
    await route.fulfill({
      status: 200,
      contentType: 'application/json',
      body: JSON.stringify(mutated),
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Oracle: UI should degrade gracefully — show a placeholder, not a crash
  await expect(page.getByRole('img', { name: /avatar/i })).toHaveAttribute(
    'src',
    /placeholder|default/i,
  );
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).not.toContainText('[object Object]');
  await expect(page.locator('body')).not.toContainText('TypeError');
  console.log('Mutated profile oracle passed — no crash or raw JS error in UI');
});
```
Tradeoff: `route.fetch()` makes a real outbound network request to the origin server, meaning the test requires a live backend (or a running dev server) — this approach is not suitable for fully offline mocking; use `route.fulfill()` with a static fixture body when the backend is unavailable, accepting that fixture drift must be managed separately.

---

**Pattern 416: `page.clock.install()` + `clock.fastForward()` Token-Expiry Exploration** [official]
JWT and session token expiry scenarios are impossible to explore in real-time (tokens typically expire after 15–60 minutes). `page.clock.install()` replaces all browser time APIs (`Date`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `performance`) with a controllable clock, and `clock.fastForward()` advances time by an arbitrary amount, triggering expiry handlers without actually waiting.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore session expiry UX — token expires after 30 minutes of inactivity', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  // Install the clock BEFORE any navigation — mandatory requirement
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-05-14T10:00:00Z') });

  await page.goto('/app');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('hunter2');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Log In' }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /dashboard/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Advance time by 31 minutes — triggers the app's inactivity timeout handler
  await page.clock.fastForward('31:00');

  // Oracle: application must prompt for re-authentication, not silently fail API calls
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /session expired/i })).toBeVisible({
    timeout: 5000,
  });
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in again/i })).toBeEnabled();

  // Verify that mid-session data is not lost — form fields should persist
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in again/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByLabel('Email')).toHaveValue('user@example.com');
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.clock.install()` replaces `performance.now()` and `requestAnimationFrame`, which can break CSS animations and libraries that rely on the native animation frame scheduler (e.g., React's `useTransition`, Framer Motion) — if the UI under exploration uses animation-gated state transitions, use `clock.setFixedTime()` (which leaves timers running naturally) instead of `install()` to avoid animation-scheduler interference.

---

**Pattern 417: `page.waitForResponse()` Predicate + `request.postDataJSON()` Payload Integrity Charter** [official]
Exploratory sessions that trigger form submissions or CRUD actions should verify both the HTTP response and the outgoing request payload. `page.waitForResponse()` with a predicate function can capture any matching response while simultaneously making the intercepted request available for payload inspection via `response.request().postDataJSON()`.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore create-order payload integrity — verify what the UI actually sends', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.goto('/orders/new');

  // Prime the payload capture before the user action
  const responsePromise = page.waitForResponse(
    (res) => res.url().includes('/api/orders') && res.request().method() === 'POST',
  );

  await page.getByLabel('Product').selectOption('Widget A');
  await page.getByLabel('Quantity').fill('3');
  await page.getByLabel('Shipping Address').fill('123 Main St, Springfield');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Place Order' }).click();

  const response = await responsePromise;
  const requestPayload = response.request().postDataJSON();
  const responseBody = await response.json();

  // Payload integrity oracles
  expect(requestPayload.quantity).toBe(3);
  expect(requestPayload.shippingAddress).toMatch(/123 Main St/);
  expect(requestPayload).not.toHaveProperty('internalUserId'); // PII leak check

  // Response contract oracles
  expect(response.status()).toBe(201);
  expect(responseBody.orderId).toMatch(/^ORD-[0-9]+$/);
  console.log('Order payload oracle passed — orderId:', responseBody.orderId);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.waitForResponse()` with a URL + method predicate will block the test indefinitely if the matching request is never made — this surfaces as a timeout rather than a clear assertion failure; always pair it with a reasonable timeout option (`{ timeout: 10000 }`) and log a descriptive message so session debriefs can distinguish "action did not trigger the API" from "API responded too slowly."

---

**Pattern 418: `page.context().setOffline(true)` + `context.setOffline(false)` Network Oscillation Oracle** [official]
Real-world users experience intermittent connectivity drops. Toggling `context.setOffline()` during an active session probes whether the application handles mid-action disconnections gracefully — specifically: does it queue mutations, show an offline indicator, and replay when connectivity returns, or does it silently discard in-flight work?
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore offline resilience — mid-save disconnection and recovery', async ({
  browser,
}) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/editor');

  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Document' }).fill('Draft content — saved offline');

  // Simulate connection drop just before the auto-save fires
  await context.setOffline(true);
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).click();

  // Oracle 1: UI must acknowledge offline state, not show "Saved" falsely
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toContainText(/offline|unsaved|pending/i);

  // Oracle 2: no JavaScript errors from the failed fetch
  const errors = await page.pageErrors();
  const networkErrors = errors.filter((e) => /network|failed to fetch/i.test(e.message));
  expect(networkErrors).toHaveLength(0); // Errors should be handled, not unhandled exceptions

  // Restore connectivity and verify the queued save completes
  await context.setOffline(false);
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toContainText(/saved|synced/i, { timeout: 8000 });

  await context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: `context.setOffline(true)` blocks all network requests at the browser context level, including background service-worker syncs, analytics beacons, and feature-flag polling — applications that depend on background network activity for state management (e.g., Firebase Realtime Database keep-alive pings) may enter unexpected states that are not representative of a real "phone goes to airplane mode" scenario; for more surgical network simulation, combine with `page.route()` to block only specific origin patterns rather than all traffic.

---

**Pattern 419: `locator.filter({ hasText, has })` Disambiguation in List Exploration** [official]
Exploratory sessions on list-heavy UIs (data tables, item cards, notification feeds) frequently need to interact with a specific row or card. Chaining `.filter()` on a list locator scopes subsequent actions to the matching item without resorting to fragile `nth()` index selection or overly specific CSS selectors.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore notification list — mark only urgent items as read', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/notifications');

  const notificationItems = page.getByRole('listitem').filter({
    has: page.getByRole('img', { name: /urgent/i }),
  });

  const urgentCount = await notificationItems.count();
  console.log(`Found ${urgentCount} urgent notifications to explore`);

  // Interact with each urgent item individually
  for (let i = 0; i < urgentCount; i++) {
    const item = notificationItems.nth(i);
    const title = await item.getByRole('heading').textContent();
    await item.getByRole('button', { name: /mark as read/i }).click();

    // Oracle: each item transitions to read state
    await expect(item).toHaveClass(/read/);
    console.log(`Marked as read: "${title}"`);
  }

  // Oracle: urgent count badge must reach zero
  await expect(page.getByRole('status', { name: /urgent/i })).toContainText('0');
});
```
Tradeoff: `.filter({ has: locator })` evaluates the inner locator relative to each candidate element — on large lists (500+ items), this performs a subtree locator query per candidate, which can cause visibly slow exploration sessions in the browser; for performance-sensitive list exploration, consider filtering server-side via URL parameters before the session begins, using `.filter()` only for final disambiguation on the narrowed result set.

---

**Pattern 420: `page.evaluate()` + `window.__playwright_coverage` Custom Exploration-Coverage Beacon** [community]
Standard code coverage tools (Istanbul/V8) require test-runner integration and do not emit per-session coverage maps for exploratory runs. Injecting a lightweight beacon script via `addInitScript()` tracks which application modules or feature flags are exercised during a free-form session, giving explorers a structured artifact to report alongside session notes.
```typescript
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';

test('explore onboarding flow — coverage beacon', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    window.__explorationBeacon = { events: [] as string[] };
    // Patch analytics events as a proxy for feature coverage
    const origTrack = (window as any).analytics?.track?.bind((window as any).analytics);
    if (origTrack) {
      (window as any).analytics.track = (event: string, props: unknown) => {
        window.__explorationBeacon.events.push(event);
        origTrack(event, props);
      };
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/onboarding');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /get started/i }).click();
  await page.getByLabel('Company Name').fill('Acme Corp');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next/i }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /invite team/i }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /skip for now/i }).click();

  const beacon = await page.evaluate(() => window.__explorationBeacon);
  fs.writeFileSync(
    `exploration-coverage-${Date.now()}.json`,
    JSON.stringify(beacon, null, 2),
  );
  console.log('Events exercised during session:', beacon.events);
});
```
Tradeoff: Patching `analytics.track` as a coverage proxy only captures explicitly instrumented user events — untouched features that have no analytics calls (often internal admin screens or developer-facing utilities) appear invisible in the beacon; supplement with `page.coverage.startJSCoverage()` (Chromium only) for byte-level V8 JS coverage when completeness is required over portability.

---

**Pattern 421: `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders()` Exploration-Mode Header Injection** [official]
Embedding a recognizable header (e.g., `X-Exploration-Session: <sessionId>`) in all browser requests during an exploratory run allows server-side logs and APM tools to filter and correlate exactly the traffic generated by that specific session, making debrief and root-cause analysis dramatically faster.
```typescript
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import { randomUUID } from 'crypto';

test('explore search feature — with correlation header', async ({ page }) => {
  const sessionId = `explore-${randomUUID()}`;

  // Inject session correlation header into every request the page makes
  await page.setExtraHTTPHeaders({
    'X-Exploration-Session': sessionId,
    'X-Tester': 'playwright-exploratory',
  });

  console.log(`[Session] Correlation ID: ${sessionId}`);
  console.log('[Session] Filter server logs with: grep X-Exploration-Session=', sessionId);

  await page.goto('/search');
  await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('quantum');
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  await page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().includes('/api/search'));

  // Explore result pagination
  for (let pageNum = 1; pageNum <= 3; pageNum++) {
    const results = page.getByRole('listitem').filter({ has: page.getByRole('link') });
    const count = await results.count();
    console.log(`Page ${pageNum}: ${count} results`);
    if (await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next page/i }).isEnabled()) {
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next page/i }).click();
      await page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().includes('/api/search'));
    } else break;
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `setExtraHTTPHeaders()` injects headers into ALL requests including third-party analytics, CDN assets, and external font requests — servers that validate or whitelist headers may reject or log unexpected header names as security events; scope the injection by combining with `page.route()` to add the header only to same-origin API requests when third-party header leakage is a concern.

---

**Pattern 422: `page.on('requestfailed')` Network-Failure Oracle During Sessions** [official]
Silent network failures (DNS errors, connection resets, CORS rejections) corrupt exploratory sessions without surfacing in the UI. Registering a `requestfailed` handler before navigation accumulates all failed requests, enabling a session-end oracle that asserts no critical paths (API calls, fonts, critical JS chunks) failed silently.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore user profile page — no silent network failures', async ({ page }) => {
  const failedRequests: Array<{ url: string; failure: string }> = [];

  page.on('requestfailed', (request) => {
    // Filter out expected failures (e.g., blocked analytics)
    const url = request.url();
    if (!url.includes('analytics.example.com')) {
      failedRequests.push({
        url,
        failure: request.failure()?.errorText ?? 'unknown',
      });
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/profile/123');
  await page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Activity' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('tab', { name: 'Settings' }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /edit profile/i }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /cancel/i }).click();

  // Session-end oracle: assert no unexpected network failures occurred
  if (failedRequests.length > 0) {
    console.warn('Failed requests:', JSON.stringify(failedRequests, null, 2));
  }
  expect(failedRequests, 'Unexpected network failures during session').toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `requestfailed` fires for aborted requests as well as genuine network errors — Playwright internally cancels prefetch/preload requests when navigating away from a page, generating false-positive failure events for background resource hints; filter out `net::ERR_ABORTED` failure texts when registering the handler to avoid false-positive session failures from normal prefetch cancellation.

---

**Pattern 423: `page.getByRole()` with `{ description }` Option for ARIA-Described Controls** [official]
The `description` option in `getByRole()` (Playwright v1.44+) matches elements by their `aria-describedby` text rather than their label — useful for exploring controls whose accessible name is generic ("Upload", "Edit") but whose description provides meaningful context ("Upload your profile photo" vs "Upload a document").
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore file upload flows — discriminate by aria description', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/documents/new');

  // Two upload buttons share the accessible name "Upload" but have distinct descriptions
  const profilePhotoUpload = page.getByRole('button', {
    name: 'Upload',
    description: /profile photo/i,
  });
  const documentUpload = page.getByRole('button', {
    name: 'Upload',
    description: /supporting document/i,
  });

  // Verify both are present and independently operable
  await expect(profilePhotoUpload).toBeEnabled();
  await expect(documentUpload).toBeEnabled();

  // Explore document upload with an oversized file
  const [fileChooser] = await Promise.all([
    page.waitForEvent('filechooser'),
    documentUpload.click(),
  ]);
  await fileChooser.setFiles({
    name: 'huge-file.pdf',
    mimeType: 'application/pdf',
    buffer: Buffer.alloc(52 * 1024 * 1024), // 52 MB — over typical 50 MB limits
  });

  // Oracle: size validation error must be scoped to the document upload, not the photo upload
  await expect(documentUpload.locator('..').getByRole('alert')).toContainText(/too large/i);
  await expect(profilePhotoUpload.locator('..').getByRole('alert')).not.toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `{ description }` matching requires that the target element actually has a valid `aria-describedby` pointing to a rendered DOM node with matching text — if the description text is rendered dynamically (e.g., loaded from an i18n bundle after mount), the locator will fail with "no element found" during early page load; use `await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded')` before resolving description-based locators on i18n-heavy pages.

---

**Pattern 424: `page.request` Context-Level API Client for Backend-State Setup** [official]
Exploratory sessions that require specific server-side state (pre-populated cart, activated trial, flagged content) should establish that state via API calls rather than UI flows, keeping session time focused on the area under exploration. `page.request` exposes the same `APIRequestContext` used in API testing, with session cookies automatically shared.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore checkout — pre-seed cart via API, explore from cart onward', async ({
  page,
  request,
}) => {
  // Authenticate via API — faster than UI login flow
  const loginResponse = await request.post('/api/auth/login', {
    data: { email: 'tester@example.com', password: 'test-password' },
  });
  expect(loginResponse.ok()).toBeTruthy();

  // Pre-seed the cart with multiple product types
  await request.post('/api/cart/items', { data: { productId: 'PROD-001', quantity: 2 } });
  await request.post('/api/cart/items', { data: { productId: 'PROD-DIGITAL-007', quantity: 1 } });
  await request.post('/api/cart/promotions', { data: { code: 'EXPLORE10' } });

  // Navigate directly to checkout — session cookies from request context carry over
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  await expect(page.getByRole('list', { name: /cart items/i })).toContainText('2×');
  await expect(page.getByRole('list', { name: /cart items/i })).toContainText('Digital');
  await expect(page.getByText(/EXPLORE10/i)).toBeVisible();

  // Explore shipping address validation with invalid inputs
  await page.getByLabel('ZIP Code').fill('00000');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue to payment/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText(/invalid zip/i);
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.request` for state setup assumes API endpoints exist and are stable for test use — if the backend enforces rate limiting, CSRF tokens, or IP-based restrictions on the test environment, API-based setup may fail intermittently; always confirm with the backend team that the setup endpoints are explicitly allowlisted for test environments, and have a UI-based fallback charter for scenarios where API setup is unavailable.

---

**Pattern 425: `expect(page).toHaveURL()` + `page.waitForURL()` Navigation Boundary Oracle** [official]
Multi-step flows (checkout, onboarding, wizards) should arrive at predictable URLs after each step. Asserting the URL pattern after each interaction catches premature navigation (step skipped), stalled navigation (step did not complete), and incorrect routing (wrong branch taken).
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore password-reset wizard — verify all URL transitions are correct', async ({
  page,
}) => {
  await page.goto('/auth/forgot-password');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/forgot-password$/);

  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /send reset link/i }).click();

  // Step 1 → 2: confirmation screen
  await page.waitForURL(/\/forgot-password\/sent/, { timeout: 8000 });
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading')).toContainText(/check your email/i);

  // Simulate clicking the reset link from email (deep link to token endpoint)
  await page.goto('/auth/reset-password?token=test-token-abc123');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/reset-password\?token=/);

  await page.getByLabel('New Password').fill('Str0ng!Pass#2026');
  await page.getByLabel('Confirm Password').fill('Str0ng!Pass#2026');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /reset password/i }).click();

  // Final step: must redirect to login, not dashboard (security oracle)
  await page.waitForURL(/\/auth\/login/, { timeout: 8000 });
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText(/password updated/i);
  // Oracle: confirm NOT redirected to authenticated area — reset must require fresh login
  await expect(page).not.toHaveURL(/\/dashboard/);
});
```
Tradeoff: `toHaveURL()` performs an exact or regex match against the full URL including query parameters and fragments — in SPAs that append tracking parameters (`?ref=email&campaign=reset`) to deep links, the URL assertion may fail due to unexpected query string additions by the marketing stack; use a permissive regex pattern that anchors only the path segment (`/\/reset-password/`) rather than a full URL match to avoid brittle failures from dynamically appended tracking parameters.

---

**Pattern 426: `test.step()` with Timeout for Bounded Charter-Step Execution** [official]
Long exploratory sessions split into named steps with `test.step()` give session reporters a structured timeline. Adding per-step timeouts via `test.step('name', fn, { timeout })` prevents any single exploration branch from blocking the entire session, making charter branching safer to implement.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore admin dashboard — bounded charter steps', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/admin');

  await test.step('Explore user management section', async () => {
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Users' }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('table')).toBeVisible();
    const rowCount = await page.getByRole('row').count();
    console.log(`User table has ${rowCount - 1} rows`); // subtract header
    await page.getByRole('searchbox', { name: /search users/i }).fill('admin');
    await page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().includes('/api/users'));
  }, { timeout: 20000 }); // cap this step at 20s — move on if it hangs

  await test.step('Explore audit log section', async () => {
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Audit Log' }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /audit/i })).toBeVisible();
    const entries = page.getByRole('row').filter({ has: page.getByRole('cell') });
    const entryCount = await entries.count();
    console.log(`Audit log has ${entryCount} visible entries`);
    await entries.first().getByRole('button', { name: /details/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();
    await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  }, { timeout: 15000 });

  await test.step('Explore system settings', async () => {
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: 'Settings' }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('form')).toBeVisible();
    const fields = await page.getByRole('textbox').count();
    console.log(`Settings form has ${fields} text inputs to explore`);
  }, { timeout: 10000 });
});
```
Tradeoff: Per-step timeouts make individual steps fail-fast but do not propagate context about what was accomplished before the timeout — session debriefs may see a step failure without knowing how far into the step exploration had progressed; add `console.log()` breadcrumbs inside long steps so the Playwright trace viewer's timeline shows the last action completed before the timeout, preserving session context even when a step is cut short.

---

**Pattern 427: `page.screenshot({ animations: 'disabled' })` Stable Visual Evidence Capture** [official]
Animated UI elements (spinners, progress bars, skeleton loaders, CSS transitions) cause screenshot-based defect evidence to capture mid-animation frames that misrepresent the actual rendered state. Setting `animations: 'disabled'` freezes all CSS and Web Animations API transitions at their start state, producing deterministic screenshots that accurately reflect what a still user would see.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as path from 'path';

async function captureStableEvidence(
  page: import('@playwright/test').Page,
  label: string,
): Promise<void> {
  await page.screenshot({
    path: path.join('session-evidence', `${label}-${Date.now()}.png`),
    animations: 'disabled',   // Freeze CSS animations at start state
    caret: 'hide',             // Hide text insertion carets for clean screenshots
    fullPage: false,           // Viewport only — avoids capturing invisible overflow
  });
}

test('explore data table — capture stable evidence at each interaction', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports/sales');
  await captureStableEvidence(page, '01-initial-load');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /filter/i }).click();
  await page.getByLabel('Date Range').selectOption('last-30-days');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /apply/i }).click();
  await page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().includes('/api/reports'));
  await captureStableEvidence(page, '02-filtered');

  await page.getByRole('columnheader', { name: 'Revenue' }).click(); // Sort
  await captureStableEvidence(page, '03-sorted-by-revenue');

  await expect(page.getByRole('table')).toBeVisible();
  console.log('Evidence screenshots captured in session-evidence/');
});
```
Tradeoff: `animations: 'disabled'` stops animations at their initial keyframe (0%), not their final state — for progress indicators that are intended to show completion (e.g., a progress bar filled to 100% after an operation), the screenshot will show the empty/start state of the animation rather than the visually meaningful final state; for completion-state evidence, await the animation's natural end using `await page.waitForFunction(() => el.getAnimations().every(a => a.playState === 'finished'))` before capturing.

---

**Pattern 428: `browserContext.tracing.start()` + `tracing.stop()` Inline Charter Trace Recording** [official]
The Playwright Trace Viewer provides a complete DOM snapshot, network log, action timeline, and console history for any recorded session. Starting a trace at charter entry and saving it on session end (or on assertion failure) produces an artifact that supports deep asynchronous debrief without requiring the session to be re-run.
```typescript
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import * as path from 'path';

test('explore payment flow — full trace evidence', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext();

  await context.tracing.start({
    screenshots: true,   // Embed viewport screenshots at each action
    snapshots: true,     // Capture full DOM snapshots for Trace Viewer
    sources: true,       // Include source file links (requires source maps)
  });

  const page = await context.newPage();

  try {
    await page.goto('/checkout/payment');
    await page.getByLabel('Card Number').fill('4111 1111 1111 1111');
    await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/28');
    await page.getByLabel('CVV').fill('123');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
    await page.waitForURL(/\/confirmation/, { timeout: 15000 });
    console.log('Payment flow completed — trace available for debrief');
  } finally {
    // Always save trace — even on failure — for session debrief
    const tracePath = path.join('session-traces', `payment-${Date.now()}.zip`);
    await context.tracing.stop({ path: tracePath });
    console.log(`Trace saved to: ${tracePath}`);
    await context.close();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Enabling `snapshots: true` captures full DOM snapshots at every action, which increases trace file size dramatically (a 50-action session can produce a 20–80 MB zip); for long exploratory sessions (100+ actions), disable `snapshots` and rely on `screenshots: true` alone for a more compact trace artifact, switching to `snapshots: true` only when re-running a specific charter for deep-debrief purposes.

---

**Pattern 428b: `page.exposeFunction()` Real-Time Error Beacon from Browser Context** [official]
Libraries that swallow exceptions internally (charting libraries, complex form frameworks, animation engines) never surface errors to `page.on('pageerror')`. Exposing a Node.js callback via `page.exposeFunction()` and calling it from an `addInitScript()` error boundary bridges the browser-to-Node gap for errors that would otherwise be invisible to the session observer.
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('explore rich-text editor — capture swallowed library errors', async ({ page }) => {
  const swallowedErrors: string[] = [];

  // Expose a Node.js callback that the browser can invoke
  await page.exposeFunction('__captureLibraryError', (msg: string) => {
    swallowedErrors.push(msg);
    console.warn('[Library Error]', msg);
  });

  // Instrument the editor library's error handler before page load
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    window.addEventListener('error', (e) => {
      (window as any).__captureLibraryError(`Global error: ${e.message} at ${e.filename}:${e.lineno}`);
    });
    window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', (e) => {
      (window as any).__captureLibraryError(`Unhandled rejection: ${String(e.reason)}`);
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/editor/rich-text');
  await page.getByRole('textbox').fill('Hello, World!');
  await page.keyboard.selectAll();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /bold/i }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /insert image/i }).click();
  await page.keyboard.press('Escape'); // Cancel without choosing image

  // Session-end oracle
  expect(swallowedErrors, 'Library errors detected during session').toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `exposeFunction()` creates a named function on the `window` object that is visible to any script running in the page — if the application under exploration uses a Content Security Policy that restricts `eval` or `unsafe-eval`, the exposed function may not be callable from inline scripts injected via `addInitScript()`; verify that the test environment's CSP allows `addInitScript()` injections, or relax the CSP header specifically for the test origin using `page.route()` response header mutation.

---

### Community Gotchas

**Gotcha G55: `page.waitForSelector()` with `state: 'visible'` resolves immediately if the element exists in the DOM but has `visibility: hidden` set via a CSS class — Playwright's "visible" state checks for non-zero bounding box and `display` not being `none`, but does NOT check the `visibility` CSS property.**
Teams exploring modal dialogs or slide-out panels that use `visibility: hidden` for their closed state (a common pattern in CSS-transition-based show/hide implementations that avoids layout reflow) found that `waitForSelector('.panel', { state: 'visible' })` resolved the instant the page loaded because the panel had `display: block; visibility: hidden` — the element occupied space in the layout but was visually invisible. The test then proceeded to click elements inside the invisible panel, which appeared to succeed but had no visible effect on screen. WHY: Playwright's actionability check defines "visible" as `offsetWidth > 0 && offsetHeight > 0 && display !== 'none'` — the `visibility` CSS property is explicitly excluded from this check because it is not part of the ARIA visibility model used by assistive technologies; a `visibility: hidden` element can still receive focus and be programmatically clicked, which is valid behavior in some accessibility patterns.
Fix: Assert `toBeVisible()` (which does include the `visibility` check via computed styles) rather than `waitForSelector(..., { state: 'visible' })`, or add `expect(locator).not.toHaveCSS('visibility', 'hidden')` as an explicit precondition before interacting with show/hide elements.

---

**Gotcha G56: `page.getByLabel()` does not match labels connected via `aria-labelledby` that reference elements outside the form field's subtree — only explicit `<label for="id">` associations and implicit label wrapping are matched.**
A team exploring a complex form built with a custom design system found that `page.getByLabel('Billing Address')` could not locate the address textarea even though the label was visually correct. The design system implemented labels as `<div id="billing-label">Billing Address</div>` with the textarea having `aria-labelledby="billing-label"`. Because the label div was not a `<label>` element and did not use `for="..."`, Playwright's `getByLabel()` traversal did not find the association. The team switched to `page.getByRole('textbox', { name: 'Billing Address' })`, which resolves the accessible name via the full ARIA name computation algorithm including `aria-labelledby`. WHY: Playwright's `getByLabel()` resolves labels using the HTML `<label>` association algorithm (explicit `for`, implicit wrapping) — it does not run the full ARIA accessible name computation that considers `aria-label` and `aria-labelledby`; use `getByRole()` with a `name` option when the label is implemented via ARIA attributes rather than native HTML label elements.
Fix: Prefer `page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /billing address/i })` over `page.getByLabel()` for form controls in design systems that use `aria-labelledby` on non-`<label>` elements; file a design system accessibility defect for non-semantic labeling if WCAG 1.3.1 compliance is required.

---

**Gotcha G57: `page.fill()` on a `<input type="number">` silently truncates string values that are not parseable as numbers — `page.fill('input[type=number]', 'abc')` results in an empty field, not the string 'abc', making input validation exploration for number fields deceptively silent.**
A team exploring input validation for a pricing field found that their attempt to inject non-numeric values using `page.fill('[data-field="price"]', 'not-a-number')` produced no visible change in the field — it appeared empty after `fill()`, and the form's validation logic never triggered the expected error state because the browser treated the field as having no value. The team assumed the validation was broken, but it was actually the `type="number"` attribute that silently rejected the non-numeric string at the browser input level before the application's validator could see it. WHY: The browser's `<input type="number">` element ignores programmatic assignment of non-numeric strings via the `value` setter (both in real user interaction and via `HTMLInputElement.value =`), which is how Playwright's `fill()` method ultimately sets the value — the sanitization happens at the DOM level, not the application level; exploratory testing of number field validation must use `page.evaluate()` to bypass this sanitization, or must test via keyboard input that triggers the browser's native numeric rejection UX.
Fix: Use `page.evaluate((el, val) => { Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype, 'value').set.call(el, val); el.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true })); }, await page.locator('[data-field="price"]').elementHandle(), 'abc')` to bypass the number sanitization and deliver non-numeric strings to the application's validation handler.

---

**Gotcha G58: `expect(locator).toHaveText()` matches against the element's `.innerText`, which excludes text inside `<script>`, `<style>`, and hidden elements, but INCLUDES text from `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements rendered by CSS — causing unexpected extra whitespace or bullet characters in the matched string.**
A team asserting notification text with `expect(page.getByRole('listitem')).toHaveText('3 new messages')` encountered intermittent failures with the actual value reported as `• 3 new messages`. The bullet character was injected by a `li::before { content: '• '; }` CSS rule in the design system's list styles. Because `innerText` includes pseudo-element rendered content in Chromium, the `toHaveText()` assertion received the extra character and failed the exact match. WHY: `innerText` (and by extension Playwright's `toHaveText()`) reflects the visual rendering of the element including CSS-generated content from `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements — this is correct browser behavior per the CSSOM specification, but it is non-obvious because pseudo-element content is not visible in the DOM tree and does not appear in `innerHTML`.
Fix: Use `toHaveText(/3 new messages/i)` with a regex that tolerates leading/trailing characters, or use `toContainText('3 new messages')` which performs a substring match; alternatively, scope the locator to a child element that does not inherit the `::before` bullet (e.g., `listitem.getByText('3 new messages', { exact: true })`).

---

**Gotcha G59: `page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` hangs indefinitely on pages that continuously poll the server (analytics heartbeats, WebSocket keep-alives, real-time data feeds) because the "networkidle" condition requires 500ms with no in-flight requests — which is never satisfied when polling intervals are shorter than 500ms.**
A team writing a session harness for a real-time dashboard found that every call to `page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` timed out after the default 30 seconds. The dashboard polled a `/api/metrics` endpoint every 200ms for live chart data. Because a new request fired every 200ms, there was never a 500ms window of network silence for `networkidle` to resolve. The team's session harnesses became unmaintainably slow and flaky. WHY: Playwright's `networkidle` state implementation uses a 500ms quiescence window — if any request completes and a new one starts within 500ms, the timer resets; this is an inherent limitation for real-time applications where continuous polling is by design, not a defect.
Fix: Replace `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` with a specific `page.waitForResponse()` call targeting the initial data load endpoint, or use `waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded')` combined with `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` for the element that signals readiness, or block the polling endpoint via `page.route()` during initial load and restore it after the page reaches a stable state.
