## Cycle 58 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 429: `locator.ariaSnapshot()` Structural Accessibility Oracle for Component-Level Exploration** [official]

Capture the ARIA accessibility tree of a specific subtree during exploratory sessions to detect hidden structural regressions in component libraries.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('aria structure oracle — data table accessibility', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/data-table');

  // Capture baseline ARIA snapshot of the table component
  const tableLocator = page.getByRole('table', { name: /customer orders/i });
  const baselineSnapshot = await tableLocator.ariaSnapshot();

  // Interact: sort by date column
  await page.getByRole('columnheader', { name: /date/i }).click();
  const afterSortSnapshot = await tableLocator.ariaSnapshot();

  // Sort must not remove rows or alter row count
  const baselineRows = (baselineSnapshot.match(/- row/g) ?? []).length;
  const afterSortRows = (afterSortSnapshot.match(/- row/g) ?? []).length;
  expect(afterSortRows, 'Row count must be stable after sort').toBe(baselineRows);

  // Sort indicator must appear on the clicked column header
  expect(afterSortSnapshot).toMatch(/columnheader.*date.*\(sorted/i);

  // Pagination controls must remain accessible throughout
  const pagination = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /pagination/i });
  const paginationSnapshot = await pagination.ariaSnapshot();
  expect(paginationSnapshot).toMatch(/button.*next/i);
});
```
Tradeoff: `ariaSnapshot()` returns a YAML-formatted string that reflects the accessibility tree as exposed by the browser's AT (Accessibility Technology) layer — the output format is not yet stable across Playwright major versions (it changed between v1.48 and v1.49 to include element references), so snapshot comparison in CI requires pinning the Playwright version or using regex matchers rather than strict string equality; using `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` on the page object is preferred over manual string comparison because Playwright's built-in matcher handles normalization, but per-locator `ariaSnapshot()` gives more surgical control for component-level exploration.

**Pattern 430: `locator.and()` Compound Locator for Ambiguous-State Element Identification** [official]

Use the `and()` locator combinator to unambiguously identify elements that have overlapping roles or names during exploratory sessions where multiple similar controls co-exist.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('compound locator — identify active tab in tabbed interface', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard/analytics');

  // Ambiguous: multiple tabs share 'tabpanel' role
  // Compound locator: role=tab AND has aria-selected=true
  const activeTab = page
    .getByRole('tab')
    .and(page.locator('[aria-selected="true"]'));

  await expect(activeTab).toBeVisible();
  const activeTabName = await activeTab.textContent();
  expect(activeTabName?.trim()).toBeTruthy();

  // Navigate to next tab
  const tabs = page.getByRole('tab');
  const tabCount = await tabs.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < tabCount; i++) {
    await tabs.nth(i).click();
    // After each click, exactly one tab should be selected
    const selectedTabs = page
      .getByRole('tab')
      .and(page.locator('[aria-selected="true"]'));
    await expect(selectedTabs).toHaveCount(1);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.and()` evaluates both locator conditions on the same element simultaneously, which correctly narrows ambiguous matches; however, it does NOT compose locators from different subtrees — both locators in the `and()` chain must match the *same* DOM node, so it cannot express "button inside a container that also has class X" (use `locator.filter({ has })` for parent-child composition instead); the `and()` operator is most useful when you need to assert on element *state* (aria attributes, CSS classes) alongside *role*, not when filtering by ancestor.

---

**Pattern 431: `page.locator(':scope > *')` Direct-Children Enumeration for Dynamic List Exploration** [official]

Enumerate direct children of a dynamic container using the `:scope` CSS pseudo-class to detect count regressions, ordering artifacts, and DOM pollution during list-rendering exploration.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('direct children oracle — virtual list rendering integrity', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products/list?view=virtual');

  const listContainer = page.locator('[data-testid="product-list"]');
  await expect(listContainer).toBeVisible();

  // Count direct rendered children (not grandchildren from item subtrees)
  const directChildren = listContainer.locator(':scope > [data-testid="product-item"]');
  const initialCount = await directChildren.count();

  // Scroll to trigger virtual rendering of next batch
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const el = document.querySelector('[data-testid="product-list"]');
    el?.scrollTo({ top: el.scrollHeight, behavior: 'instant' });
  });
  await page.waitForTimeout(300); // allow virtual renderer to flush

  const afterScrollCount = await directChildren.count();

  // Virtual list should add items, not replace them wholesale
  expect(afterScrollCount).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(initialCount);

  // No orphaned sentinel nodes should appear (data-testid must be present on all children)
  const orphans = listContainer.locator(':scope > :not([data-testid])');
  await expect(orphans).toHaveCount(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `:scope > *` is a CSS relational selector that is evaluated in the Playwright selector engine via the browser's own CSS matching — it is reliable but requires the selector string to be passed as a `locator()` argument, not as a role/text locator chain; the `:scope` keyword only works inside CSS selector strings and cannot be mixed with Playwright's ARIA locator methods (`getByRole`, `getByText`), meaning this pattern is limited to structural/DOM exploration and cannot carry semantic ARIA meaning without additional assertions.

---

**Pattern 432: `page.evaluate()` + `PerformanceObserver` Long-Task Detection During Interaction Exploration** [community]

Inject a `PerformanceObserver` before a chartered interaction to surface JavaScript long tasks (>50ms) that block the main thread — a key heuristic for detecting UI jank and input-responsiveness regressions during exploratory sessions.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('long-task oracle — form submission main-thread budget', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/payment');

  // Inject long-task observer before the charter interaction
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    (window as any).__longTasks = [] as PerformanceEntry[];
    const observer = new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
      (window as any).__longTasks.push(...list.getEntries());
    });
    observer.observe({ type: 'longtask', buffered: true });
  });

  // Execute the charter: fill and submit payment form
  await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4242 4242 4242 4242');
  await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/28');
  await page.getByLabel('CVV').fill('123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL(/\/checkout\/confirmation/);

  // Retrieve long tasks logged during the interaction
  const longTasks: PerformanceEntry[] = await page.evaluate(
    () => (window as any).__longTasks ?? []
  );

  const totalBlockingTime = longTasks.reduce((sum, t) => sum + (t.duration - 50), 0);

  // Budget: no single interaction sequence should exceed 500ms TBT
  expect(
    totalBlockingTime,
    `Total blocking time ${totalBlockingTime.toFixed(0)}ms exceeded 500ms budget`
  ).toBeLessThan(500);

  if (longTasks.length > 0) {
    console.log('[LongTask Oracle]', longTasks.map(t => `${t.name}: ${t.duration.toFixed(1)}ms`));
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `PerformanceObserver` with `type: 'longtask'` is only available in Chromium-based browsers — Firefox and WebKit do not implement the Long Tasks API (it is a W3C Editor's Draft, not a finalized standard), so this pattern produces meaningful data only in Chromium contexts and must be guarded with `test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', 'Long Tasks API requires Chromium')` in multi-browser suites; the `buffered: true` option captures tasks that fired before the observer was attached but only within the current navigation's performance timeline, so tasks that ran during page load before `page.goto()` resolved are not captured without pre-navigation injection via `addInitScript()`.

**Pattern 433: `page.route()` + `abort()` Selective Dependency-Failure Injection Charter** [official]

Abort individual third-party requests during exploratory sessions to charter the application's graceful-degradation behavior when CDN assets, analytics scripts, or feature-flag endpoints are unavailable.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('dependency-failure charter — graceful degradation without analytics', async ({ page }) => {
  const abortedUrls: string[] = [];

  // Block only third-party analytics; allow all first-party requests
  await page.route('**/*.{segment.io,mixpanel.com,hotjar.com}/**', async (route) => {
    abortedUrls.push(route.request().url());
    await route.abort('failed');
  });

  // Also block feature-flag CDN to simulate cold-start degradation
  await page.route('**/api/feature-flags', async (route) => {
    abortedUrls.push(route.request().url());
    await route.abort('failed');
  });

  await page.goto('/');

  // Core page must render despite blocked dependencies
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation')).toBeVisible();

  // No visible error states should appear to the user
  const errorBanners = page.locator('[data-testid*="error"], [role="alert"]');
  await expect(errorBanners).toHaveCount(0);

  // Critical interactions must still work
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: /products/i }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/products/);

  console.log('[Dependency Failure Charter] Blocked:', abortedUrls.length, 'requests');
  console.log(abortedUrls.map(u => `  - ${new URL(u).hostname}`).join('\n'));
});
```
Tradeoff: `route.abort()` with the `'failed'` reason causes the browser to treat the request as a network-level failure (ECONNREFUSED equivalent) — this correctly triggers `fetch()` catch handlers and `onerror` callbacks in the application code, but it does NOT simulate HTTP error responses (4xx/5xx); applications that check `response.ok` in a `try/catch` around `fetch()` will receive a thrown `TypeError: Failed to fetch` rather than a response object, which may exercise different error-handling code paths than a real CDN 503; use `route.fulfill({ status: 503 })` when the charter requires testing HTTP-level error handling rather than network-level failure.

---

**Pattern 434: `locator.filter({ visible: true })` Visible-Only Subset Exploration for Progressive-Disclosure UIs** [official]

Filter a locator set to only currently visible elements to explore progressive-disclosure patterns (accordions, tabs, lazy sections) without coupling the test to the total count of hidden elements.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('progressive-disclosure oracle — accordion visible-section charter', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/faq');

  const allSections = page.getByRole('region');
  const visibleSections = allSections.filter({ visible: true });
  const hiddenSections = allSections.filter({ visible: false });

  // Initially, some sections should be collapsed (not visible)
  const initialVisibleCount = await visibleSections.count();
  const initialHiddenCount = await hiddenSections.count();
  expect(initialHiddenCount).toBeGreaterThan(0);

  // Expand the first accordion header
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /expand|show|open/i }).first().click();

  const afterExpandVisible = await visibleSections.count();
  expect(afterExpandVisible).toBeGreaterThan(initialVisibleCount);

  // Each visible section must have accessible content
  for (let i = 0; i < afterExpandVisible; i++) {
    const section = visibleSections.nth(i);
    await expect(section).not.toBeEmpty();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.filter({ visible: true })` uses Playwright's visibility definition (non-zero bounding box, `display !== 'none'`) — it does NOT filter by `visibility: hidden` or `opacity: 0`, meaning elements that are visually invisible through those CSS properties will still be included in the "visible" filter results; for accordions using `visibility: hidden` transitions, add a secondary `.filter({ hasCSS: { visibility: 'visible' } })` step or assert `toHaveCSS('visibility', 'visible')` on suspicious elements.

**Pattern 435: `expect(locator).toHaveCSS()` Computed-Style Oracle for Design-Token Regression Exploration** [official]

Assert computed CSS property values during exploratory sessions to detect silent design-token regressions where components render in the wrong color, spacing, or typography without throwing JS errors.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('design-token oracle — primary button computed style charter', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/button-showcase');

  const primaryButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /primary action/i }).first();
  await expect(primaryButton).toBeVisible();

  // Assert computed background color matches design token (deep blue)
  await expect(primaryButton).toHaveCSS('background-color', 'rgb(37, 99, 235)');

  // Assert border-radius matches rounded button specification
  await expect(primaryButton).toHaveCSS('border-radius', '8px');

  // Assert font-weight is semibold
  await expect(primaryButton).toHaveCSS('font-weight', '600');

  // Hover state: simulate and assert
  await primaryButton.hover();
  // Give CSS transition time to complete
  await page.waitForTimeout(200);
  const hoverBg = await primaryButton.evaluate((el) =>
    window.getComputedStyle(el).backgroundColor
  );
  // Hover background must differ from resting state (darkened)
  expect(hoverBg).not.toBe('rgb(37, 99, 235)');

  // Focus state: keyboard focus
  await primaryButton.focus();
  await expect(primaryButton).toHaveCSS('outline-style', /(solid|auto)/);
});
```
Tradeoff: `toHaveCSS()` compares against computed (resolved) CSS values, not authored values — `rgb()` triplets rather than hex codes or CSS variables, `px` values rather than `rem` or `em`, which means the expected value in the assertion must be in the browser-resolved format and will differ between browsers (Chromium resolves `border-radius: 0.5rem` to `8px` at 16px base font size, but Safari may report slightly different sub-pixel values); maintain a separate `design-tokens.test.ts` file with expected computed values rather than inlining magic RGB strings in exploratory session code, and use regex matchers for values susceptible to sub-pixel rounding.

---

**Pattern 436: `page.on('pageerror')` Runtime Exception Oracle for Exploration Session Health Monitoring** [official]

Register a `pageerror` listener at session start to automatically capture unhandled JavaScript exceptions thrown anywhere in the application during the exploration charter, surfacing hidden error states that do not manifest as visible UI failures.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('runtime exception oracle — dashboard exploration health monitor', async ({ page }) => {
  const pageErrors: Error[] = [];

  // Register before navigation to capture boot-time errors
  page.on('pageerror', (error) => {
    pageErrors.push(error);
  });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Charter: explore all major dashboard sections
  const navLinks = page.getByRole('navigation').getByRole('link');
  const linkCount = await navLinks.count();

  for (let i = 0; i < Math.min(linkCount, 8); i++) {
    const link = navLinks.nth(i);
    const href = await link.getAttribute('href');
    if (!href || href.startsWith('#') || href.startsWith('http')) continue;

    await link.click();
    await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

    // Brief exploration at each route
    const interactables = page.getByRole('button').filter({ visible: true });
    const count = await interactables.count();
    if (count > 0) {
      await interactables.first().hover(); // hover, not click, to avoid navigation
    }
  }

  // Session-end oracle: no unhandled exceptions during any visited route
  expect(
    pageErrors,
    `Unhandled exceptions:\n${pageErrors.map(e => `  ${e.message}`).join('\n')}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.on('pageerror')` captures uncaught exceptions that bubble to `window.onerror` — it does NOT capture errors inside `Promise` rejections that are caught by a `.catch()` handler or errors thrown inside `async` functions that are silently swallowed; to cover promise rejections, also register `page.on('console')` filtering for `console.error` messages and listen for the `unhandledrejection` event via `addInitScript()` injection; note that some applications deliberately suppress `pageerror` events by overriding `window.onerror = () => true` to prevent error propagation — verify the override does not apply in the test environment.

---

**Pattern 437: `locator.allTextContents()` Bulk-Text Extraction Oracle for List-Content Completeness Exploration** [official]

Extract all text content from a list of elements in one call to validate completeness, ordering, and uniqueness invariants during content-rendering exploration.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('bulk text oracle — search results completeness and dedup charter', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search?q=laptop&limit=20');

  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="result-title"]');

  const resultTitles = page.locator('[data-testid="result-title"]');
  const titles = await resultTitles.allTextContents();

  // All results must have non-empty titles
  const emptyTitles = titles.filter(t => !t.trim());
  expect(emptyTitles, 'Empty result titles found').toHaveLength(0);

  // No duplicate titles in a single search results page
  const uniqueTitles = new Set(titles.map(t => t.trim().toLowerCase()));
  expect(
    uniqueTitles.size,
    `Duplicate titles detected: ${titles.length - uniqueTitles.size} duplicates`
  ).toBe(titles.length);

  // All titles must contain at least 3 characters (no truncation artifacts)
  const tooShortTitles = titles.filter(t => t.trim().length < 3);
  expect(tooShortTitles, 'Suspiciously short titles found').toHaveLength(0);

  console.log(`[Text Oracle] Validated ${titles.length} result titles`);
});
```
Tradeoff: `allTextContents()` returns an array of strings in DOM order but does not resolve in strict mode — if no elements match the locator, it returns an empty array rather than throwing, meaning a misconfigured selector silently produces a vacuously passing test (all assertions against an empty array trivially pass); always add `expect(titles.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` as the first assertion after `allTextContents()` to catch selector misconfiguration.

**Pattern 438: `page.waitForFunction()` Custom Convergence Predicate for Framework-Specific State Exploration** [official]

Poll a JavaScript predicate in the browser context until application-framework state converges, enabling exploration of Vuex/Redux/Zustand store state without coupling tests to implementation-specific selectors.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('state convergence oracle — Redux store cart total exploration', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/shop/catalog');

  // Add items to cart
  const addButtons = page.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i });
  await addButtons.first().click();
  await addButtons.nth(1).click();

  // Wait for Redux store to reflect 2 items (framework-agnostic convergence)
  await page.waitForFunction(() => {
    // Access Redux store via DevTools bridge or window export
    const store = (window as any).__REDUX_STORE__;
    if (!store) return false;
    const state = store.getState();
    return state.cart?.items?.length >= 2;
  }, { timeout: 5000 });

  // Verify UI reflects store state
  const cartBadge = page.locator('[data-testid="cart-count"]');
  await expect(cartBadge).toHaveText('2');

  // Explore: remove one item and assert store + UI converge
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /remove from cart/i }).first().click();

  await page.waitForFunction(() => {
    const store = (window as any).__REDUX_STORE__;
    return store?.getState()?.cart?.items?.length === 1;
  }, { timeout: 3000 });

  await expect(cartBadge).toHaveText('1');
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.waitForFunction()` runs the predicate in the browser context at a polling interval (default 100ms), making it framework-agnostic and independent of visual selectors — but it requires the application to expose its internal store on `window` (either via a Redux DevTools extension bridge or a deliberate `window.__REDUX_STORE__ = store` line in non-production builds); this creates a coupling to the application's debug/test surface that must be maintained; prefer this pattern in exploratory sessions over arbitrary `waitForTimeout()` calls, but do not promote `waitForFunction()` with `window.__` access to the production test suite without establishing a formal test-surface API.

---

**Pattern 439: `test.use({ viewport })` Per-Test Viewport Override for Responsive-Layout Breakpoint Exploration** [official]

Override the viewport per test using `test.use()` to systematically explore responsive layout breakpoints without spawning separate browser instances or relying on device emulation presets.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const BREAKPOINTS = [
  { name: 'mobile-xs',  width: 320,  height: 568  },
  { name: 'mobile',     width: 390,  height: 844  },
  { name: 'tablet',     width: 768,  height: 1024 },
  { name: 'desktop-sm', width: 1280, height: 800  },
  { name: 'desktop-lg', width: 1920, height: 1080 },
];

for (const bp of BREAKPOINTS) {
  test(`responsive layout charter — navigation at ${bp.name} (${bp.width}px)`, async ({ page }) => {
    test.use({ viewport: { width: bp.width, height: bp.height } });

    await page.goto('/');

    const nav = page.getByRole('navigation');
    await expect(nav).toBeVisible();

    if (bp.width < 768) {
      // Mobile: hamburger menu must be present and desktop nav hidden
      const hamburger = page.getByRole('button', { name: /menu|hamburger|open nav/i });
      await expect(hamburger).toBeVisible();

      const desktopLinks = page.locator('[data-testid="desktop-nav-links"]');
      await expect(desktopLinks).toBeHidden();

      // Open mobile nav
      await hamburger.click();
      await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /navigation/i })
        .or(page.locator('[data-testid="mobile-nav"]'))
      ).toBeVisible();
    } else {
      // Desktop/tablet: inline nav links must be visible
      const navLinks = nav.getByRole('link');
      await expect(navLinks.first()).toBeVisible();
    }
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: `test.use({ viewport })` inside a `test()` body takes effect for that specific test's browser context — however, calling `test.use()` inside a test function body (rather than in a `test.describe()` block or at the file's top level) is a pattern that Playwright supports but warns against in some configurations because `test.use()` is designed as a describe-level hook; the recommended pattern is to wrap each viewport test in a `test.describe()` with a `test.use()` inside the describe block, or to use `page.setViewportSize()` directly within the test body for mid-test viewport changes; for comprehensive breakpoint matrix testing, use Playwright's `projects` configuration with named viewport projects instead.

---

**Pattern 440: `page.frameLocator()` + `locator.contentFrame()` Dual-Path iframe Exploration Strategy** [official]

Use both `page.frameLocator()` and the newer `locator.contentFrame()` method to explore iframe-embedded components, choosing the approach based on whether the frame is identified by selector or by traversing to a known locator.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('iframe exploration — payment widget dual-path charter', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/step-2');

  // Path A: frameLocator() — when you know the iframe's selector
  const paymentFrameBySelector = page.frameLocator('[data-testid="payment-iframe"]');

  await expect(
    paymentFrameBySelector.getByLabel('Card number')
  ).toBeVisible();

  // Path B: contentFrame() — when you've already located the iframe element
  const iframeElement = page.locator('[data-testid="payment-iframe"]');
  const paymentFrameByLocator = iframeElement.contentFrame();

  if (paymentFrameByLocator) {
    const cardInput = paymentFrameByLocator.getByLabel('Card number');
    await expect(cardInput).toBeVisible();

    // Both paths must point to the same element
    const frameAHandle = await paymentFrameBySelector.getByLabel('Card number').elementHandle();
    const frameBHandle = await paymentFrameByLocator.getByLabel('Card number').elementHandle();
    expect(await page.evaluate(
      ([a, b]) => a?.isSameNode(b ?? null),
      [frameAHandle, frameBHandle]
    )).toBe(true);
  }

  // Explore form interaction within frame
  await paymentFrameBySelector.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4111 1111 1111 1111');
  await paymentFrameBySelector.getByLabel('Expiry date').fill('12/28');
  await paymentFrameBySelector.getByLabel('Security code').fill('737');

  // Outer page submit must trigger iframe validation
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /confirm payment/i }).click();
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/checkout\/confirmation|step-3/);
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.contentFrame()` returns `null` synchronously if the locator does not resolve to an `<iframe>` or `<frame>` element at call time — unlike `frameLocator()` which is lazily evaluated and defers resolution until an action is performed; this means `contentFrame()` must be called after the iframe is visible in the DOM (use `await expect(iframeElement).toBeVisible()` first), whereas `frameLocator()` tolerates late-appearing iframes gracefully; use `contentFrame()` when you need to inspect frame metadata (src, name) from the element handle before interacting with the frame's content, and use `frameLocator()` for straightforward interaction-oriented charters.

---

**Pattern 441: `page.keyboard.type()` vs `locator.fill()` Distinguishing Input Mechanism Exploration** [official]

Explicitly charter the difference between `keyboard.type()` (simulates keystroke-by-keystroke input) and `locator.fill()` (direct value assignment) to expose input-handler bugs that only surface during real typing — e.g., autocomplete triggering, input masking, and character throttling.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('input mechanism oracle — typeahead vs fill behavior charter', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');

  const searchInput = page.getByRole('searchbox');

  // Charter A: fill() — bypasses keystroke events, sets value atomically
  await searchInput.fill('laptop');
  const fillValue = await searchInput.inputValue();
  expect(fillValue).toBe('laptop');

  // Does fill() trigger the autocomplete dropdown?
  const suggestionsFill = page.getByRole('listbox');
  const fillTriggersSuggestions = await suggestionsFill.isVisible();
  console.log('[Input Oracle] fill() triggers autocomplete:', fillTriggersSuggestions);

  // Clear for next charter
  await searchInput.clear();

  // Charter B: keyboard.type() — simulates real keystroke events
  await searchInput.click(); // ensure focus
  await page.keyboard.type('laptop', { delay: 80 });
  const typeValue = await searchInput.inputValue();
  expect(typeValue).toBe('laptop');

  // Does keyboard.type() trigger the autocomplete dropdown?
  const suggestionsType = page.getByRole('listbox');
  await expect(suggestionsType).toBeVisible();

  // Autocomplete must have at least one suggestion
  const suggestions = suggestionsType.getByRole('option');
  await expect(suggestions).not.toHaveCount(0);

  // Select first suggestion with keyboard
  await page.keyboard.press('ArrowDown');
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');
  const selectedValue = await searchInput.inputValue();
  expect(selectedValue.length).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  expect(selectedValue).not.toBe('laptop'); // should be replaced by suggestion
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.keyboard.type()` dispatches individual `keydown`, `keypress`, `keyup`, and `input` events for each character in the string — this correctly triggers debounced `oninput` handlers and autocomplete libraries that listen for individual keystrokes, but it is significantly slower than `locator.fill()` (which fires a single synthetic `input` event) and may cause flakiness under high CPU load if the application's debounce timer fires before all characters are delivered; the `delay` option in `keyboard.type()` adds artificial inter-keystroke delay to simulate realistic typing speed but increases test duration proportionally — use `delay: 0` in CI and `delay: 80` locally for readable slow-motion debugging.

---

**Pattern 442: `browserContext.addCookies()` Pre-Seeded Cookie State for Charter Session Bootstrapping** [official]

Seed authentication and feature-flag cookies before navigation using `context.addCookies()` to bootstrap exploratory sessions into specific application states without executing the full login flow in every charter.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('cookie bootstrap oracle — premium feature access charter', async ({ context, page }) => {
  const baseURL = 'http://localhost:3000';

  // Seed session + feature-flag cookies before navigation
  await context.addCookies([
    {
      name: 'session_token',
      value: 'test-premium-user-token-abc123',
      domain: 'localhost',
      path: '/',
      httpOnly: true,
      secure: false,
      sameSite: 'Lax',
    },
    {
      name: 'feature_flags',
      value: JSON.stringify({ premiumDashboard: true, betaExport: true }),
      domain: 'localhost',
      path: '/',
      httpOnly: false,
      secure: false,
      sameSite: 'Strict',
    },
  ]);

  await page.goto(baseURL + '/dashboard');

  // Premium features should be accessible with seeded cookies
  const premiumBadge = page.getByTestId('premium-badge');
  await expect(premiumBadge).toBeVisible();

  const exportButton = page.getByRole('button', { name: /export data/i });
  await expect(exportButton).toBeVisible();

  // Explore: verify feature-flag gating respects the cookie value
  const betaIndicator = page.getByTestId('beta-feature-indicator');
  await expect(betaIndicator).toBeVisible();

  // Verify cookies are still present after navigation
  const cookies = await context.cookies();
  const sessionCookie = cookies.find(c => c.name === 'session_token');
  expect(sessionCookie).toBeDefined();
});
```
Tradeoff: `context.addCookies()` sets cookies in the Playwright browser context's cookie jar before any navigation — the cookies are available from the first request, including the initial `GET` to the page, making this the most efficient way to bootstrap authenticated sessions; however, cookies set this way bypass the server's `Set-Cookie` flow, meaning they do not carry server-generated signatures or HMAC tokens that a real authentication flow would produce; if the application validates cookie signatures (e.g., JWT signatures, server-side session hash verification), the seeded cookie values must be real valid tokens for the test environment, not arbitrary strings — work with the backend team to maintain a set of long-lived test tokens that are safe to commit to the test fixtures.

---

**Pattern 443: `page.screenshot({ fullPage: true })` + Evidence Archive for Multi-Step Charter Documentation** [community]

Capture full-page screenshots at each charter step and archive them with step context metadata to create an audit-quality evidence trail for defects discovered during exploratory sessions.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as path from 'path';

test('evidence archive charter — user onboarding flow exploration', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  const evidenceDir = testInfo.outputDir;
  let stepIdx = 0;

  async function captureEvidence(stepName: string) {
    const filename = `step-${String(++stepIdx).padStart(2, '0')}-${stepName.replace(/\s+/g, '-')}.png`;
    const screenshotPath = path.join(evidenceDir, filename);
    await page.screenshot({ path: screenshotPath, fullPage: true });
    testInfo.attach(stepName, { path: screenshotPath, contentType: 'image/png' });
    return screenshotPath;
  }

  await page.goto('/onboarding/start');
  await captureEvidence('initial-state');

  // Step 1: enter email
  await page.getByLabel('Email address').fill('tester@example.com');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue/i }).click();
  await captureEvidence('after-email-entry');

  // Step 2: choose plan
  await page.getByRole('radio', { name: /professional/i }).check();
  await captureEvidence('plan-selected');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /start trial/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL(/onboarding\/profile/);
  await captureEvidence('profile-step');

  // Assertions on final state
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /tell us about yourself/i })).toBeVisible();
  expect(stepIdx).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.screenshot({ fullPage: true })` triggers a full-page scroll-capture in Playwright by stitching multiple viewport-height screenshots together — on pages with `position: fixed` elements (sticky headers, floating action buttons), these fixed elements will appear repeated in every stitched section of the full-page screenshot, creating visually confusing artifacts; use `{ clip: { x: 0, y: 0, width: viewport.width, height: totalPageHeight } }` or `{ fullPage: false }` combined with explicit scroll position for a cleaner evidence capture, or suppress fixed elements during capture via the `stylePath` option by injecting `* { position: static !important }` temporarily.

---

### Community Gotchas

**G60: `locator.fill()` on a `contenteditable` element does NOT dispatch `input` or `change` events in the same way as a standard `<input>` — rich-text editors built on `contenteditable` (Slate.js, Quill, TipTap) rely on `beforeinput` events and `MutationObserver` callbacks that `fill()` does not trigger, causing the editor's internal document model to desync from the DOM.**
Teams exploring rich-text editor components found that `page.getByRole('textbox').fill('Hello bold text')` appeared to set the text visually in the contenteditable div, but subsequent toolbar actions (bold, italic) had no effect because the editor's internal model (Slate.js document tree, Quill Delta) was not updated — only the raw DOM changed. Submitting the form sent an empty or stale value because the editor read its value from the internal model, not the DOM `textContent`. WHY: `locator.fill()` uses `HTMLInputElement.value =` assignment semantics for `<input>` elements and `element.textContent =` assignment for `contenteditable` — the latter bypasses the `beforeinput` event that all major rich-text frameworks use as their primary input hook; `MutationObserver` callbacks may fire, but only after the entire value is set atomically, which does not match the character-by-character input sequence the editor expects for cursor tracking and document history management.
Fix: Use `locator.click()` followed by `page.keyboard.type(text, { delay: 30 })` for contenteditable rich-text editors; if performance is critical in CI, use `locator.evaluate((el, val) => { el.focus(); document.execCommand('insertText', false, val); })` which dispatches the `input` event that most editors handle — note that `execCommand('insertText')` is deprecated but remains the most compatible programmatic insertion method.

---

**G61: `page.getByRole('dialog')` matches elements with `role="dialog"` but NOT elements with `role="alertdialog"` — these are distinct ARIA roles, and a modal that uses `alertdialog` (the correct role for destructive confirmation dialogs) will not be found by `getByRole('dialog')`.**
A team exploring modal behavior for a delete-confirmation flow found that `expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible()` failed after clicking "Delete account" — the modal was present in the DOM and visible, but used `role="alertdialog"` as per WCAG's requirement that dialogs interrupting workflow with a required response should use `alertdialog`. The assertion timed out with "locator resolved to 0 elements" even though the DevTools clearly showed the modal. WHY: ARIA distinguishes `dialog` (a modal that can be dismissed without making a choice) from `alertdialog` (a modal that requires a user decision — the user MUST respond); Playwright's `getByRole('dialog')` performs a strict role match against the element's resolved ARIA role, which does not include `alertdialog` as a subtype; this is correct per the ARIA specification, but it is non-obvious to testers who use "dialog" generically.
Fix: Use `page.getByRole('alertdialog')` for confirmation modals, or use `page.locator('[role="dialog"], [role="alertdialog"]')` when exploring pages where both types may appear, or use `page.getByText('Confirm delete').locator('..')` to locate the modal by its content when the role is uncertain.

---

**G62: `page.waitForSelector()` with default options resolves as soon as the element is added to the DOM — even if it is immediately removed in the same microtask queue flush by a React state update, causing the `waitForSelector` promise to resolve and the subsequent action to find the element already gone.**
Teams exploring React applications with rapid conditional rendering (e.g., components that mount and unmount within a single `setState` batch during an animation transition) found that `await page.waitForSelector('.toast-notification')` resolved, but the immediately following `await page.locator('.toast-notification').textContent()` threw "element not found" because the toast had already unmounted. The issue was a React component that mounted a toast, immediately started a fade-out animation, and unmounted after the CSS transition in a single event loop tick. WHY: Playwright's `waitForSelector` default state is `'attached'` (present in DOM), not `'visible'` — if the React reconciler mounts and unmounts a component within the same task, `waitForSelector` with `'attached'` can resolve during the brief attachment window before the subsequent unmount has already occurred.
Fix: Use `page.waitForSelector('.toast-notification', { state: 'visible' })` or the locator equivalent `await expect(locator).toBeVisible()` which waits for the element to reach a stable visible state; if the component mounts-and-immediately-unmounts is the actual bug, capture it as a defect using `page.on('pageerror')` and `console.error` listener rather than trying to assert on the transient state.

---

**G63: `context.storageState()` does NOT capture `IndexedDB` data — only `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, and cookies are serialized into the storage state file; applications that cache user preferences, offline data, or session artifacts in IndexedDB will lose that state when a new browser context is created from the saved `storageState`.**
A team setting up reusable authentication fixtures using `context.storageState()` found that while the session cookie was correctly preserved, the application's "remember me" feature (which stored the user's theme preference and sidebar state in IndexedDB) was lost on every test run that loaded from the storage state file. The application showed the default theme instead of the user's saved preference on every test that used the saved auth state. WHY: Playwright's `storageState()` API is explicitly scoped to `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, and HTTP cookies because these are the primary authentication-relevant stores; IndexedDB is a more complex structured storage mechanism that is not included because it can contain large binary blobs, versioned object stores, and schema migrations that make serialization impractical for a portable state file.
Fix: For applications that use IndexedDB for preference storage, supplement `storageState()` with a `page.evaluate()` call that reads the IndexedDB values and stores them in `localStorage` (if they are small), or use `page.addInitScript()` to re-seed the IndexedDB at the start of each test that depends on it, injecting the values from a fixtures JSON file.

---

**G64: `locator.selectOption()` on a `<select>` element fires a `change` event but does NOT fire a `click` event — applications that attach `click` listeners to `<select>` elements to open a custom styled dropdown (rather than relying on the native browser `<select>` popup) will not activate the custom dropdown, and `selectOption()` will appear to have no effect on the visual UI.**
A team exploring a filter panel built with a CSS-styled custom select (a `<select>` element with `appearance: none` and a positioned `<div>` overlay that opens on `click`) found that `page.getByRole('combobox', { name: 'Category' }).selectOption('Electronics')` succeeded without error but the visual dropdown never opened, the custom option list never appeared, and the filtered results never changed. The native `<select>` value was set correctly (the DOM showed the correct `value` attribute), but the application only re-fetched results when the custom dropdown's overlay received a `click` event on an option element. WHY: `selectOption()` uses `HTMLSelectElement.value =` assignment combined with dispatching a `change` event — it does not simulate a user clicking on the `<select>` element, clicking on an option, or triggering any `click`, `mousedown`, or `mouseup` events on the select or its containing overlay.
Fix: For custom-styled selects, use `page.locator('[data-testid="category-select-trigger"]').click()` to open the custom dropdown overlay, then `page.getByRole('option', { name: 'Electronics' }).click()` to select the option; file a defect if the custom select is not keyboard-accessible (it must support `ArrowDown`/`Enter` for WCAG 2.1 Level AA compliance).

## Cycle 59 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 443** — Soft-Assertion Batch Reporter for Multi-Checkpoint Sessions

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('soft-assertion batch session — checkout flow', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Soft assertions: execution continues even on failure
  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order summary/i })).toBeVisible();
  await expect.soft(page.getByLabel('Promo code')).toBeEditable();

  await page.getByLabel('Promo code').fill('SAVE10');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /apply/i }).click();

  await expect.soft(page.getByText(/discount applied/i)).toBeVisible();
  await expect.soft(page.locator('[data-testid="discount-line"]')).toContainText('-$');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /place order/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL(/order\/confirmation/);

  await expect.soft(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /thank you/i })).toBeVisible();
  await expect.soft(page.getByTestId('order-number')).not.toBeEmpty();

  // Harvest all soft failures at the end of the session
  const failures = testInfo.errors;
  if (failures.length > 0) {
    testInfo.annotations.push({
      type: 'soft-failure-count',
      description: `${failures.length} soft assertion(s) failed during session`,
    });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `expect.soft()` allows a session to continue past failing assertions and collect a full picture of defects in a single run — but it masks severity: a critical heading being absent carries the same weight as a cosmetic label mismatch until you re-read the failure list; annotate or rank failures by severity manually in the debrief so the session sheet accurately reflects risk.

---

**Pattern 444** — `page.route()` + JSON Mutation for API Response Oracle

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('mutated API response oracle — empty cart edge case', async ({ page }) => {
  // Intercept cart API and return an empty items array
  await page.route('**/api/cart', async (route) => {
    const response = await route.fetch();
    const body = await response.json();
    const mutated = { ...body, items: [], total: 0 };
    await route.fulfill({ json: mutated });
  });

  await page.goto('/cart');

  // Oracle: UI must gracefully handle empty cart
  await expect(page.getByText(/your cart is empty/i)).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /checkout/i })).toBeDisabled();
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="cart-total"]')).toContainText('$0');

  // Explore: does the empty state suggest next actions?
  const ctaVisible = await page.getByRole('link', { name: /continue shopping/i }).isVisible();
  expect(ctaVisible).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: Mutating API responses via `page.route()` lets you explore edge states (empty results, error payloads, partial data) that are hard to reproduce with real data — but the mutation runs client-side only; if your application performs server-side rendering or edge-caches API responses, the mutated route applies only to fetch calls made in the browser context and will not affect the initial SSR HTML payload, potentially leaving the page in a split state.

---

**Pattern 445** — `test.step()` Timeout + Structured Charter Segment Labelling

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter-segmented session — settings page', async ({ page }) => {
  await test.step('Segment 1: Navigation & accessibility surface scan', async () => {
    await page.goto('/settings');
    await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
    // Keyboard-nav check
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
    const focused = page.locator(':focus');
    await expect(focused).toBeVisible();
  }, { timeout: 15_000 });

  await test.step('Segment 2: Form field oracle — labels and constraints', async () => {
    const inputs = page.locator('input, select, textarea');
    const count = await inputs.count();
    for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) {
      const input = inputs.nth(i);
      const ariaLabel = await input.getAttribute('aria-label');
      const id = await input.getAttribute('id');
      const labelFor = id ? await page.locator(`label[for="${id}"]`).count() : 0;
      expect(ariaLabel !== null || labelFor > 0,
        `Input at index ${i} has no accessible label`).toBeTruthy();
    }
  }, { timeout: 20_000 });

  await test.step('Segment 3: Save / discard state oracle', async () => {
    await page.getByLabel(/display name/i).fill('Renamed User');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /cancel/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByLabel(/display name/i)).not.toHaveValue('Renamed User');
  }, { timeout: 10_000 });
});
```
Tradeoff: Per-step timeouts via `test.step({ timeout })` (Playwright v1.50+) prevent a single slow segment from consuming the entire test budget, making session harnesses more predictable — however, if a step timeout triggers mid-animation or mid-navigation, the subsequent step inherits a partially-settled page state; always await stable UI signals (e.g., `waitForLoadState('networkidle')`) at the start of each step rather than relying on the previous step's cleanup.

---

**Pattern 446** — `expect(locator).toMatchAriaSnapshot()` Structural Regression Oracle

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('aria snapshot structural oracle — navigation menu', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/');

  const nav = page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /main/i });

  // First run: generate snapshot (use --update-snapshots to regenerate)
  await expect(nav).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - navigation "Main":
      - link "Home"
      - link "Products"
      - link "About"
      - link "Contact"
  `);

  // Simulate post-login state: admin link should appear
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    window.__testUser = { role: 'admin' };
    window.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('authchange'));
  });
  await page.waitForTimeout(200); // allow React re-render

  // Oracle: admin link must be present only for admin role
  await expect(page.getByRole('navigation', { name: /main/i }))
    .toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
      - navigation "Main":
        - link "Home"
        - link "Products"
        - link "Admin"
        - link "About"
        - link "Contact"
    `);
});
```
Tradeoff: `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` (Playwright v1.49+) validates the semantic ARIA tree — not pixel layout — making it robust to CSS refactors and theme changes; the tradeoff is that it is brittle to legitimate copy changes (renaming "Products" to "Catalog") which will cause snapshot failures that require intentional `--update-snapshots` runs; treat snapshot failures as a review gate, not a blocking hard failure, in exploratory CI pipelines.

---

**Pattern 447** — `page.requestGC()` + WeakRef Memory-Leak Exploration

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('memory-leak oracle — component mount/unmount cycle', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Seed a WeakRef to a DOM node that should be GC'd after unmount
  await page.evaluate(() => {
    const modal = document.querySelector('[data-testid="welcome-modal"]');
    if (modal) {
      (window as any).__leakRef = new WeakRef(modal);
    }
  });

  // Dismiss the modal (triggering React unmount)
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /close/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByTestId('welcome-modal')).not.toBeAttached();

  // Force GC via Playwright CDP (Chromium only, v1.48+)
  await page.requestGC();

  // Oracle: WeakRef should be deref'd to undefined if GC'd correctly
  const isLeaking = await page.evaluate(() => {
    return (window as any).__leakRef?.deref() !== undefined;
  });

  expect(isLeaking, 'Modal DOM node was NOT garbage-collected — potential memory leak').toBe(false);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.requestGC()` (Playwright v1.48+, Chromium only) provides a deterministic signal for detecting DOM-node and closure leaks that would otherwise only manifest as gradual heap growth in production — the tradeoff is Chromium exclusivity; Firefox and WebKit lack the CDP `HeapProfiler.collectGarbage` endpoint, so you cannot include this pattern in cross-browser session harnesses without a browser guard (`test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium')`).

---

**Pattern 448** — `page.clock()` Time-Sensitive Feature Exploration

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('clock oracle — session expiry warning and auto-logout', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-05-14T10:00:00Z') });
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  // Advance time to 25 minutes before session expiry (assume 30-min session)
  await page.clock.fastForward('25m');

  // Oracle: warning banner should appear at the 25-minute mark
  await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /session expiring/i })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByText(/5 minutes/i)).toBeVisible();

  // Advance to just past expiry
  await page.clock.fastForward('6m');

  // Oracle: user should be redirected to login
  await page.waitForURL(/\/login/);
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /sign in/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Oracle: redirect should preserve the original URL as a return_to param
  const url = new URL(page.url());
  expect(url.searchParams.get('return_to')).toContain('/dashboard');
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.clock()` (Playwright v1.45+) makes time-dependent behaviour deterministic in tests — what would require `setTimeout` delays of 30 minutes in production can be verified in milliseconds — but it only controls the JavaScript `Date` and timer APIs within the browser context; server-side session expiry is enforced by the backend clock, so if your session logic is purely server-enforced, `page.clock()` only validates the client's UI response after receiving a 401 response, not the expiry trigger itself.

**Pattern 449** — `page.routeWebSocket()` Real-Time Feed Exploration Oracle

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('WebSocket route oracle — live price feed update handling', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.routeWebSocket('wss://api.example.com/prices', (ws) => {
    ws.onMessage((msg) => {
      // Echo back a mutated price to simulate a dramatic drop
      const parsed = JSON.parse(msg.toString());
      ws.send(JSON.stringify({ ...parsed, price: 0.01, change: -99.9 }));
    });

    // After 500ms, inject an unsolicited server-push with an extreme value
    setTimeout(() => {
      ws.send(JSON.stringify({ symbol: 'BTCUSD', price: 9999999, change: +1000000 }));
    }, 500);
  });

  await page.goto('/trading/btcusd');

  // Oracle: app must handle extreme price without crashing
  await expect(page.getByTestId('price-display')).toBeVisible();
  const errors: string[] = [];
  page.on('pageerror', (err) => errors.push(err.message));
  await page.waitForTimeout(1000);

  expect(errors, 'Page errors on extreme WebSocket value').toHaveLength(0);
  // Oracle: price should render a readable number (not NaN, Infinity, or blank)
  const priceText = await page.getByTestId('price-display').textContent();
  expect(priceText).toMatch(/\d/);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.routeWebSocket()` (Playwright v1.48+) enables session-level injection of synthetic real-time events without a real WebSocket server — ideal for exploring edge-case payloads (extreme values, malformed JSON, rapid bursts) — but the route only intercepts WebSocket connections initiated after `page.routeWebSocket()` is registered; connections opened during page load before the route is established will not be intercepted, so route registration must precede `page.goto()`.

**Pattern 450** — `browserContext.storageState({ indexedDB: true })` Auth-State Exploration

```typescript
import { test, expect, type BrowserContext } from '@playwright/test';

async function seedIndexedDB(context: BrowserContext, dbName: string, storeName: string, data: Record<string, unknown>) {
  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.evaluate(({ dbName, storeName, data }) => {
    return new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      const req = indexedDB.open(dbName, 1);
      req.onupgradeneeded = (e) => {
        (e.target as IDBOpenDBRequest).result.createObjectStore(storeName);
      };
      req.onsuccess = (e) => {
        const db = (e.target as IDBOpenDBRequest).result;
        const tx = db.transaction(storeName, 'readwrite');
        Object.entries(data).forEach(([k, v]) => tx.objectStore(storeName).put(v, k));
        tx.oncomplete = () => resolve();
        tx.onerror = () => reject(tx.error);
      };
    });
  }, { dbName, storeName, data });
  await page.close();
}

test('IndexedDB storage-state oracle — theme preference persistence', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext();
  await seedIndexedDB(context, 'appDB', 'preferences', { theme: 'dark', language: 'fr' });

  // Save state WITH indexedDB (Playwright v1.51+)
  const state = await context.storageState({ indexedDB: true });
  await context.close();

  // Restore state in a fresh context
  const restored = await browser.newContext({ storageState: state });
  const page = await restored.newPage();
  await page.goto('/');

  // Oracle: app should restore dark theme from IndexedDB
  await expect(page.locator('html')).toHaveAttribute('data-theme', 'dark');
  await restored.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: `storageState({ indexedDB: true })` (Playwright v1.51+) captures IndexedDB object stores alongside cookies and localStorage, enabling full-fidelity session restoration for apps that store preferences or offline data in IndexedDB — however, the serialization format is JSON-based, so IndexedDB stores containing non-JSON-serializable values (ArrayBuffer, Blob, circular references) will produce incomplete or corrupted state snapshots; audit your app's IndexedDB schema before relying on this pattern.

**Pattern 451** — `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` Form-Error Oracle

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('accessible error message oracle — checkout form validation', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout/payment');

  // Submit with all fields blank
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();

  // Oracle: card number field must have an accessible error message
  const cardField = page.getByLabel(/card number/i);
  await expect(cardField).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/required|enter.*card/i);

  // Oracle: expiry field must surface a specific constraint message
  const expiryField = page.getByLabel(/expiry date/i);
  await expect(expiryField).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/required|mm\/yy/i);

  // Fix card number and re-submit with invalid format
  await cardField.fill('1234');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();

  // Oracle: format error must be specific enough to guide the user
  await expect(cardField).toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage(/16.digit|invalid.*card/i);

  // Oracle: error must NOT be the generic "An error occurred"
  const errorText = await cardField.evaluate((el) =>
    el.getAttribute('aria-errormessage')
      ? document.getElementById(el.getAttribute('aria-errormessage')!)?.textContent
      : el.getAttribute('aria-describedby')
          ? document.getElementById(el.getAttribute('aria-describedby')!)?.textContent
          : null
  );
  expect(errorText).not.toMatch(/an error occurred/i);
});
```
Tradeoff: `toHaveAccessibleErrorMessage()` (Playwright v1.50+) validates `aria-errormessage` and `aria-describedby` linkage — ensuring screen reader users receive the same error context as sighted users — but it only checks the programmatic relationship; it does not verify that the error text is rendered visibly on screen, so pair it with `expect(page.getByText(/16.digit/i)).toBeVisible()` to confirm both accessibility and visual correctness simultaneously.

**Pattern 452** — `locator.filter({ visible: true })` Dense-UI State Disambiguation

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('visible-filter oracle — multi-step wizard hidden panel exploration', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/wizard/onboarding');

  // The wizard renders all steps in the DOM but hides inactive steps via CSS
  const allStepPanels = page.getByRole('tabpanel');
  const visiblePanels = allStepPanels.filter({ visible: true });

  // Oracle: exactly one panel should be visible at any wizard step
  await expect(visiblePanels).toHaveCount(1);

  // Explore each step by advancing the wizard
  const stepLabels: string[] = [];
  for (let step = 0; step < 5; step++) {
    const active = visiblePanels.first();
    const heading = await active.getByRole('heading').first().textContent();
    stepLabels.push(heading ?? `step-${step}`);

    // Oracle: each visible panel must contain a primary action button
    await expect(active.getByRole('button').filter({ visible: true }).first()).toBeVisible();

    const nextBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /next|continue|finish/i })
      .filter({ visible: true });
    if (await nextBtn.count() > 0) {
      await nextBtn.click();
      await page.waitForTimeout(150); // allow CSS transition
    } else break;
  }

  // Oracle: no duplicate step labels (navigation loop detection)
  const uniqueLabels = new Set(stepLabels);
  expect(uniqueLabels.size).toBe(stepLabels.length);
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.filter({ visible: true })` (Playwright v1.51+) precisely targets the subset of matching elements that are currently rendered and interactable, solving the "0 of N elements are visible" disambiguation problem in tabbed or wizard UIs — the tradeoff is that CSS `visibility: hidden` and `display: none` are treated identically by Playwright's visibility check, but `opacity: 0` elements ARE considered visible (Playwright visibility is purely about layout presence); use `toHaveCSS('opacity', '1')` as a supplemental oracle if your UI uses opacity-based show/hide transitions.

**Pattern 453** — `page.consoleMessages()` + `page.pageErrors()` Post-Hoc Diagnostic Oracle

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('post-hoc diagnostic oracle — full user journey console audit', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('user@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel(/password/i).fill('correct-password');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/);

  await page.goto('/settings/profile');
  await page.getByLabel(/display name/i).fill('Updated Name');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).click();

  await page.goto('/notifications');
  await page.getByRole('switch', { name: /email notifications/i }).click();

  // Post-hoc diagnostic harvest (Playwright v1.56+)
  const consoleMessages = await page.consoleMessages();
  const pageErrors = await page.pageErrors();

  // Oracle: no errors or warnings during the full journey
  const errors = consoleMessages.filter((m) => m.type() === 'error');
  const warnings = consoleMessages.filter((m) => m.type() === 'warning');

  expect(errors, `Console errors during session: ${errors.map((e) => e.text()).join('; ')}`).toHaveLength(0);

  // Soft-oracle: warn on unexpected console warnings but don't fail
  if (warnings.length > 0) {
    console.warn('Session warnings:', warnings.map((w) => w.text()));
  }

  expect(pageErrors, `Uncaught JS errors: ${pageErrors.map((e) => e.message).join('; ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.consoleMessages()` and `page.pageErrors()` (Playwright v1.56+) provide a complete post-hoc log of all console output and uncaught errors from the entire page lifetime without requiring event listeners to be registered before navigation — far simpler than `page.on('console', ...)` in session harnesses; the tradeoff is that these methods return all messages buffered in memory for the page's lifetime, so on very long-running sessions with high console verbosity (e.g., React DevTools in development mode), the buffer can grow large; filter aggressively by type and source URL to keep assertions focused.

**Pattern 454** — `expect.poll()` Async Convergence Oracle for Background Jobs

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('async convergence oracle — file processing job completion', async ({ page, request }) => {
  await page.goto('/uploads');

  // Trigger an upload that initiates a background processing job
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /upload file/i }).click();
  await page.setInputFiles('input[type="file"]', {
    name: 'test-import.csv',
    mimeType: 'text/csv',
    buffer: Buffer.from('id,name\n1,Alice\n2,Bob\n3,Charlie'),
  });
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /start import/i }).click();

  // Capture job ID from the response
  const jobIdEl = page.getByTestId('job-id');
  await expect(jobIdEl).not.toBeEmpty();
  const jobId = await jobIdEl.textContent();

  // expect.poll() retries the assertion until timeout or success
  await expect.poll(
    async () => {
      const res = await request.get(`/api/jobs/${jobId}`);
      const body = await res.json();
      return body.status;
    },
    { timeout: 30_000, intervals: [500, 1000, 2000, 5000], message: 'Job did not complete in time' }
  ).toBe('completed');

  // Oracle: result page must reflect imported row count
  await page.goto(`/imports/${jobId}/results`);
  await expect(page.getByText(/3 records imported/i)).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `expect.poll()` (Playwright v1.23+, enhanced in v1.61) replaces custom retry loops with a declarative async convergence assertion that has configurable intervals and a clear timeout message — it automatically retries any async callback and provides a structured failure message; the tradeoff is that each poll interval makes a real network request (or page interaction), so in high-frequency polling (every 200ms) across many parallel test workers, you risk saturating the backend API under test; use the `intervals` array to implement exponential backoff rather than a fixed short interval.

**Pattern 455** — Charter Branching with `test.info().annotations` Risk Re-Scorer

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

type RiskLevel = 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'critical';

function rescore(
  current: RiskLevel,
  raisers: number,
  lowers: number
): RiskLevel {
  const scale: RiskLevel[] = ['low', 'medium', 'high', 'critical'];
  let idx = scale.indexOf(current);
  idx = Math.min(scale.length - 1, idx + raisers);
  idx = Math.max(0, idx - lowers);
  return scale[idx];
}

test('risk re-scorer — payment settings charter', async ({ page }, testInfo) => {
  let risk: RiskLevel = 'medium';
  let raisers = 0, lowers = 0;

  await page.goto('/settings/payment');

  // Observation 1: no HTTPS warning — lower risk
  const isHttps = page.url().startsWith('https');
  if (isHttps) lowers++;
  else raisers += 2; // security concern raises risk significantly

  // Observation 2: CVV field masks input
  const cvvVisible = await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).getAttribute('type');
  if (cvvVisible === 'password') lowers++;
  else raisers++;

  // Observation 3: form submits without CSRF token — risk raiser
  const csrfInput = await page.locator('input[name="_csrf"], input[name="csrfToken"]').count();
  if (csrfInput === 0) raisers++;

  risk = rescore(risk, raisers, lowers);

  testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'session-risk', description: risk });
  testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'branch-decision', description: risk === 'critical' ? 'escalate' : 'continue' });

  if (risk === 'critical') {
    testInfo.annotations.push({ type: 'branch-charter', description: 'Explore payment CSRF/XSS surface in dedicated security charter' });
  }

  // Oracle: regardless of risk score, form must have basic security attributes
  await expect(page.locator('form[method="post"]')).toHaveCount(1);
});
```
Tradeoff: Inline risk re-scoring during session execution lets a harness make charter-branching decisions dynamically (continue / extend / escalate) based on accumulated evidence — this mirrors the in-session risk judgment a skilled human tester makes, and produces a structured annotation trail in the Playwright HTML report; the tradeoff is that automated risk scoring can create false confidence: the heuristics encoded in `rescore()` encode the tester's priors, not ground truth, and a low risk score does not mean an area is safe — treat the score as a routing signal, not a security certification.

---

**Pattern 456** — `page.setInputFiles()` with Virtual Buffer for Upload-Surface Exploration

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const maliciousFilenames = [
  '../../../etc/passwd',
  'test<script>.csv',
  'file with spaces.csv',
  'very-' + 'long-'.repeat(50) + 'name.csv',
  '␀null-byte.csv',
  '.hidden-file',
];

test('upload surface oracle — filename sanitisation and type enforcement', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/uploads/new');

  const fileInput = page.locator('input[type="file"]');

  for (const filename of maliciousFilenames) {
    await fileInput.setInputFiles({
      name: filename,
      mimeType: 'text/csv',
      buffer: Buffer.from('id,value\n1,test'),
    });
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /upload/i }).click();

    // Oracle: server must reject or sanitise — never echo the raw filename back
    const pageText = await page.locator('body').textContent();
    expect(pageText).not.toContain('../../../etc/passwd');
    expect(pageText).not.toContain('<script>');

    // Check for unhandled error pages
    const httpError = await page.locator('[data-testid="error-boundary"], .error-page').isVisible();
    expect(httpError, `Unhandled error on filename: ${filename}`).toBe(false);
  }

  // Oracle: accept-attribute restricts MIME type in the file picker
  const acceptAttr = await fileInput.getAttribute('accept');
  expect(acceptAttr, 'File input should restrict accepted types').toBeTruthy();
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.setInputFiles()` with virtual buffer objects (no real file on disk) enables rapid iteration over dozens of edge-case filenames and MIME types in a single session without creating temporary files — but virtual buffers bypass OS-level file system security checks (e.g., macOS Gatekeeper won't scan a buffer); pair this with server-side integration tests that actually write the files to disk to cover the full sanitisation pipeline end-to-end.

**Pattern 457** — `locator.pressSequentially()` Progressive Form-Field Exploration

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('pressSequentially oracle — autocomplete and masked input exploration', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/profile/edit');

  // Explore autocomplete: type character by character to trigger suggestions
  const cityField = page.getByLabel(/city/i);
  await cityField.click();
  await cityField.pressSequentially('San F', { delay: 80 });

  // Oracle: autocomplete dropdown should appear after 3+ chars
  const dropdown = page.locator('[role="listbox"], [role="option"]');
  await expect(dropdown.first()).toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });
  const firstSuggestion = await dropdown.first().textContent();
  expect(firstSuggestion).toMatch(/san f/i);

  // Explore masked phone input: type digits and verify formatting
  const phoneField = page.getByLabel(/phone/i);
  await phoneField.click();
  await phoneField.pressSequentially('4155550123', { delay: 50 });

  // Oracle: phone field should auto-format as (415) 555-0123
  const phoneValue = await phoneField.inputValue();
  expect(phoneValue).toMatch(/\(415\)\s?555.0123/);

  // Oracle: no digit beyond the mask length should be accepted
  await phoneField.pressSequentially('9999', { delay: 30 });
  const afterOverflow = await phoneField.inputValue();
  expect(afterOverflow).toMatch(/\(415\)\s?555.0123/); // unchanged
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.pressSequentially()` (Playwright v1.38+, replacing the deprecated `locator.type()`) fires individual `keydown`, `keypress`, `input`, and `keyup` events for each character with an optional delay, faithfully simulating real typing for autocomplete, masked input, and inline validation listeners — the tradeoff over `locator.fill()` is speed: in CI without delay, `pressSequentially` is still slower than `fill` because it dispatches multiple events per character; use `pressSequentially` only for fields where character-by-character event handling is the feature under test, and `fill` for fields where the final value is what matters.

### Community Gotchas

**G65: `page.waitForNavigation()` is deprecated in Playwright v1.26+ — tests that still use it receive a no-op promise in newer versions, silently missing navigation completion and proceeding before the page has loaded.**
Teams migrating older Playwright suites to v1.40+ found that `await page.waitForNavigation()` calls no longer produced errors but also no longer waited for anything: navigation completed before the deprecated method resolved, but the test continued immediately, causing intermittent failures in the following assertions. The root cause is that Playwright replaced `waitForNavigation` with the promise-based `page.goto()` + `page.waitForURL()` model; the method was deprecated (with a deprecation warning in v1.26) and eventually became a no-op stub. Teams relying on it for post-click navigation waits in session harnesses produced tests that passed in isolation but failed under CI load.
Fix: Replace all `await page.waitForNavigation()` calls with `await page.waitForURL(/expected-path/)` after the triggering click, or use `await Promise.all([page.waitForURL(...), trigger.click()])` for synchronous click+navigate patterns. Run `npx playwright codegen` on the same flow to see the generated modern equivalent.

---

**G66: `locator.nth(0)` on a list of dynamically rendered items does not guarantee the first item by insertion order — it returns the first element in DOM order, which in virtualised lists (react-window, TanStack Virtual) may be a recycled node from a previous scroll position.**
A team exploring a paginated data table built with TanStack Virtual found that `page.getByRole('row').nth(0).getByRole('cell').first().textContent()` returned a different row's data on repeated runs — the virtual list recycled DOM nodes during scroll, meaning the first DOM row at test assertion time was not the first data row. The test appeared stable in headed mode (where scroll position was always reset) but flaked in headless CI runs where scroll position was occasionally non-zero from a previous test's state leaking through a shared context.
Fix: For virtualised lists, scroll to the top explicitly (`page.locator('[data-testid="list-container"]').evaluate((el) => el.scrollTop = 0)`) before targeting items by index. Prefer selecting rows by their data content (`page.getByRole('row', { name: /expected-value/ })`) rather than positional index, as content-based matching is stable regardless of virtual scroll state.

---

**G67: `page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i })` matches buttons whose accessible name includes "submit" anywhere — including hidden ARIA labels on icon-only buttons with a visually-hidden `<span>Submit</span>`, causing unexpected matches in forms with multiple such elements.**
A team building a form explorer found that `page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i })` matched three different buttons on a complex form page: the primary "Submit" CTA, a confirmation dialog's "Submit changes" button (rendered in the DOM but hidden via `display:none`), and an icon button with an ARIA label of "Submit feedback" in the page footer. The test failed with "strict mode violation: getByRole resolved to 3 elements." The team had not accounted for hidden-but-present elements (Playwright includes elements with `display:none` in role matching by default unless `{ visible: true }` is specified).
Fix: Add `.filter({ visible: true })` to scope matching to currently rendered elements, or use a more specific accessible name (e.g., `{ name: 'Submit order' }` with exact string matching using `{ exact: true }`) to disambiguate. Document which button you intend to target in the charter's exploration notes for future session reproducibility.

---

**G68: `page.evaluate()` callbacks execute in the browser context and cannot reference TypeScript variables from the outer test scope via closure — only values explicitly passed through the second argument are serialised and available inside the callback.**
Teams writing session harnesses in TypeScript found that referencing a test-scoped constant inside `page.evaluate()` (e.g., `await page.evaluate(() => console.log(myConst))`) always produced `undefined` for `myConst`, even though it was defined in the enclosing `test()` block. TypeScript compiled the test without error because the closure reference was syntactically valid, but at runtime the serialised callback string contained no closure — Playwright serialises the function to a string and re-evaluates it in the browser, where the outer scope variables do not exist.
Fix: Always pass external values as the second argument to `page.evaluate()`: `await page.evaluate((val) => console.log(val), myConst)`. For complex objects, ensure they are JSON-serialisable (no class instances, functions, or circular references). Add a custom ESLint rule (`no-restricted-syntax` targeting `page.evaluate(fn)` without a second arg when `fn` references outer variables) to catch this pattern during code review.

---

**G69: `expect(locator).toBeEnabled()` returns `true` for form elements whose parent `<fieldset>` is `disabled` — the locator assertion checks only the element's own `disabled` attribute, not the inherited disabled state from an ancestor `<fieldset>`.**
A team exploring a multi-step form with a disabled fieldset (used to lock completed sections) found that `await expect(page.getByLabel('Email')).toBeEnabled()` passed even though the email input was inside a `<fieldset disabled>` and was visually greyed out and non-interactive. The root cause is that the HTML `disabled` attribute is only valid on specific form elements (`input`, `button`, `select`, `textarea`, `optgroup`, `option`, `fieldset`) and inherits to descendants when set on a `<fieldset>`, but Playwright's `toBeEnabled()` checks only the element's own `disabled` IDL attribute — not the inherited computed disabled state that the browser applies through the `fieldset` ancestor.
Fix: Supplement `toBeEnabled()` with a direct attribute check on the `<fieldset>`: `await expect(page.locator('fieldset:has([name="email"])')).not.toHaveAttribute('disabled')`, or use `locator.evaluate((el) => (el as HTMLInputElement).matches(':disabled'))` which respects the CSS `:disabled` pseudo-class and includes inherited disabled state. File this as a Playwright known limitation in your team's testing handbook.

## Cycle 60 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 458** — `page.addLocatorHandler()` for Automatic Overlay Dismissal in Exploration Sessions
```typescript
test('explore checkout flow past intermittent cookie banner', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Register a handler that fires before any actionability check
  // when the cookie consent overlay becomes visible
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie/i }),
    async (dialog) => {
      await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: /accept/i }).click();
    },
    { times: 1 } // auto-deregisters after first invocation
  );

  // Now explore checkout steps without defensive overlay logic on each action
  await page.getByLabel(/first name/i).fill('Ada');
  await page.getByLabel(/last name/i).fill('Lovelace');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue/i }).click();

  // Oracle: billing step should be visible without banner interference
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /billing/i })).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `addLocatorHandler` removes defensive overlay-dismissal boilerplate from every action in a long session harness, but the handler alters focus and mouse position mid-test, so any subsequent action that depends on retained focus or cursor state (e.g., `keyboard.press('Enter')` after a `locator.focus()`) must be rewritten as self-contained `locator.press()` calls — mixing focus-dependent sequences with an active handler produces nondeterministic results.
