## Cycle 62 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 488: `page.clock.install()` + `clock.setFixedTime()` for Exploratory Session Replay of Timestamp-Sensitive UI** [official]

Freeze the browser clock to a specific point in time before beginning an exploratory session so that every timestamp-dependent UI element renders deterministically. This removes flakiness caused by the system clock advancing between actions and allows the session to be replayed identically at any future date without snapshot drift.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test.describe('Session: timestamp-sensitive dashboard exploration', () => {
  test('explore activity feed at a fixed point in time', async ({ page }) => {
    // Freeze the clock BEFORE navigating so all Date constructors in
    // app bootstrap code see the same epoch value.
    await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-03-15T09:00:00Z') });

    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    // Confirm the "last updated" badge renders the frozen date, not now.
    await expect(
      page.getByTestId('last-updated-badge')
    ).toHaveText(/Mar 15, 2026/);

    // Advance clock by 30 minutes to explore auto-refresh behaviour.
    await page.clock.fastForward('30:00');

    // The feed should have issued a refresh request after 30 min.
    await expect(
      page.getByTestId('feed-refresh-indicator')
    ).toBeVisible();

    // Advance to 8-hour session-timeout threshold to explore logout prompt.
    await page.clock.fastForward('07:30:00');
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /session expiring/i })
    ).toBeVisible();

    // Screenshot the final state as a session artefact.
    await page.screenshot({ path: 'session-artefacts/clock-expiry.png' });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Freezing the browser clock with `page.clock.install()` before navigation gives the exploratory session a stable, reproducible time baseline and enables fast-forwarding through multi-hour inactivity timeouts in milliseconds — the tradeoff is that `page.clock.install()` intercepts `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, `requestAnimationFrame`, and `performance.now()` at the browser level but does NOT affect server-side timestamps returned by API responses; if the server generates `createdAt` fields using its own clock, the UI may show a mismatch between the frozen browser date and the server-issued timestamps, producing confusing session artefacts; pair `clock.install()` with a `route.fulfill()` or `route.fetch()` response modifier that rewrites server-issued date fields to match the frozen clock epoch.

---

**Pattern 489: `page.exposeFunction()` Probe Injection for In-Session DOM Mutation Logging** [official]

Inject a named JavaScript function into the page's global scope that the exploratory session's app code can call to stream internal state events back to the test process, enabling passive observation of mutations, state transitions, and Redux/Zustand dispatch events without any permanent instrumentation in the source code.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';

test('session: observe internal state transitions during checkout flow', async ({ page }) => {
  const stateLog: Array<{ ts: number; event: string; payload: unknown }> = [];

  // Expose a probe function into the page's global scope.
  // The app (or an addInitScript) can call window.__probe(event, payload)
  // to stream events back to this test process.
  await page.exposeFunction(
    '__probe',
    (event: string, payload: unknown) => {
      stateLog.push({ ts: Date.now(), event, payload });
    }
  );

  // Inject an init script that hooks into the app's state manager.
  // This runs before every navigation so the hook survives SPA route changes.
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    const origDispatch = (window as any).__store?.dispatch;
    if (origDispatch) {
      (window as any).__store.dispatch = (action: unknown) => {
        (window as any).__probe('redux-dispatch', action);
        return origDispatch(action);
      };
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i }).click();
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /proceed to checkout/i }).click();
  await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /place order/i }).click();
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })
  ).toBeVisible();

  // Flush log to session artefact for debrief review.
  fs.writeFileSync(
    'session-artefacts/checkout-state-log.json',
    JSON.stringify(stateLog, null, 2)
  );

  // Assert that a payment action was dispatched.
  const paymentEvent = stateLog.find(e => e.event === 'redux-dispatch' &&
    (e.payload as any)?.type === 'PAYMENT_CONFIRMED');
  expect(paymentEvent).toBeDefined();
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.exposeFunction()` lets the test process receive real-time events from inside the browser sandbox without modifying source code, making it ideal for passive observation during exploratory sessions — the tradeoff is that the exposed function is registered on the page object after it is created, meaning it is not available during the initial HTML parse or any scripts that run synchronously before the first `DOMContentLoaded`; combine it with `page.addInitScript()` (which runs before page scripts) to install the hook early, but note that `addInitScript` callbacks cannot directly call the exposed function — they can only queue calls that will execute after `exposeFunction` has registered the bridge, so avoid relying on probe calls from synchronous top-level module initializers.

---

**Pattern 490: `context.routeFromHAR()` with `update: true` + `update: false` Toggle for Offline-Reproducible Exploratory Branches** [official]

Record a live network session to a HAR file during the first exploratory pass, then replay it in subsequent branches with the network fully mocked, enabling consistent offline re-exploration of the exact same server state without API rate limits, authentication expiry, or backend state drift between runs.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as path from 'path';

const HAR_PATH = path.join(__dirname, 'fixtures', 'product-search.har');

// STEP 1 — Run once with UPDATE_HAR=true to record a live session.
// STEP 2 — Run without the env var to replay from the recorded HAR.
const recordMode = process.env.UPDATE_HAR === 'true';

test.describe('Session: product search exploration (HAR-backed)', () => {
  test.use({ storageState: './tmp/auth-state.json' });

  test('explore search result ranking and filter combinations', async ({ context, page }) => {
    // In record mode: proxy all requests through the real server and save.
    // In replay mode: serve all matching requests from the saved HAR.
    await context.routeFromHAR(HAR_PATH, {
      update: recordMode,
      url: '**/api/**',             // only intercept API traffic
      updateContent: 'embed',       // embed response bodies inside the HAR
    });

    await page.goto('/products');

    // Branch 1: default sort order
    await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /sort by/i }).selectOption('relevance');
    await expect(page.getByTestId('result-count')).toContainText(/\d+ results/);

    // Branch 2: price ascending — explores a different server query
    await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /sort by/i }).selectOption('price-asc');
    await expect(page.getByTestId('result-count')).toContainText(/\d+ results/);

    // Branch 3: apply category filter while sorted by price
    await page.getByRole('checkbox', { name: /electronics/i }).check();
    const filteredCount = await page
      .getByTestId('result-count')
      .textContent();

    await page.screenshot({
      path: 'session-artefacts/filtered-results.png',
      fullPage: true,
    });

    expect(filteredCount).toMatch(/\d+ results/);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `context.routeFromHAR()` with `update: true` on the first pass captures a real-network session snapshot that all subsequent offline branches replay deterministically, eliminating flakiness from live backend state changes, rate limits, and auth token rotation — the tradeoff is that HAR replay uses exact URL + HTTP method matching (and body matching for POST requests), so any variation in request payloads between the record session and the replay session (e.g., a timestamp or CSRF token embedded in POST body) will cause the interceptor to fall back to a real network call or return a 404 from the HAR; use `context.routeFromHAR()` with `{ notFound: 'fallback' }` so unmatched requests pass through to the real server during development, and audit the HAR file after recording to replace volatile tokens with `*` glob patterns in the `url` field.

---

**Pattern 491: `page.addLocatorHandler()` for Automatic Overlay Dismissal During Free-Form Exploration Sessions** [official]

Register a `locator handler` for every overlay, cookie banner, survey popup, and GDPR consent dialog that might appear mid-session. This prevents the exploration from halting on unexpected UI interruptions, allows the session to continue unattended through all branches, and accumulates a log of every overlay that appeared for post-session debrief review.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: free-form navigation with automatic overlay dismissal', async ({ page }) => {
  const overlayLog: Array<{ overlay: string; url: string; ts: number }> = [];

  // Register handlers for all known overlay types.
  // Each handler fires whenever the locator is visible before an action.
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('button', { name: /accept all cookies/i }),
    async (btn) => {
      overlayLog.push({ overlay: 'cookie-banner', url: page.url(), ts: Date.now() });
      await btn.click();
    }
  );

  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /take a survey/i }),
    async (dialog) => {
      overlayLog.push({ overlay: 'survey-modal', url: page.url(), ts: Date.now() });
      await dialog.getByRole('button', { name: /no thanks/i }).click();
    }
  );

  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByTestId('gdpr-banner'),
    async (banner) => {
      overlayLog.push({ overlay: 'gdpr-banner', url: page.url(), ts: Date.now() });
      await banner.getByRole('button', { name: /dismiss/i }).click();
    }
  );

  // Begin exploration — overlays are handled transparently.
  const explorationPaths = ['/home', '/products', '/blog', '/pricing', '/contact'];
  for (const path of explorationPaths) {
    await page.goto(path);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    await page.screenshot({
      path: `session-artefacts/${path.replace('/', '')}-clean.png`,
    });
  }

  // Surface overlay encounter report for session debrief.
  console.log('Overlay encounters during session:', JSON.stringify(overlayLog, null, 2));

  // Assert no overlay appeared more than once per route (regression signal).
  const routeOverlayCounts = overlayLog.reduce<Record<string, number>>((acc, e) => {
    acc[e.url] = (acc[e.url] ?? 0) + 1;
    return acc;
  }, {});
  const problemRoutes = Object.entries(routeOverlayCounts).filter(([, count]) => count > 1);
  expect(problemRoutes).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.addLocatorHandler()` enables fully unattended exploratory sessions across routes that intermittently surface overlays without stopping the session charter — the tradeoff is that locator handlers are checked before every Playwright action (not on a timer), so a handler registered for a modal that only appears after a delay may not trigger if the next action happens before the modal becomes visible; additionally, if two handlers match simultaneously (e.g., a GDPR banner and a cookie consent dialog appearing together), Playwright fires them sequentially in registration order without waiting for the first dismissed overlay to fully close before evaluating the second, which can cause `ElementNotVisible` errors in the second handler; add a `page.waitForTimeout(200)` inside each handler after clicking to allow CSS transitions to complete before the next handler fires.

---

**Pattern 492: `page.ariaSnapshot()` Structural Diffing Between Session Branches for Accessibility Regression Detection** [official]

Capture the ARIA accessibility tree as a YAML string at key branch decision points during an exploratory session and diff the snapshots programmatically to detect structural regressions — missing roles, changed accessible names, or collapsed heading hierarchies — that would not be visible in a visual screenshot comparison.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';

test('session: ARIA structure comparison across user roles', async ({ browser }) => {
  // Branch A: explore as anonymous user
  const anonContext = await browser.newContext();
  const anonPage = await anonContext.newPage();
  await anonPage.goto('/dashboard');
  await anonPage.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  const anonSnapshot = await anonPage.ariaSnapshot();
  await anonContext.close();

  // Branch B: explore as authenticated admin
  const adminContext = await browser.newContext({
    storageState: './tmp/admin-auth.json',
  });
  const adminPage = await adminContext.newPage();
  await adminPage.goto('/dashboard');
  await adminPage.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  const adminSnapshot = await adminPage.ariaSnapshot();
  await adminContext.close();

  // Persist both snapshots as session artefacts for debrief.
  fs.writeFileSync('session-artefacts/aria-anon.yaml', anonSnapshot);
  fs.writeFileSync('session-artefacts/aria-admin.yaml', adminSnapshot);

  // Assert that the admin view exposes admin-only navigation landmarks.
  expect(adminSnapshot).toContain('navigation "Admin Panel"');

  // Assert the anon view does NOT expose admin controls.
  expect(anonSnapshot).not.toContain('Admin Panel');

  // Assert common structural invariant: both views have a main landmark.
  expect(anonSnapshot).toContain('- main');
  expect(adminSnapshot).toContain('- main');

  // Assert heading hierarchy integrity in admin view.
  await expect(adminPage.locator('main')).toMatchAriaSnapshot(`
    - main:
      - heading "Dashboard" [level=1]
      - heading /Analytics/ [level=2]
      - heading /Users/ [level=2]
  `);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.ariaSnapshot()` captures the full ARIA accessibility tree as a diffable YAML string, enabling structural regression detection across session branches that reveals missing roles and changed accessible names invisible to pixel-level screenshot comparison — the tradeoff is that the ARIA tree reflects the browser's computed accessibility tree, which can differ significantly across browsers (Chromium's AX tree is more granular than WebKit's for certain composite widgets like `combobox` and `listbox`), so snapshots recorded in Chromium cannot be reliably diffed against WebKit-captured snapshots without role-normalisation preprocessing; when using `toMatchAriaSnapshot()` in cross-browser test projects, prefer partial matching patterns with `[level=1]`-style attribute filters rather than full tree exact matches to avoid browser-specific tree shape differences causing false negatives.

**Pattern 493: `page.evaluate()` + `PerformanceObserver` Registration for Long-Task Budget Monitoring During Exploratory Flows** [official]

Inject a `PerformanceObserver` that collects `longtask` entries during the exploratory session charter and flush them as a session artefact at the end, establishing a passive performance budget oracle that flags interactions exceeding 50 ms of main-thread blocking without requiring any app-side instrumentation.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: long-task budget monitoring during multi-step onboarding', async ({ page }) => {
  // Install the PerformanceObserver before navigation.
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    (window as any).__longTasks = [];
    const obs = new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
      for (const entry of list.getEntries()) {
        (window as any).__longTasks.push({
          name: entry.name,
          duration: Math.round(entry.duration),
          startTime: Math.round(entry.startTime),
        });
      }
    });
    obs.observe({ type: 'longtask', buffered: true });
  });

  await page.goto('/onboarding/step-1');

  // Step through all onboarding stages while the observer accumulates entries.
  const steps = [
    { button: /next: choose plan/i, heading: /choose your plan/i },
    { button: /next: account setup/i, heading: /create your account/i },
    { button: /next: payment/i, heading: /payment details/i },
    { button: /complete setup/i, heading: /welcome!/i },
  ];

  for (const step of steps) {
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: step.button }).click();
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('heading', { name: step.heading })
    ).toBeVisible();
  }

  // Flush the observer and retrieve long-task entries.
  const longTasks = await page.evaluate(
    () => (window as any).__longTasks as Array<{ name: string; duration: number; startTime: number }>
  );

  // Attach findings to the test report.
  const report = longTasks.length > 0
    ? JSON.stringify(longTasks, null, 2)
    : 'No long tasks detected.';

  await test.info().attach('long-tasks-report', {
    body: report,
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  // Fail the session if any single interaction blocked the main thread > 200 ms.
  const criticalTasks = longTasks.filter(t => t.duration > 200);
  expect(criticalTasks, `Critical long tasks detected: ${JSON.stringify(criticalTasks)}`).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Embedding a `PerformanceObserver` via `addInitScript` gives the exploratory session passive access to every long task entry throughout the entire charter without pausing or instrumenting any application code — the tradeoff is that the `longtask` entry type is only supported in Chromium-based browsers; Firefox and Safari do not expose `PerformanceObserver` `longtask` entries, so this pattern is inherently Chromium-specific and should be guarded with `test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', ...)` in cross-browser projects to avoid false passes where the observer silently registers zero entries because the entry type is unsupported rather than because no long tasks occurred.

**Pattern 494: `testInfo.attach()` + Named Session Artefact Taxonomy for Structured Exploratory Debrief** [official]

Define a session artefact taxonomy (screenshots, network logs, state snapshots, aria dumps, console logs) and attach each artefact to the Playwright HTML report using `testInfo.attach()` with a consistent naming convention, transforming the HTML report into a structured exploratory session debrief document that reviewers can navigate without access to the raw file system.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Artefact taxonomy constants for consistent naming across sessions.
const ARTEFACT = {
  SCREENSHOT: (label: string) => `screenshot:${label}`,
  NETWORK: (label: string) => `network-log:${label}`,
  ARIA: (label: string) => `aria-snapshot:${label}`,
  CONSOLE: 'console-log',
  STATE: (label: string) => `state-dump:${label}`,
} as const;

test('session: user profile edit — charter-driven exploration', async ({ page }) => {
  const consoleEntries: string[] = [];
  page.on('console', msg => consoleEntries.push(`[${msg.type()}] ${msg.text()}`));

  await page.goto('/profile/edit');
  await test.info().attach(ARTEFACT.SCREENSHOT('initial-state'), {
    body: await page.screenshot(),
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });

  // Charter branch 1: explore validation error states.
  await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('not-an-email');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save changes/i }).click();
  await test.info().attach(ARTEFACT.SCREENSHOT('validation-errors'), {
    body: await page.screenshot(),
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });

  // Capture ARIA snapshot of error messages for accessibility audit.
  const errorRegion = page.getByRole('alert');
  await test.info().attach(ARTEFACT.ARIA('validation-error-alerts'), {
    body: Buffer.from(await errorRegion.ariaSnapshot()),
    contentType: 'text/plain',
  });

  // Charter branch 2: explore successful save.
  await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('valid@example.com');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save changes/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toContainText(/saved/i);
  await test.info().attach(ARTEFACT.SCREENSHOT('after-successful-save'), {
    body: await page.screenshot(),
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });

  // Attach console log as session debrief evidence.
  await test.info().attach(ARTEFACT.CONSOLE, {
    body: consoleEntries.join('\n') || '(no console output)',
    contentType: 'text/plain',
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Attaching all session artefacts via `testInfo.attach()` with a structured naming taxonomy surfaces exploratory evidence directly in the Playwright HTML report, making the session self-documenting and reviewable by stakeholders without file-system access — the tradeoff is that `testInfo.attach()` with `body` buffers holds artefacts in memory until the test completes, and attaching many large screenshots (especially `fullPage: true` at high resolution) or long console logs across a multi-branch exploratory test with 20+ route visits can push the Playwright worker process beyond its memory budget, causing the test to be killed by the OS rather than fail gracefully; for long exploratory sessions, use `testInfo.attachPath()` (which references an on-disk file by path rather than buffering the content in memory) for large artefacts like full-page screenshots, reserving in-memory `attach()` for small text payloads like ARIA snapshots and state dumps.

**Pattern 495: Multi-Context Role Simulation with `browser.newContext()` + Shared `browserServer` for Concurrent Session Branching** [official]

Create multiple isolated browser contexts within a single exploratory test to simulate concurrent users in different roles, enabling exploration of real-time collaboration features, role-based access boundaries, and session isolation invariants within a single test charter.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: concurrent admin + regular-user collaboration exploration', async ({ browser }) => {
  // Spawn isolated contexts for each role — separate cookies, localStorage, etc.
  const adminCtx = await browser.newContext({
    storageState: './tmp/admin-auth.json',
  });
  const userCtx = await browser.newContext({
    storageState: './tmp/user-auth.json',
  });

  const adminPage = await adminCtx.newPage();
  const userPage = await userCtx.newPage();

  // Both parties navigate to the same shared document.
  await Promise.all([
    adminPage.goto('/docs/shared-123'),
    userPage.goto('/docs/shared-123'),
  ]);

  // Admin locks the document for editing.
  await adminPage.getByRole('button', { name: /lock for editing/i }).click();
  await expect(
    adminPage.getByRole('status')
  ).toContainText(/document locked/i);

  // Explore: does the user view reflect the lock in real time?
  await userPage.waitForResponse('**/api/docs/*/lock-status');
  await expect(
    userPage.getByRole('alert', { name: /read-only/i })
  ).toBeVisible();

  // Explore: can the user still attempt an edit? (should be blocked)
  await userPage.getByRole('textbox', { name: /document body/i }).fill('attempted edit');
  await expect(
    userPage.getByRole('status')
  ).toContainText(/cannot edit: document is locked/i);

  // Admin unlocks — user should regain write access.
  await adminPage.getByRole('button', { name: /unlock document/i }).click();
  await userPage.waitForResponse('**/api/docs/*/lock-status');
  await expect(
    userPage.getByRole('textbox', { name: /document body/i })
  ).toBeEnabled();

  await Promise.all([adminCtx.close(), userCtx.close()]);
});
```
Tradeoff: Using multiple `browser.newContext()` instances in a single test enables real-time multi-role exploratory charters that verify collaboration and role-boundary invariants within a single test session without requiring two separate test runs — the tradeoff is that each context spawns a separate browser renderer process, meaning a test with four concurrent contexts can consume 400–600 MB of RAM; in resource-constrained CI environments this can trigger OOM kills of the worker process; limit concurrent exploratory contexts to two or three roles per test and use `Promise.all([ctx.close()])` cleanup to release renderer memory eagerly before the test teardown phase rather than relying on the fixture lifecycle's automatic cleanup, which occurs after the test result is recorded.

**Pattern 496: `page.route()` + `route.fetch()` Response-Mutation Oracle for API Contract Exploration** [official]

Intercept real API responses, mutate specific fields to boundary or invalid values, and verify how the UI responds to each mutation, enabling systematic contract exploration of every UI component's resilience to unexpected API payloads without requiring backend changes or a separate contract-testing tool.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const MUTATIONS: Array<{ label: string; mutate: (body: Record<string, unknown>) => void }> = [
  { label: 'null-user-name',     mutate: b => { (b as any).user.name = null; } },
  { label: 'empty-items-array',  mutate: b => { (b as any).items = []; } },
  { label: 'negative-total',     mutate: b => { (b as any).total = -99.99; } },
  { label: 'missing-status',     mutate: b => { delete (b as any).status; } },
  { label: 'huge-item-count',    mutate: b => { (b as any).items = Array(500).fill({ id: 1, name: 'x', qty: 1 }); } },
];

for (const { label, mutate } of MUTATIONS) {
  test(`session: order summary resilience — mutation:${label}`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.route('**/api/orders/current', async (route) => {
      // Fetch the real response then mutate it before forwarding to the browser.
      const response = await route.fetch();
      const body = await response.json() as Record<string, unknown>;
      mutate(body);
      await route.fulfill({
        response,
        body: JSON.stringify(body),
        contentType: 'application/json',
      });
    });

    await page.goto('/order-summary');

    // The UI must not throw a JS error regardless of the mutation applied.
    const errors: string[] = [];
    page.on('pageerror', err => errors.push(err.message));

    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    await page.screenshot({
      path: `session-artefacts/mutation-${label}.png`,
      fullPage: true,
    });

    expect(errors, `JS errors with mutation ${label}: ${errors.join('; ')}`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Iterating over a mutation matrix with `route.fetch()` + `route.fulfill()` lets an exploratory session probe every field of a real API response for UI contract violations in a single chartered test file, catching missing null guards, negative-number rendering bugs, and empty-state omissions without requiring backend fixture data — the tradeoff is that `route.fetch()` performs a real network call for every intercepted request, meaning each mutation branch makes a live API call; in CI environments with strict egress firewalling or slow API backends this increases test duration and introduces network-failure flakiness; replace the `route.fetch()` call with a `route.fulfill({ json: baseFixture })` approach that starts from a static fixture (recorded once from a real response) and applies mutations to the fixture object, eliminating the live-network dependency entirely.

---

**Pattern 497: `test.step()` Charter Annotation with `test.info().annotations` for Machine-Readable Session Debrief Export** [official]

Annotate exploratory session branches with structured metadata via `test.info().annotations.push()` inside each `test.step()` scope, enabling post-session tooling to extract branch decisions, findings, and risk ratings from the Playwright `test-results.json` file without requiring a separate session note document.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

type BranchRating = 'low-risk' | 'medium-risk' | 'high-risk' | 'bug-found';

function annotate(type: BranchRating, value: string) {
  test.info().annotations.push({ type, value });
}

test('session: payment flow charter — branch exploration', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  await test.step('Branch 1: happy-path card payment', async () => {
    await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4111111111111111');
    await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('12/28');
    await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).fill('123');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /payment successful/i })).toBeVisible();
    annotate('low-risk', 'Happy-path card payment completes correctly. No anomalies.');
  });

  await page.goto('/checkout');

  await test.step('Branch 2: expired card handling', async () => {
    await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4111111111111111');
    await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('01/20'); // past date
    await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).fill('123');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();

    const errorMsg = page.getByRole('alert', { name: /card expired/i });
    const visible = await errorMsg.isVisible();
    if (!visible) {
      annotate('bug-found', 'Expired card: no error message shown. Card was charged. Severity: P1.');
    } else {
      annotate('low-risk', 'Expired card correctly rejected with user-facing error message.');
    }
    await page.screenshot({ path: 'session-artefacts/expired-card.png' });
  });

  await test.step('Branch 3: CVV mismatch', async () => {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4111111111111111');
    await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('12/28');
    await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).fill('999');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
    const declined = await page.getByText(/cvv.*incorrect|declined/i).isVisible();
    annotate(
      declined ? 'low-risk' : 'medium-risk',
      `CVV mismatch: ${declined ? 'correctly declined' : 'WARN — no CVV error shown'}`
    );
    await page.screenshot({ path: 'session-artefacts/cvv-mismatch.png' });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Pushing structured annotations into `test.info().annotations` during each `test.step()` branch embeds machine-readable session metadata directly in the Playwright `test-results.json` output, allowing post-session tooling to extract branch risk ratings and bug reports without parsing free-text notes — the tradeoff is that `test.info().annotations` is a flat array with no schema enforcement; every team member must agree on the `type` string vocabulary (e.g., `'bug-found'`, `'high-risk'`) and the `value` format convention, because Playwright does not validate annotation types; inconsistent annotation types across different sessions produce a polluted annotation set that is difficult to aggregate; define annotation type constants in a shared module (as shown with the `BranchRating` union type) and enforce the vocabulary via a lint rule that flags raw `annotations.push({ type: '...' })` calls outside the shared helper function.

---

**Pattern 498: `page.waitForResponse()` with Predicate Function for Adaptive Branch Navigation in Long-Running Exploration Charters** [official]

Use `page.waitForResponse()` with a predicate callback rather than a URL glob to make branching decisions based on actual API response status codes and body content, enabling the exploratory session to dynamically route to different charter branches based on what the server actually returns rather than what was expected.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: adaptive checkout exploration based on real API responses', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('12/28');
  await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).fill('123');

  // Start the response listener before triggering the action.
  const paymentResponsePromise = page.waitForResponse(
    async (response) =>
      response.url().includes('/api/payment') &&
      response.request().method() === 'POST'
  );

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
  const paymentResponse = await paymentResponsePromise;

  const status = paymentResponse.status();
  const body = await paymentResponse.json().catch(() => null) as Record<string, unknown> | null;

  // Adaptive branching: explore the actual path the server took.
  if (status === 200 && body?.transactionId) {
    // Happy path confirmed — explore post-payment state.
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();
    const orderId = await page.getByTestId('order-id').textContent();
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: `order-confirmed:${orderId}` });
  } else if (status === 402) {
    // Payment declined — explore decline recovery UX.
    await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /payment declined/i })).toBeVisible();
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /try another card/i }).click();
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: `payment-declined:${body?.declineCode}` });
  } else if (status >= 500) {
    // Server error during payment — explore error handling UX.
    const errorShown = await page.getByRole('alert', { name: /unexpected error/i }).isVisible();
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'bug-found',
      value: `Server error ${status} during payment. Error UI shown: ${errorShown}.`,
    });
    expect(errorShown, 'Server error must show user-facing error message').toBe(true);
  }

  await page.screenshot({ path: `session-artefacts/payment-outcome-${status}.png` });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.waitForResponse()` with a predicate that inspects status codes and body content allows the session to adaptively branch based on real server behaviour rather than assuming the happy path, making the charter resilient to backend state changes that cause different response codes mid-run — the tradeoff is that `page.waitForResponse()` resolves with the first matching response and then discards all subsequent matching responses; if the checkout page issues multiple `POST /api/payment` requests (e.g., a pre-auth followed by a capture), only the first response is captured for the branching decision; use `page.on('response', handler)` instead to collect all matching responses into an array, and apply the branching logic after `waitForLoadState('networkidle')` once all requests have settled.

---

**Pattern 499: `context.setOffline(true)` / `setOffline(false)` Network Oscillation for Offline-Recovery Exploration Charters** [official]

Toggle the browser context between online and offline states at precise points in the session charter to explore how the application handles connectivity loss during critical operations, verifying offline indicator display, request queuing, automatic retry, and data integrity after reconnection.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: offline recovery during form submission charter', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await page.goto('/long-form');
  await page.getByLabel(/name/i).fill('Session Explorer');
  await page.getByLabel(/email/i).fill('session@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel(/message/i).fill('Exploring offline behaviour during submission.');

  // Go offline immediately before submit to explore mid-submit failure.
  await context.setOffline(true);

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /submit/i }).click();

  // Explore: does the UI surface an offline indicator?
  await expect(
    page.getByRole('alert', { name: /you are offline/i })
  ).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });

  // Explore: are form field values preserved while offline?
  await expect(page.getByLabel(/message/i)).toHaveValue(
    'Exploring offline behaviour during submission.'
  );

  await page.screenshot({ path: 'session-artefacts/offline-state.png' });

  // Restore connectivity and explore retry behaviour.
  await context.setOffline(false);

  // Wait for the app to detect reconnection and auto-retry.
  const retryResponse = await page
    .waitForResponse('**/api/contact', { timeout: 10_000 })
    .catch(() => null);

  if (retryResponse) {
    // Auto-retry succeeded — explore success confirmation.
    await expect(
      page.getByRole('status', { name: /message sent/i })
    ).toBeVisible();
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'low-risk', value: 'Auto-retry on reconnect works correctly.' });
  } else {
    // No auto-retry — explore manual re-submit path.
    const resubmitBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /retry/i });
    const hasRetryButton = await resubmitBtn.isVisible();
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: hasRetryButton ? 'medium-risk' : 'high-risk',
      value: hasRetryButton
        ? 'No auto-retry, but manual retry button is available.'
        : 'BUG: No auto-retry and no retry button. User must reload page and re-enter data.',
    });
  }

  await page.screenshot({ path: 'session-artefacts/after-reconnection.png' });
});
```
Tradeoff: Toggling `context.setOffline(true/false)` at charter branch points gives the session precise control over connectivity state without requiring network proxies or firewall rules, enabling deterministic exploration of offline/reconnect flows on any developer machine — the tradeoff is that `context.setOffline(true)` simulates a complete loss of all TCP connectivity at the browser network layer, which is more severe than real-world offline conditions (where DNS may still resolve cached entries or the device may switch to a slower connection); this means the session may trigger error states that users rarely see (e.g., all XHR requests failing simultaneously rather than timing out gradually), inflating the severity of findings; complement offline oscillation tests with throttled-network tests using `context.route()` + artificial delays to explore realistic degraded-network scenarios.

---

**Pattern 500: `page.keyboard.press()` + `page.keyboard.type()` Keyboard Navigation Charter for Focus Order and Shortcut Coverage** [official]

Drive the entire exploratory session exclusively via keyboard input to systematically charter the tab order, focus indicator visibility, and keyboard shortcut coverage across every interactive element, producing a structured keyboard accessibility map as a session artefact.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: keyboard-only navigation charter for settings page', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings');

  const focusMap: Array<{ index: number; role: string; name: string; hasFocusStyle: boolean }> = [];

  // Tab through the page and record what receives focus.
  for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

    const focused = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement;
      if (!el || el === document.body) return null;
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(el);
      const rect = el.getBoundingClientRect();
      return {
        role: el.getAttribute('role') ?? el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
        name: (el as HTMLElement).getAttribute('aria-label')
          ?? (el as HTMLElement).innerText?.slice(0, 40)
          ?? '',
        hasFocusStyle:
          style.outlineStyle !== 'none' &&
          style.outlineWidth !== '0px' &&
          rect.width > 0,
      };
    });

    if (!focused) break;
    focusMap.push({ index: i, ...focused });

    // Explore: activate focused element via keyboard and check for errors.
    if (focused.role === 'button' || focused.role === 'checkbox') {
      await page.keyboard.press('Space');
      await page.waitForTimeout(100);
    }
  }

  // Attach the focus map as a session debrief artefact.
  await test.info().attach('keyboard-focus-map', {
    body: JSON.stringify(focusMap, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  // Assert: no interactive element has invisible focus styling.
  const noFocusStyle = focusMap.filter(e => !e.hasFocusStyle);
  expect(
    noFocusStyle,
    `Elements missing focus indicator: ${JSON.stringify(noFocusStyle)}`
  ).toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Driving an exploratory session purely via `page.keyboard.press('Tab')` and `page.keyboard.type()` produces a machine-generated focus order map and exposes missing focus indicators without any manual browser inspection — the tradeoff is that the Tab order produced by Playwright's keyboard simulation exactly matches the browser's natural tab sequence only when no `tabindex` attribute overrides exist on the page; pages that use positive `tabindex` values (e.g., `tabindex="2"`) to reorder focus will produce a focus sequence in the keyboard session that differs from what a screen reader user experiences (screen readers follow DOM order by default, ignoring positive tabindex for most reading modes); after the keyboard charter, run a secondary `page.evaluate()` pass that collects all `tabindex` attribute values greater than zero and flag them as accessibility findings, since positive tabindex is an anti-pattern per WCAG 2.4.3.

---

**Pattern 501: Playwright Codegen-Assisted Charter Seed with `--save-storage` for Authenticated Session Recording** [official]

Use `playwright codegen --save-storage=auth.json <url>` to manually record an authenticated session seed, then replay the saved storage state in automated exploratory branches to start each charter branch from the exact authentication and application state captured during the manual exploration recording.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
// Usage: run 'npx playwright codegen --save-storage=tmp/recorded-session.json https://app.example.com'
// to record an interactive session. The saved state is then loaded here for automated re-exploration.

const RECORDED_SESSION = './tmp/recorded-session.json';

test.describe('Session: codegen-seeded branch exploration', () => {
  test.use({ storageState: RECORDED_SESSION });

  test('branch A: explore starting from codegen-recorded midpoint', async ({ page }) => {
    // Page is already authenticated with the exact cookies and localStorage
    // captured during the manual codegen session.
    await page.goto('/dashboard');

    // Verify we are in the expected recorded state.
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /dashboard/i })).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('user-avatar')).toBeVisible();

    // Begin automated exploration from this state.
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: /analytics/i }).click();
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    await test.info().attach('screenshot:analytics-from-seed', {
      body: await page.screenshot({ fullPage: true }),
      contentType: 'image/png',
    });

    const ariaTree = await page.ariaSnapshot();
    await test.info().attach('aria-snapshot:analytics-initial', {
      body: Buffer.from(ariaTree),
      contentType: 'text/plain',
    });
  });

  test('branch B: explore notification centre from same recorded state', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/notifications');
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /notifications/i })).toBeVisible();
    const count = await page.getByTestId('unread-badge').textContent().catch(() => '0');
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: `unread-count:${count}` });
    await page.screenshot({ path: 'session-artefacts/notifications-from-seed.png' });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `playwright codegen --save-storage` to capture an authenticated session state during manual exploration and then loading it in automated branches gives each charter branch an identical, replay-stable starting point that preserves the exact cookies, localStorage, and session tokens recorded during a real manual session — the tradeoff is that the saved storage state is a point-in-time snapshot and session tokens commonly have short TTLs (15–60 minutes); if the automated exploratory suite takes longer than the token TTL to execute, later branches will encounter 401/403 redirects and silently start from the login page rather than the expected application state, making branch A pass while branch B fails for unrelated reasons; add an assertion in each branch's first `test` block that verifies the authenticated landing page heading is visible before proceeding with the charter, and set a `test.setTimeout()` guard calibrated to the shortest token TTL so that stale-token failures surface as timeout errors rather than mysterious assertion failures.

---

**Pattern 502: `page.coverage` + Istanbul-Compatible Coverage Reporting for Code-Area Gap Analysis in Exploratory Sessions** [official]

Enable Playwright's built-in JavaScript and CSS coverage instrumentation during an exploratory session and export the coverage data in Istanbul V8 format, then overlay it with the application's source map to identify which code areas were never exercised during the session charter.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

test('session: checkout flow coverage gap analysis', async ({ page }) => {
  // Start both JS and CSS coverage before navigation.
  await Promise.all([
    page.coverage.startJSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false }),
    page.coverage.startCSSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false }),
  ]);

  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Charter the main branches of the checkout flow.
  await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('12/28');
  await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).fill('123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Stop coverage and collect results.
  const [jsCoverage, cssCoverage] = await Promise.all([
    page.coverage.stopJSCoverage(),
    page.coverage.stopCSSCoverage(),
  ]);

  // Compute basic coverage metrics for the session debrief.
  const coverageReport = jsCoverage.map((entry) => {
    const totalBytes = entry.text.length;
    const coveredBytes = entry.ranges.reduce((sum, range) => sum + (range.end - range.start), 0);
    const pct = totalBytes > 0 ? ((coveredBytes / totalBytes) * 100).toFixed(1) : '0.0';
    return { url: entry.url, totalBytes, coveredBytes, coveragePct: `${pct}%` };
  });

  const outDir = path.join('session-artefacts', 'coverage');
  fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(
    path.join(outDir, 'js-coverage.json'),
    JSON.stringify(coverageReport, null, 2)
  );

  await test.info().attach('js-coverage-summary', {
    body: JSON.stringify(coverageReport, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });

  // Flag files with very low coverage as potential unexplored charters.
  const lowCoverage = coverageReport.filter(
    e => parseFloat(e.coveragePct) < 10 && e.totalBytes > 2000
  );
  if (lowCoverage.length > 0) {
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'medium-risk',
      value: `Low-coverage files (potential unexplored charters): ${lowCoverage.map(e => e.url).join(', ')}`,
    });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.coverage.startJSCoverage()` with `resetOnNavigation: false` accumulates coverage data across all SPA route changes within the session, giving a holistic picture of which JavaScript code paths were exercised during the entire charter rather than just the landing page — the tradeoff is that V8 coverage reports byte-range coverage of the transpiled/minified bundle, not of original TypeScript source lines; without a source-map processing step (using tools like `istanbul-lib-coverage` + `v8-to-istanbul`) the coverage data is expressed as byte offsets in minified code that is impossible to review manually; the raw `jsCoverage` output is still useful for relative comparisons between session branches (which bundle files were touched more or less), but deriving actionable "which feature code was not exercised" conclusions requires the full source-map pipeline to be configured in the project.

---

### Community Gotchas

**G80: `page.addLocatorHandler()` handlers registered for a locator that matches multiple elements simultaneously only dismiss the first matched element — if two cookie banners or two overlays are present in the DOM at the same time, the handler fires once, dismisses the first, and then the second remains blocking subsequent actions.**
Why this matters: A team testing a multi-step wizard found that the wizard injected both a "terms and conditions" modal and a "promotional offer" popup simultaneously on first load. The registered `addLocatorHandler` for `getByRole('dialog')` fired once, dismissed the terms modal, and then Playwright proceeded to the next action — which was immediately blocked by the still-visible promotional popup. Because the handler did not fire again (the terms modal was gone, but the promotional popup matched a different selector), the team spent three hours debugging what appeared to be a random "element is not visible" flake before realising that two overlays were being rendered at once.
Fix: Register separate `addLocatorHandler` calls for every distinct overlay type using the most specific possible locator (prefer `getByRole('dialog', { name: /terms/i })` over `getByRole('dialog')`). After each handler's dismiss click, add `await page.waitForSelector('[role="dialog"]', { state: 'hidden', timeout: 3000 }).catch(() => {})` to confirm the specific dialog closed before allowing Playwright to proceed. If the exact overlay names are unknown in advance, use a polling helper that calls `page.getByRole('dialog').all()` and dismisses each visible dialog in sequence.

---

**G81: `page.coverage.startJSCoverage()` must be called before the first navigation on the page — calling it after `page.goto()` returns means the initial page-load scripts have already executed and their coverage ranges will report as fully covered (all bytes executed) regardless of which code paths were actually taken, producing misleading 100% coverage for bootstrap modules.**
Why this matters: A team integrating coverage gap analysis into their exploratory session pipeline called `page.goto('/checkout')` first, waited for `networkidle`, then called `page.coverage.startJSCoverage()`. Their coverage report showed every JavaScript bundle at or near 100% coverage for the initial page load, making it appear that the session had thoroughly exercised all code paths. The root cause is that V8 coverage instrumentation only tracks execution ranges from the moment it is activated; any script that completed execution before `startJSCoverage()` was called has all its byte ranges marked as "executed" by default (since V8 only records ranges for code that runs after instrumentation begins, and the pre-instrumentation execution count is treated as non-zero). The team incorrectly concluded their exploratory sessions had no gaps and stopped adding new branches.
Fix: Always call `page.coverage.startJSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false })` and `page.coverage.startCSSCoverage()` before the first `page.goto()` call. If using fixtures, start coverage in the fixture's setup phase before `await use(page)` is called, or use `page.addInitScript` to ensure the coverage instrumentation is active during the very first script execution on the page.

---

**G82: `page.waitForResponse()` with a URL glob pattern matches the first response whose URL fits the glob regardless of HTTP method — if your exploratory session has both a GET and a POST to the same API endpoint (e.g., `/api/cart` for reading and for updating), `waitForResponse('**/api/cart')` may resolve on the GET response that fires first, and the test proceeds before the POST mutation response arrives, causing subsequent assertions to read pre-mutation state.**
Why this matters: A team chartering the add-to-cart flow used `await page.waitForResponse('**/api/cart')` after clicking "Add to Cart". The click triggered a POST `/api/cart` mutation request, but there was also a background GET `/api/cart` polling call firing every 10 seconds to keep the cart badge count fresh. On fast machines the polling GET arrived before the POST response, so `waitForResponse` resolved immediately on the GET, the assertion ran before the POST mutation was committed, and the cart count showed the pre-add value. The test passed intermittently depending on whether the GET poll happened to fire within the waitForResponse window.
Fix: Always pass a predicate function to `waitForResponse` that filters on both URL and HTTP method: `page.waitForResponse(r => r.url().includes('/api/cart') && r.request().method() === 'POST')`. For exploratory sessions where multiple API calls to the same endpoint are expected, use `page.on('response', handler)` to accumulate all matching responses into an array and assert on the full set after `waitForLoadState('networkidle')`.

---

**G83: `context.routeFromHAR()` with `update: false` in replay mode silently passes through requests that have no matching HAR entry to the real network by default — if your exploratory session navigates to a URL that was not captured during the recording pass, the request hits the live API and may return different data than expected, causing the "offline" replay session to depend on live network state without any warning.**
Why this matters: A team recorded a HAR file for their product listing page, then added a new feature that introduced a `/api/recommendations` endpoint after the HAR was recorded. When running the exploratory session in offline replay mode, the recommendations request found no HAR match and fell back to the live API. On developer machines connected to the internet this worked transparently, but in the CI environment with no outbound internet access the request failed with a network error, causing the recommendations component to render an error state. The team could not reproduce the CI failure locally because their local replay sessions quietly used the live API as a fallback.
Fix: Always set `{ notFound: 'abort' }` in `context.routeFromHAR()` for exploratory sessions that must be fully offline: `await context.routeFromHAR(HAR_PATH, { url: '**/api/**', notFound: 'abort' })`. This converts unmatched requests into explicit network errors that cause immediate, visible test failures rather than silent live-API fallback. Run the HAR update pass (`update: true`) after every feature that introduces new API endpoints to keep the recorded session in sync.

---

**G84: `test.info().annotations.push()` calls made inside `test.step()` are visible in the final test result but the Playwright JUnit XML reporter does not include annotations in its `<testcase>` elements — CI systems that parse JUnit XML for pass/fail categorisation and bug tagging will silently discard all annotation data, meaning bug-found and risk-rating annotations are present in the HTML report but absent from ticket-linking integrations.**
Why this matters: A team used `test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'bug-found', value: 'P1: ...' })` inside exploratory test sessions and built a post-CI script that parsed the JUnit XML output to automatically create Jira tickets for every `bug-found` annotation. After deploying the pipeline, no tickets were ever created. Investigation revealed that the Playwright JUnit reporter's `<testcase>` XML elements contain `<failure>` and `<skipped>` child nodes but no annotation nodes; the annotation data only appears in the `test-results.json` file and the HTML report. The JUnit XML format has no standard field for test annotations, so Playwright omits them from JUnit output entirely.
Fix: Write the post-CI ticket-creation script to parse `test-results.json` (which does include the `annotations` array per test result) rather than the JUnit XML. The `test-results.json` file is always written to the project root by Playwright unless overridden by `outputDir`. Alternatively, in the `globalTeardown` script, read `test-results.json`, filter for results with `bug-found` annotations, and call your Jira API directly, using `testResult.annotations.filter(a => a.type === 'bug-found')` to extract the structured finding data.
