## Cycle 63 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 503: `page.clock.install()` + `page.clock.fastForward()` — Time-Sensitive UI State Charter**

Use `page.clock.install()` before the first navigation to take over all browser time primitives, then use `page.clock.fastForward()` to drive the application through time-dependent states (session expiry warnings, countdown timers, scheduled banners) without waiting for real wall-clock time.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: inactivity-timeout warning and auto-logout flow', async ({ page }) => {
  // Install clock BEFORE first navigation — required constraint.
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-05-14T09:00:00Z') });

  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /dashboard/i })).toBeVisible();

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter',
    value: 'Explore: inactivity warning at 25 min, forced logout at 30 min',
  });

  // Advance 25 minutes — expect warning modal to appear.
  await page.clock.fastForward('25:00');
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /session expiring/i }))
    .toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });
  await test.info().attach('screenshot:inactivity-warning', {
    body: await page.screenshot({ fullPage: true }),
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });

  // Advance the remaining 5 minutes — expect redirect to login.
  await page.clock.fastForward('05:00');
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login/);
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'session-outcome',
    value: 'auto-logout confirmed after 30 min inactivity',
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.clock.install()` replaces all timer primitives globally in the browser context including `requestAnimationFrame`, `performance.now()`, and `Event.timeStamp` — this gives precise deterministic control over every scheduled timer in the application without any real waiting, making inactivity-timeout and expiry-banner charters complete in milliseconds instead of minutes; the tradeoff is that some animation libraries (GSAP, Framer Motion) and WebGL renderers use `performance.now()` internally for frame interpolation and may produce visually corrupted or frozen renders when clock is under test control, meaning screenshot artefacts captured mid-`fastForward()` may show UI in a state that never occurs in production and cannot be used as reliable visual regression baselines.

---

**Pattern 504: `page.clock.pauseAt()` + `page.clock.runFor()` — Granular Interval Tick Charter**

Pause the clock at a specific timestamp then step forward in fine-grained increments using `runFor()` to explore how the application behaves at precise interval boundaries — useful for chartering debounce logic, polling intervals, and rate-limit reset windows.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: debounce search input fires at exactly 300 ms boundary', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') });
  await page.goto('/search');

  const apiRequests: string[] = [];
  page.on('request', req => {
    if (req.url().includes('/api/search')) apiRequests.push(req.url());
  });

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter',
    value: 'Explore: search debounce boundary at 300 ms — does it fire early?',
  });

  await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill('playwright');
  // Pause so we can tick manually.
  await page.clock.pauseAt(new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z'));

  // Tick 299 ms — request should NOT fire yet.
  await page.clock.runFor(299);
  expect(apiRequests).toHaveLength(0);

  // Tick 1 more ms — request should fire at exactly 300 ms.
  await page.clock.runFor(1);
  await page.waitForTimeout(50); // let microtask queue flush
  expect(apiRequests.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(1);
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'session-outcome',
    value: `debounce fired after tick: requestCount=${apiRequests.length}`,
  });
  await test.info().attach('screenshot:debounce-fired', {
    body: await page.screenshot(),
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.clock.runFor()` with millisecond-level precision exposes exactly when debounce timers, polling callbacks, and retry backoff handlers fire relative to a frozen time baseline, making timing-boundary bugs reproducible in a deterministic test rather than relying on statistical flake from wall-clock timing — the tradeoff is that `page.waitForTimeout()` itself is subject to the mocked clock when clock is installed, so a call like `page.waitForTimeout(50)` after `runFor()` will return immediately without advancing real time; any real async side-effects (microtasks, network responses) that need real-time settling between clock ticks must be awaited via `page.waitForResponse()` or `page.waitForFunction()` predicates rather than `waitForTimeout()` sleeps.

---

**Pattern 505: `page.clock.setFixedTime()` — Date-Dependent Feature Branch Charter**

Set a fixed wall-clock time before navigating to exercise date-gated features, seasonal promotions, and "available from" content without needing to manipulate server-side feature flags or database date records.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const DATE_SCENARIOS = [
  { label: 'before-promo', date: '2026-04-30T23:59:59Z', expectBanner: false },
  { label: 'promo-first-day', date: '2026-05-01T00:00:01Z', expectBanner: true },
  { label: 'promo-last-day', date: '2026-05-31T23:59:00Z', expectBanner: true },
  { label: 'after-promo', date: '2026-06-01T00:00:01Z', expectBanner: false },
];

for (const scenario of DATE_SCENARIOS) {
  test(`session: promo-banner visibility — ${scenario.label}`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date(scenario.date));
    await page.goto('/home');

    const banner = page.getByTestId('promo-banner');
    if (scenario.expectBanner) {
      await expect(banner).toBeVisible();
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: `banner visible at ${scenario.date}` });
    } else {
      await expect(banner).not.toBeVisible();
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: `banner hidden at ${scenario.date}` });
    }
    await test.info().attach(`screenshot:${scenario.label}`, {
      body: await page.screenshot({ fullPage: true }),
      contentType: 'image/png',
    });
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: `page.clock.setFixedTime()` alters only the return value of `Date.now()` and `new Date()` in the browser process without pausing or replacing timer callbacks, so ongoing `setInterval` and `setTimeout` handlers still fire on real wall-clock schedule — this means date-display components that read `new Date()` once on mount will reflect the fixed time while real-timer-driven components (countdown widgets that call `Date.now()` inside a `setInterval`) will compute the duration relative to the fixed time but still fire their callbacks on the real clock, which can produce confusing mixed-time UI states where some elements show the mocked date and others show current real-elapsed durations.

---

**Pattern 506: `context.routeFromHAR()` with `update: false` + `notFound: 'abort'` — Strict Offline Session Replay**

Record a HAR during a manual exploratory session then replay it with `notFound: 'abort'` to ensure the automated re-exploration session is fully isolated from the live network, converting any unmatched requests into explicit test failures rather than silent live-API fallback.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as path from 'path';

const HAR_PATH = path.join(__dirname, 'fixtures', 'checkout-session.har');

test('session: offline-replay checkout flow charter', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext();

  // Strict mode: any request not in HAR is aborted, never sent to live network.
  await context.routeFromHAR(HAR_PATH, {
    url: '**/api/**',
    notFound: 'abort',
    update: false,
  });

  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /checkout/i })).toBeVisible();

  await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('12/28');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'session-outcome',
    value: 'HAR replay: checkout completed with no live-network fallback',
  });
  await test.info().attach('screenshot:offline-checkout', {
    body: await page.screenshot({ fullPage: true }),
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });
  await context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: Routing all API traffic through a recorded HAR with `notFound: 'abort'` eliminates network flakiness and environment dependencies from exploratory replay sessions, making them executable in CI without internet access and ensuring the application under exploration is driven by deterministic canned responses rather than live server state — the tradeoff is that the HAR file becomes a maintenance artifact that must be re-recorded whenever the API contract changes; `context.routeFromHAR()` matches requests by URL and HTTP method but does not match on request body content by default, so if your application sends subtly different POST body payloads under different user-interaction paths, the HAR may return the same canned response for all variants, masking payload-specific API validation bugs that would surface against a real server.

---

**Pattern 507: `context.routeFromHAR({ update: true })` — Living HAR Update Pass**

Run a dedicated HAR update pass with `update: true` after each sprint to refresh the recorded network interactions, then commit the updated HAR to version control as a reproducible network fixture for offline exploratory sessions.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as path from 'path';

const HAR_PATH = path.join(__dirname, 'fixtures', 'product-listing-session.har');
// Set UPDATE_HAR=true in CI to refresh the HAR; omit for replay-only runs.
const IS_UPDATE_PASS = process.env.UPDATE_HAR === 'true';

test('session: HAR update pass — product listing flow', async ({ browser }) => {
  const context = await browser.newContext();

  await context.routeFromHAR(HAR_PATH, {
    url: '**/api/**',
    update: IS_UPDATE_PASS,
    notFound: IS_UPDATE_PASS ? 'fallthrough' : 'abort',
  });

  const page = await context.newPage();
  await page.goto('/products');
  await expect(page.getByRole('list', { name: /product results/i })).toBeVisible();

  // Charter main interaction paths to ensure all API calls are captured in the HAR.
  await page.getByRole('combobox', { name: /sort/i }).selectOption('price-asc');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /filter/i }).click();
  await page.getByLabel(/category/i).check();
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: IS_UPDATE_PASS ? 'har-updated' : 'session-outcome',
    value: IS_UPDATE_PASS ? `HAR refreshed at ${HAR_PATH}` : 'offline replay completed',
  });
  await context.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `update: true` on a scheduled CI job keeps the HAR file current with evolving API contracts without requiring manual re-recording, and committing the HAR to version control gives the team a versioned snapshot of the expected network interactions for every sprint — the tradeoff is that running the update pass requires a live network connection to the target API environment, and if the update CI job runs against a staging environment whose data changes between runs (e.g., dynamic product IDs, user-specific session tokens), the captured HAR responses will include environment-specific data that may cause exploratory replay sessions on a different environment (or after a database reset) to present the wrong application state when replayed.

---

**Pattern 508: `page.addInitScript()` — Deterministic Random and Crypto Seeding**

Inject a `page.addInitScript()` script before each exploratory session branch to replace `Math.random()` and `crypto.getRandomValues()` with deterministic pseudo-random implementations, ensuring that any application behaviour that depends on client-side randomness is reproducible across session replay runs.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// A simple seedable LCG for deterministic Math.random replacement.
const SEED_SCRIPT = `
  (function () {
    let seed = 42;
    const lcg = () => {
      seed = (seed * 1664525 + 1013904223) & 0xffffffff;
      return (seed >>> 0) / 0x100000000;
    };
    Object.defineProperty(Math, 'random', { value: lcg, configurable: true });
    window.__randomSeed = 42;
  })();
`;

test('session: seeded-random branch — A/B variant determinism', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.addInitScript(SEED_SCRIPT);
  await page.goto('/home');

  // Record which A/B variant the seeded random produced.
  const variant = await page.evaluate(() => (window as any).__abVariant ?? 'none');
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter',
    value: `A/B variant with seed=42: ${variant}`,
  });

  await test.info().attach('screenshot:ab-variant-seeded', {
    body: await page.screenshot({ fullPage: true }),
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });

  // Re-run the same page load and confirm the same variant is selected.
  await page.reload();
  const variantReplay = await page.evaluate(() => (window as any).__abVariant ?? 'none');
  expect(variantReplay).toBe(variant);
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'session-outcome',
    value: `A/B variant reproducible: ${variantReplay === variant}`,
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Replacing `Math.random()` via `addInitScript()` with a seeded LCG makes client-side randomness deterministic for the entire page lifetime including any third-party scripts loaded before the first user interaction, enabling reproducible A/B variant selection and random-ID generation across session replays — the tradeoff is that `page.addInitScript()` evaluation order relative to other init scripts registered at the `browserContext` level is not guaranteed by Playwright; if the application's bundle itself calls `Math.random()` during module initialization before the LCG replacement script has fully executed, those early calls will use the native unseeded random, meaning only post-initialization randomness is deterministic; to guarantee coverage of module-level random calls, the seed script must be delivered as the first script on the page using `context.addInitScript()` rather than `page.addInitScript()`.

---

**Pattern 509: `page.exposeFunction()` — Host-Side State Spy During Exploratory Navigation**

Expose a Node.js callback function to the browser page via `page.exposeFunction()` so that client-side application code can report internal state transitions, routing events, and feature flag evaluations back to the test runner in real time, creating a live telemetry stream during exploratory navigation.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface StateEvent { type: string; payload: unknown; timestamp: number }

test('session: client-state telemetry during checkout charter', async ({ page }) => {
  const events: StateEvent[] = [];

  // Expose a function that application code can call via window.__reportState().
  await page.exposeFunction('__reportState', (event: StateEvent) => {
    events.push({ ...event, timestamp: Date.now() });
  });

  // Inject a shim that hooks into window.history for route tracking.
  await page.addInitScript(`
    const orig = window.history.pushState.bind(window.history);
    window.history.pushState = function (...args) {
      window.__reportState && window.__reportState({ type: 'route', payload: args[2], timestamp: 0 });
      return orig(...args);
    };
  `);

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'session-outcome',
    value: `client-state events captured: ${events.length}`,
  });
  await test.info().attach('client-state-events', {
    body: JSON.stringify(events, null, 2),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });
  expect(events.some(e => e.type === 'route' && String(e.payload).includes('confirmation'))).toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.exposeFunction()` creates a persistent bridge from the browser context to the Node.js test runner that survives page navigations, enabling the exploration session to collect a continuous stream of client-side application events (route changes, Redux actions, feature-flag evaluations) without instrumenting the application source code — the tradeoff is that the exposed function is a global on the `window` object and any third-party script loaded on the page can call it, meaning adversarial or buggy ad/analytics scripts could inject spurious events into the telemetry stream; additionally, since the function call crosses the browser-Node boundary synchronously from the page's perspective but is handled asynchronously in Node, high-frequency event emitters (scroll handlers, animation frame callbacks) can produce thousands of IPC calls per second and noticeably degrade page rendering performance during the exploratory session.

---

**Pattern 510: `page.coverage.startJSCoverage({ reportAnonymousScripts: true })` — Dynamic Script Coverage in SPAs**

Enable anonymous script reporting to capture coverage data for dynamically evaluated scripts (`eval()`, `new Function()`, inline `<script>` tags without a `src` attribute) that would otherwise be silently excluded from the coverage report, then use the coverage data to identify dynamically injected code paths that were never executed during the charter.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

test('session: dynamic-script coverage — widget lazy-eval paths', async ({ page }) => {
  await Promise.all([
    page.coverage.startJSCoverage({
      resetOnNavigation: false,
      reportAnonymousScripts: true,
    }),
    page.coverage.startCSSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false }),
  ]);

  await page.goto('/widgets');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /load chart widget/i }).click();
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const [jsCoverage] = await Promise.all([
    page.coverage.stopJSCoverage(),
    page.coverage.stopCSSCoverage(),
  ]);

  const dynamicScripts = jsCoverage.filter(entry => !entry.url || entry.url.startsWith('__playwright'));
  const uncoveredDynamic = dynamicScripts.filter(entry => {
    const totalBytes = entry.source?.length ?? 0;
    const coveredBytes = entry.functions.reduce((sum, fn) =>
      sum + fn.ranges.filter(r => r.count > 0).reduce((s, r) => s + (r.endOffset - r.startOffset), 0), 0);
    return totalBytes > 500 && coveredBytes / totalBytes < 0.1;
  });

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'session-outcome',
    value: `dynamic scripts: total=${dynamicScripts.length} low-coverage=${uncoveredDynamic.length}`,
  });
  fs.mkdirSync('session-artefacts', { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(
    path.join('session-artefacts', 'dynamic-coverage.json'),
    JSON.stringify(uncoveredDynamic.map(e => ({ url: e.url, sourceLength: e.source?.length })), null, 2)
  );
});
```
Tradeoff: Setting `reportAnonymousScripts: true` in `startJSCoverage()` includes dynamically evaluated scripts and inline script blocks that are typically invisible to coverage analysis, surfacing gaps in lazy-loaded widget initialization code and `eval()`-based feature-flag evaluators that would otherwise appear as never-exercised code paths — the tradeoff is that anonymous script entries in the coverage report have no URL (they are identified only by `scriptId`), making it impossible to map coverage byte-ranges back to original source files without maintaining a side-channel map of which `eval()` call site produced which scriptId; the coverage data for anonymous scripts is also far less actionable for human review since there is no source map, and high numbers of anonymous script entries may indicate a bundler configuration that should be splitting code into named chunks rather than emitting large inline evaluations.

---

**Pattern 511: `test.info().annotations` Multi-Tier Risk Rating — Machine-Readable Session Debrief**

Establish a convention of pushing structured risk-tier annotations (`critical-risk`, `high-risk`, `medium-risk`, `low-risk`, `session-outcome`) during every exploratory charter, then parse `test-results.json` in a `globalTeardown` hook to generate an aggregated session debrief report with actionable finding counts per tier.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: payment flow risk-tiered exploration', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');

  // Charter: missing CSRF token on payment POST.
  const tokenPresent = await page.evaluate(() => {
    const meta = document.querySelector('meta[name="csrf-token"]');
    return meta !== null && meta.getAttribute('content') !== '';
  });
  if (!tokenPresent) {
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'critical-risk',
      value: 'CSRF token missing on /checkout — all POST requests unprotected',
    });
  }

  // Charter: error message leaks stack trace.
  await page.route('**/api/payment', route =>
    route.fulfill({ status: 500, body: '{"error":"Error at PaymentService.java:42"}' })
  );
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
  const errText = await page.getByRole('alert').textContent().catch(() => '');
  if (errText.includes('.java') || errText.includes('at ')) {
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'high-risk',
      value: `Server stack trace exposed in UI: "${errText.slice(0, 120)}"`,
    });
  }

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'session-outcome',
    value: `payment-flow charter complete: ${test.info().annotations.filter(a => a.type.endsWith('-risk')).length} risk findings`,
  });
  await test.info().attach('screenshot:payment-risk-charter', {
    body: await page.screenshot({ fullPage: true }),
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using a consistent annotation taxonomy (`critical-risk`, `high-risk`, `medium-risk`) across all charter tests enables the `globalTeardown` parser of `test-results.json` to aggregate finding counts by tier without requiring any manual triage step, allowing a post-CI report to automatically surface "3 critical-risk findings found this session" and route them to the on-call engineer — the tradeoff is that `test.info().annotations.push()` is additive and immutable within a test run; there is no mechanism to retract or deduplicate an annotation once pushed, so if a mitigation check later in the same test confirms a finding is a false positive, the annotation remains in the results JSON and will still be counted by the aggregation script; defensive convention requires annotators to push a corresponding `false-positive-confirmed` annotation rather than relying on the ability to remove the original finding annotation.

---

**Pattern 512: `browser.newContext()` Role-Pair Concurrency — Simultaneous Multi-Actor Charter**

Create two browser contexts representing different user roles (admin and regular user) and drive them concurrently within a single test to explore race conditions, permission boundary violations, and cross-user data leakage that only manifest when two actors interact with the same resource simultaneously.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: concurrent admin-edit + user-read race condition charter', async ({ browser }) => {
  const adminCtx = await browser.newContext({ storageState: './fixtures/admin.json' });
  const userCtx  = await browser.newContext({ storageState: './fixtures/user.json' });
  const [adminPage, userPage] = await Promise.all([
    adminCtx.newPage(),
    userCtx.newPage(),
  ]);

  // Both navigate to the same resource simultaneously.
  await Promise.all([
    adminPage.goto('/admin/articles/123/edit'),
    userPage.goto('/articles/123'),
  ]);

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter',
    value: 'Explore: concurrent edit by admin while user reads — stale read, 403, or live update?',
  });

  // Admin saves a title change while user is reading.
  await adminPage.getByLabel(/title/i).fill('Updated Title by Admin');
  await adminPage.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).click();
  await adminPage.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Check whether user page reflects the update or shows stale data.
  const userTitle = await userPage.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 }).textContent();
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: userTitle?.includes('Updated Title') ? 'low-risk' : 'medium-risk',
    value: `User saw title: "${userTitle}" after admin save — live-update: ${userTitle?.includes('Updated Title')}`,
  });

  await Promise.all([
    test.info().attach('screenshot:admin-after-save', { body: await adminPage.screenshot(), contentType: 'image/png' }),
    test.info().attach('screenshot:user-after-admin-save', { body: await userPage.screenshot(), contentType: 'image/png' }),
  ]);
  await Promise.all([adminCtx.close(), userCtx.close()]);
});
```
Tradeoff: Driving two browser contexts concurrently within a single Playwright test faithfully simulates real multi-actor usage scenarios and surfaces synchronization bugs (stale reads, optimistic-lock violations, WebSocket broadcast gaps) that would never be discovered by single-actor sequential test scripts — the tradeoff is that Playwright does not provide any built-in synchronization primitives between contexts; coordinating the exact moment each actor performs an action requires careful use of `Promise.all()`, `page.waitForResponse()`, and shared timing signals; without precise coordination, the "simultaneous" actions may be serialized by the event loop under load, making the race condition non-reproducible in low-contention CI environments even though it reliably occurs in production under concurrent user load.

---

**Pattern 513: `context.setOffline(true/false)` — Network Oscillation Resilience Charter**

Repeatedly toggle the browser context between online and offline states at application checkpoints to explore how the application handles intermittent connectivity — validating offline banners, queued mutations, sync-on-reconnect behaviour, and data consistency after a reconnect.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: offline-oscillation charter — form draft persistence', async ({ context, page }) => {
  await page.goto('/compose');
  await expect(page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /message/i })).toBeVisible();

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter',
    value: 'Explore: typed draft survives offline → online transition without loss',
  });

  // Type a draft while online.
  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /message/i }).fill('Draft message typed before going offline');
  await context.setOffline(true);

  // Verify offline indicator appears.
  await expect(page.getByText(/offline/i)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });
  await test.info().attach('screenshot:offline-state', {
    body: await page.screenshot(),
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });

  // Attempt a submit while offline.
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /send/i }).click();
  const queuedNotice = page.getByText(/queued|will send when online/i);
  const submitError  = page.getByRole('alert');

  if (await queuedNotice.isVisible()) {
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'low-risk', value: 'offline submit correctly queued' });
  } else if (await submitError.isVisible()) {
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'medium-risk', value: 'offline submit showed error without queue' });
  } else {
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'high-risk', value: 'offline submit gave no feedback to user' });
  }

  // Restore network and verify draft sends or persists.
  await context.setOffline(false);
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  const draftText = await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /message/i }).inputValue();
  expect(draftText).toBe('Draft message typed before going offline');
});
```
Tradeoff: `context.setOffline(true)` cuts all network traffic for the entire browser context at the Chromium network stack level without requiring any application-level service worker or mock, providing a realistic offline simulation that affects all resources (API calls, WebSocket frames, CDN assets) simultaneously — the tradeoff is that `setOffline` is a blunt instrument: it cannot simulate partial connectivity (e.g., high latency but not full disconnection, or only API calls failing while static assets remain cached), and it cannot simulate a flapping connection that drops individual packets; for latency and partial-failure exploration, `context.setExtraHTTPHeaders()` combined with `page.route()` abort logic provides more surgical control than the boolean online/offline toggle.

---

**Pattern 514: `page.keyboard.press()` Sequential Navigation Charter — Focus Order Verification**

Drive the entire application interaction using only keyboard events via `page.keyboard.press()` and `page.keyboard.type()` to charter the focus order, keyboard trap patterns, and modal escape behaviour without using any mouse actions, surfacing accessibility gaps that visual regression tests cannot detect.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: keyboard-only checkout charter — focus order and trap detection', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter',
    value: 'Explore: keyboard-only navigation through entire checkout — focus traps, skip links, modal escape',
  });

  const focusOrder: string[] = [];
  // Track which elements receive focus during Tab traversal.
  await page.exposeFunction('__trackFocus', (label: string) => { focusOrder.push(label); });
  await page.addInitScript(`
    document.addEventListener('focusin', e => {
      const el = e.target;
      const label = el.getAttribute('aria-label') || el.getAttribute('name') || el.tagName;
      window.__trackFocus && window.__trackFocus(label);
    }, true);
  `);
  await page.reload(); // Re-navigate to apply the init script.

  // Tab through form fields and interact using keyboard only.
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  await page.keyboard.type('4111111111111111'); // Card number field.
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  await page.keyboard.type('12/28');            // Expiry.
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  await page.keyboard.type('123');              // CVV.
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  await page.keyboard.press('Enter');           // Submit.
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'session-outcome',
    value: `focus-order: ${focusOrder.join(' -> ')}`,
  });
  await test.info().attach('focus-order-log', {
    body: Buffer.from(focusOrder.join('\n')),
    contentType: 'text/plain',
  });

  // Check for focus traps: if any element appears more than 3 times in the focus order, flag it.
  const counts = focusOrder.reduce<Record<string, number>>((acc, el) => {
    acc[el] = (acc[el] ?? 0) + 1; return acc;
  }, {});
  const traps = Object.entries(counts).filter(([, n]) => n > 3);
  if (traps.length > 0) {
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'high-risk', value: `Potential focus trap: ${JSON.stringify(traps)}` });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.keyboard.press()` exclusively for an entire charter run confirms that the application is fully operable without a pointing device, and combining it with a `focusin` listener exposed via `exposeFunction()` produces a focus-order log that documents the exact Tab sequence as a session artefact — the tradeoff is that `page.keyboard.press('Tab')` in Playwright dispatches a synthetic keyboard event that bypasses the browser's native tab-stop algorithm for certain edge cases (e.g., tabindex on SVG elements, shadow DOM tab delegation), meaning the synthetic focus order may differ from the order a real user would experience with a physical keyboard in some browsers; always cross-validate keyboard charter findings against a real browser session before filing accessibility bugs.

---

**Pattern 515: `page.ariaSnapshot()` Baseline Diff — Structural Regression Detection in Exploratory Sessions**

Capture `page.ariaSnapshot()` at the start and end of each exploratory charter branch and diff the two strings to detect structural accessibility-tree mutations that are invisible to screenshot comparisons — surfacing added, removed, or reordered ARIA roles without any pre-configured snapshot files.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

function diffAriaLines(before: string, after: string): string[] {
  const beforeLines = new Set(before.split('\n').map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean));
  const afterLines  = new Set(after.split('\n').map(l => l.trim()).filter(Boolean));
  const removed = [...beforeLines].filter(l => !afterLines.has(l)).map(l => `- ${l}`);
  const added   = [...afterLines].filter(l => !beforeLines.has(l)).map(l => `+ ${l}`);
  return [...removed, ...added];
}

test('session: aria-snapshot structural diff — product filter charter', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const beforeAria = await page.ariaSnapshot();
  await test.info().attach('aria-snapshot:before-filter', {
    body: Buffer.from(beforeAria),
    contentType: 'text/plain',
  });

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter', value: 'Explore: filter panel opens and adds results region to ARIA tree' });

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /filter/i }).click();
  await page.getByLabel(/category/i).check();
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const afterAria = await page.ariaSnapshot();
  const diff = diffAriaLines(beforeAria, afterAria);

  if (diff.length === 0) {
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'medium-risk', value: 'Filter action produced no ARIA-tree changes — screen-reader experience may be static' });
  } else {
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: `ARIA diff lines: ${diff.length}` });
  }
  await test.info().attach('aria-snapshot:diff', {
    body: Buffer.from(diff.join('\n')),
    contentType: 'text/plain',
  });
  await test.info().attach('aria-snapshot:after-filter', {
    body: Buffer.from(afterAria),
    contentType: 'text/plain',
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Diffing `page.ariaSnapshot()` before and after a charter interaction produces a concise, text-diffable record of every ARIA role, label, and state change that occurred during the exploration step, making structural accessibility regressions detectable without any screenshot comparison tooling or pre-committed snapshot files — the tradeoff is that `page.ariaSnapshot()` reflects the computed accessibility tree as Chromium reports it, which applies ARIA attribute inheritance, presentation role suppression, and landmark merging rules that differ between browsers; a diff that shows an added `region` landmark on Chromium may not appear on Firefox or Safari if those engines compute the accessibility tree differently, so `ariaSnapshot` diffs are useful for within-Chromium regression detection but cannot be used as cross-browser accessibility conformance evidence.

---

**Pattern 516: `test.step()` Charter Phase Segmentation — Structured Session Timeline**

Wrap each logical exploration phase of a charter in a named `test.step()` call to create a hierarchical timeline of session activities in the Playwright HTML report, making it easy to pinpoint which charter phase produced a finding without reading through flat console logs.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('session: structured-step charter — user onboarding flow', async ({ page }) => {
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter',
    value: 'Explore: onboarding wizard — happy path, skip behaviour, and back-navigation state',
  });

  await test.step('Phase 1: Land on onboarding start', async () => {
    await page.goto('/onboarding');
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /welcome/i })).toBeVisible();
    await test.info().attach('screenshot:onboarding-start', {
      body: await page.screenshot(),
      contentType: 'image/png',
    });
  });

  await test.step('Phase 2: Complete step 1 — profile setup', async () => {
    await page.getByLabel(/full name/i).fill('Exploratory Tester');
    await page.getByLabel(/role/i).selectOption('engineer');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /preferences/i })).toBeVisible();
  });

  await test.step('Phase 3: Navigate back and verify state preservation', async () => {
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /back/i }).click();
    const name = await page.getByLabel(/full name/i).inputValue();
    if (name !== 'Exploratory Tester') {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'high-risk', value: 'Back navigation clears step-1 form data' });
    } else {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: 'Back navigation preserves form state' });
    }
  });

  await test.step('Phase 4: Skip optional preferences step', async () => {
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next/i }).click(); // re-advance to step 2
    const skipBtn = page.getByRole('button', { name: /skip/i });
    if (await skipBtn.isVisible()) {
      await skipBtn.click();
      await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /you.re all set/i })).toBeVisible();
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: 'skip button present and functional' });
    } else {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'medium-risk', value: 'no skip option on optional preferences step' });
    }
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Wrapping charter phases in `test.step()` calls creates a collapsible, labelled timeline in the Playwright HTML report that maps directly to the charter's exploration structure, making it trivial to correlate a failure or finding with the specific phase that produced it — the tradeoff is that `test.step()` introduces a promise boundary that can interact unexpectedly with `page.on()` event listeners and `page.waitForEvent()` calls; if a navigation or response event fires between the `await test.step()` setup and the `async` callback's first `await`, the event may be missed because the listener has not yet been registered inside the step closure; always register persistent listeners (`page.on('response', ...)`) outside step boundaries before the first navigation.

---

**Pattern 517: `context.tracing.start()` + `context.tracing.stop()` — On-Demand Charter Trace Capture**

Programmatically start and stop Playwright tracing around specific charter phases rather than relying on the global `trace: 'on-first-retry'` config, capturing dense artefact packages (screenshots, DOM snapshots, network logs) only for the highest-risk exploration branches where the trace overhead is justified.

```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

test('session: high-risk payment branch — on-demand trace capture', async ({ context, page }) => {
  // Only start tracing for the high-risk branch to avoid overhead on routine charters.
  await context.tracing.start({
    screenshots: true,
    snapshots: true,
    sources: true,
    title: 'payment-failure-branch-charter',
  });

  try {
    await page.goto('/checkout');
    await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4000000000000002'); // Card that triggers decline.
    await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('12/28');
    await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).fill('123');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();

    const declined = page.getByRole('alert', { name: /declined/i });
    const confirmed = page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i });

    if (await declined.isVisible({ timeout: 5000 })) {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: 'card-decline handled with user-visible error' });
    } else if (await confirmed.isVisible({ timeout: 5000 })) {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'critical-risk', value: 'declined card reached order-confirmed state — payment guard bypass' });
    } else {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'high-risk', value: 'card-decline produced no visible feedback' });
    }
  } finally {
    fs.mkdirSync('session-artefacts', { recursive: true });
    const tracePath = path.join('session-artefacts', 'payment-decline-charter.zip');
    await context.tracing.stop({ path: tracePath });
    await test.info().attach('charter-trace', {
      body: fs.readFileSync(tracePath),
      contentType: 'application/zip',
    });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Calling `context.tracing.start()` and `context.tracing.stop()` programmatically within specific high-risk charter branches produces a complete Playwright trace (DOM snapshots, network HAR, console logs, screenshots at each action) for exactly those branches without the overhead of tracing every exploratory test in the suite — the tradeoff is that `context.tracing.start()` cannot be called more than once per context without calling `stop()` first; if a previous test in the same context left tracing running (e.g., due to an unhandled exception before the `stop()` call), subsequent `start()` calls will throw, silently aborting trace capture; always wrap `tracing.stop()` in a `try/finally` block and check context state if reusing contexts across tests, or use a fresh context per high-risk charter branch to avoid state leakage.

---

### Community Gotchas

**G85: `page.clock.fastForward()` does not advance `Date.now()` for code running inside Web Workers — timers and `Date` calls within a Worker thread continue to use real system time even when the main page clock is fully under Playwright control.**
Why this matters: A team chartering a session-expiry flow used `page.clock.install()` and `page.clock.fastForward('30:00')` to simulate 30 minutes of inactivity and trigger the expected logout redirect. The main-thread inactivity timer fired correctly and the UI showed the "Session expired" modal, but the logout was never actually executed because the application delegated the server-side token revocation call to a shared Web Worker that maintained its own 30-minute countdown using `Date.now()` directly. Since the Worker's `Date.now()` was not mocked, the Worker's countdown had only advanced by the real elapsed test time (roughly 200 ms), so it never triggered the logout API call. The session-expiry flow appeared to pass — the modal was visible — but the token remained valid on the server and subsequent authenticated requests succeeded, leaving a security gap undiscovered until a penetration test.
Fix: For applications that use Web Workers for security-critical timer logic, supplement `page.clock.install()` with a `page.addInitScript()` that patches the `Worker` constructor to inject a mocked clock channel into the Worker context, or use `page.evaluate()` to dispatch a `MessageChannel` message to the Worker telling it to advance its own internal countdown. Document this Worker-clock gap as a known limitation in the charter and add a separate charter branch that uses real wall-clock time (without `page.clock`) to validate the Worker-side logout path.

---

**G86: `page.addInitScript()` called after `page.goto()` has been awaited has no effect on the current page — the script is only evaluated on the next navigation, so calling `addInitScript()` post-navigation to patch a global is a silent no-op that leaves the intended mock absent without any warning or error.**
Why this matters: A developer writing a charter for A/B variant determinism called `page.goto('/home')`, waited for the page to load, then called `page.addInitScript(seedScript)` intending to make the next interaction use the seeded random. The `addInitScript` call returned without error, but the seed script never executed because the page was already past its initialization phase. Subsequent interactions on the same page used native `Math.random()`, meaning A/B variant assignments were non-deterministic and the charter produced different variant paths on every run. The developer spent considerable time adding logging to the seed script before realising the script was never called — there is no Playwright API to confirm which init scripts have actually executed on the current page.
Fix: Always call `page.addInitScript()` before the first `page.goto()` or before `page.reload()`. If the target page is already loaded (e.g., in an `afterEach` cleanup hook), trigger a reload after registering the script: `await page.addInitScript(script); await page.reload()`. For scripts that must persist across multiple navigations within a session, use `context.addInitScript()` instead, which registers the script for every new page created by the context and every subsequent navigation.

---

**G87: `context.routeFromHAR()` only intercepts requests made through Playwright's HTTP network stack — WebSocket connections, WebRTC data channels, and `fetch()` calls initiated from inside a Web Worker are not routed through the HAR intercept layer and will attempt live network connections regardless of HAR configuration.**
Why this matters: A team recorded a HAR for a real-time collaborative editing feature that used WebSocket connections to sync document state between clients. They configured `context.routeFromHAR(HAR_PATH, { notFound: 'abort' })` expecting all network traffic to be served from the HAR offline. The WebSocket connection bypassed the route handler entirely — HAR routing applies to HTTP/HTTPS requests only, not to the WebSocket upgrade and subsequent frame exchange — and the application failed to establish the sync connection, causing the collaborative editing panel to show a "Connection failed" error. The team incorrectly concluded the feature was broken in their CI environment and spent time investigating network configuration before discovering that WebSocket traffic is categorically excluded from `routeFromHAR()` interception.
Fix: Use `page.routeWebSocket()` (available in Playwright 1.48+) to intercept and mock WebSocket connections separately from HTTP routes. For offline exploratory sessions that involve WebSocket-dependent features, combine `context.routeFromHAR()` for HTTP traffic with explicit `page.routeWebSocket()` handlers that replay pre-recorded WebSocket message sequences from a separate JSON fixture, rather than relying on a single HAR file to cover all protocol types.

---

**G88: `page.exposeFunction()` callbacks that throw a JavaScript error cause the browser-side `await window.yourFunction()` call to reject with an unhandled promise rejection — if the page does not have a global unhandled-rejection handler, the rejection is silently swallowed, and the test continues as if the callback succeeded.**
Why this matters: A team used `page.exposeFunction('__reportBug', reporter)` where `reporter` wrote findings to a database. During a long exploratory session run, the database connection dropped and `reporter()` started throwing `ECONNREFUSED` errors. The browser-side calls to `window.__reportBug()` all rejected, but because the application code called `window.__reportBug(data).catch(() => {})` to be resilient, all errors were silently suppressed. The test suite continued running and reported successful completion, but zero bug findings were written to the database. The team reviewed the exploratory session results the next morning and found an empty findings table with no indication of the recording failure.
Fix: In the Node-side `exposeFunction` callback, catch and re-throw errors with a structured payload that the browser side can detect: return `{ ok: false, error: message }` instead of throwing. On the browser side, assert on the return value: `const result = await window.__reportBug(data); if (!result.ok) console.error('Bug reporting failed:', result.error)`. Additionally, in `globalTeardown`, verify that the expected number of findings were written to the database and fail the teardown if the count is zero when the session produced at least one charter branch.

---

**G89: `page.coverage.stopJSCoverage()` returns coverage for all scripts loaded since `startJSCoverage()` was called, including Playwright's own injected evaluation scripts and any browser extension scripts — these internal entries inflate the total script count and skew coverage-gap heuristics if not filtered before analysis.**
Why this matters: A team built a coverage-gap detector that flagged any script with less than 10% coverage as a potential unexplored charter target. After integrating the detector into their session pipeline, it consistently flagged 5–8 "mystery" scripts with 0% coverage per session. Investigation revealed these were Playwright's own `__playwright_evaluation_script__` entries (scripts injected by `page.evaluate()` and `page.exposeFunction()` calls) and scripts from a browser extension installed in the test profile. Because these internal scripts had no corresponding application-code source maps, the detector treated them as unexercised application code and generated false-positive "unexplored charter" recommendations, wasting triage time every sprint.
Fix: Before processing coverage data, filter out entries whose URL is empty, starts with `__playwright`, or matches known extension URL patterns: `const appCoverage = jsCoverage.filter(e => e.url && !e.url.startsWith('__playwright') && !e.url.startsWith('chrome-extension://') && !e.url.startsWith('data:'))`. Also filter out entries whose `source` field is absent, as these typically represent dynamically injected evaluation fragments rather than application bundle files. Apply the same filter to CSS coverage to exclude injected stylesheets from coverage gap analysis.

## Cycle 64 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 518** — Clock `install()` + `runFor()` Loop: Chartering Recurring Timer Drift
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: recurring notification timer accumulates drift', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-05-14T09:00:00Z') });
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const notificationBadge = page.getByTestId('notification-badge');
  const initialCount = parseInt(await notificationBadge.textContent() ?? '0', 10);

  for (let tick = 1; tick <= 5; tick++) {
    await page.clock.runFor(60_000); // advance 1 minute per iteration
    const count = parseInt(await notificationBadge.textContent() ?? '0', 10);
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'timer-tick',
      value: `minute ${tick}: badge count = ${count}`,
    });
  }

  const finalCount = parseInt(await notificationBadge.textContent() ?? '0', 10);
  expect(finalCount).toBeGreaterThan(initialCount);
  await page.screenshot({ path: 'session-artefacts/timer-drift-final.png', fullPage: true });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.clock.runFor()` in a loop with explicit tick-by-tick annotation lets the charter detect badge-count drift or missed increments mid-sequence without committing to a single `fastForward()` jump that would skip intermediate states — the tradeoff is that each `runFor()` call processes the full Playwright event loop including any pending microtasks and `requestAnimationFrame` callbacks, so a tight loop of 60 iterations can take several seconds of real wall-clock time for animation-heavy dashboards and is not a substitute for `fastForward()` when the goal is simply to reach an end state quickly.

---

**Pattern 519** — `page.clock.pauseAt()` + `page.clock.resume()`: Chartering Race Conditions at Exact Millisecond Boundaries
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: token refresh races with expiry boundary', async ({ page }) => {
  const expiryMs = new Date('2026-05-14T10:00:00.000Z').getTime();
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date(expiryMs - 5000) }); // 5 s before expiry
  await page.goto('/app');

  // pause exactly 1 ms before the boundary
  await page.clock.pauseAt(expiryMs - 1);

  const refreshPromise = page.waitForResponse(
    (r) => r.url().includes('/api/auth/refresh') && r.status() === 200,
    { timeout: 3000 },
  ).catch(() => null);

  await page.clock.resume(); // let time reach the boundary
  const refreshResponse = await refreshPromise;

  if (!refreshResponse) {
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'high-risk',
      value: 'no token refresh fired at expiry boundary — session may silently expire',
    });
  }
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible(); // confirm UI is still rendered
});
```
Tradeoff: Parking the clock 1 ms before the boundary with `pauseAt()` and then calling `resume()` while simultaneously awaiting the refresh response gives the charter a deterministic window to observe whether the application triggers a proactive refresh or falls through to an expired-token error — the tradeoff is that `page.clock.resume()` re-activates real-time clock progression, so if the application has a 200 ms debounce on the refresh trigger, the `waitForResponse` timeout must be set generously to avoid false-negative findings on slower CI machines where the debounce may consume more than the default 3-second window.

**Pattern 520** — `startJSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false })`: Cross-Navigation Bundle Coverage Charter
```typescript
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

test('charter: multi-page journey coverage heatmap', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.coverage.startJSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false, reportAnonymousScripts: false });

  const journey = ['/home', '/products', '/product/42', '/cart', '/checkout'];
  for (const route of journey) {
    await page.goto(route);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'coverage-step', value: `navigated to ${route}` });
  }

  const jsCoverage = await page.coverage.stopJSCoverage();
  const appEntries = jsCoverage.filter(
    (e) => e.url && !e.url.startsWith('__playwright') && !e.url.startsWith('chrome-extension://'),
  );

  const report = appEntries.map((e) => {
    const used = e.functions.flatMap((f) => f.ranges.filter((r) => r.count > 0));
    const totalChars = e.source?.length ?? 1;
    const coveredChars = used.reduce((acc, r) => acc + (r.endOffset - r.startOffset), 0);
    return { url: e.url, coveragePct: Math.round((coveredChars / totalChars) * 100) };
  });

  fs.mkdirSync('session-artefacts', { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join('session-artefacts', 'coverage-heatmap.json'), JSON.stringify(report, null, 2));
  await test.info().attach('coverage-heatmap', {
    body: Buffer.from(JSON.stringify(report, null, 2)),
    contentType: 'application/json',
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Setting `resetOnNavigation: false` accumulates coverage across the entire multi-page journey in a single collection pass, which reveals which application bundles are dead code across the full user flow — the tradeoff is that Playwright's JS coverage API is Chromium-only, so this pattern cannot be used to gather coverage data for charter sessions that must validate Firefox or WebKit behaviour, and coverage percentage calculations based on character offsets (rather than AST-level branch counts) systematically over-count coverage for minified bundles where a single executed statement covers hundreds of characters.

---

**Pattern 521** — `startCSSCoverage()` + Dead-Style Charter: Finding Unreachable UI States
```typescript
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

test('charter: identify dead CSS rules across auth flows', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.coverage.startCSSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false });

  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('hunter2');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');
  await page.getByRole('link', { name: /settings/i }).click();
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const cssCoverage = await page.coverage.stopCSSCoverage();
  const deadRules = cssCoverage.flatMap((sheet) => {
    const totalLength = sheet.text?.length ?? 0;
    const coveredLength = sheet.ranges.reduce((a, r) => a + (r.end - r.start), 0);
    const deadPct = totalLength > 0 ? Math.round(((totalLength - coveredLength) / totalLength) * 100) : 0;
    return deadPct > 50 ? [{ url: sheet.url, deadPct }] : [];
  });

  fs.mkdirSync('session-artefacts', { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join('session-artefacts', 'dead-css.json'), JSON.stringify(deadRules, null, 2));
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'dead-css-count', value: String(deadRules.length) });
});
```
Tradeoff: Flagging stylesheets with over 50% dead rules during the auth-and-settings journey surfaces UI states (error modals, empty-state illustrations, premium-tier feature panels) that are never rendered during happy-path exploration and therefore become high-value charter targets — the tradeoff is that `stopCSSCoverage()` reports used byte ranges within the raw stylesheet text, not individual selector-level usage, so a single used property in a rule block counts the entire block as covered; the heuristic is directionally useful for prioritising charter breadth but must not be used as a definitive "dead code" audit without parser-level CSS analysis.

**Pattern 522** — `context.routeFromHAR({ update: true })` + Charter Diff: Living-HAR Session Replay
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';

const HAR_PATH = 'fixtures/product-list.har';

test('charter: product list HAR replay with live diff', async ({ context, page }) => {
  const harExists = fs.existsSync(HAR_PATH);
  await context.routeFromHAR(HAR_PATH, {
    update: !harExists,       // record on first run, replay on subsequent runs
    notFound: 'fallback',     // allow unmatched requests through for new endpoints
  });

  await page.goto('/products');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="product-card"]');

  const productCards = await page.getByTestId('product-card').all();
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'har-product-count',
    value: `${productCards.length} product cards rendered`,
  });

  if (harExists) {
    // On replay runs, screenshot for visual regression against HAR baseline
    await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('product-list-baseline.png', {
      maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.03,
      animations: 'disabled',
    });
  }

  for (const card of productCards.slice(0, 3)) {
    await card.click();
    await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');
    await page.goBack();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `update: !harExists` makes the first run a HAR recording pass and every subsequent run a deterministic offline replay, giving the charter team a self-bootstrapping fixture that stays current whenever the baseline is deleted — the tradeoff is that `notFound: 'fallback'` silently passes unmatched requests to the live network, which means newly added API endpoints are exercised live without being recorded into the HAR; if those endpoints have side effects (e.g., incrementing an analytics counter), the charter will cause unintended mutations in the live environment until the team explicitly refreshes the HAR by deleting it and re-running.

**Pattern 523** — `page.routeWebSocket()`: Mocking Real-Time Collaboration Messages in a Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: collaborative cursor sync under high-frequency message burst', async ({ page }) => {
  const receivedMessages: string[] = [];

  await page.routeWebSocket('/ws/collab', (ws) => {
    ws.onMessage((message) => {
      receivedMessages.push(typeof message === 'string' ? message : '<binary>');
      ws.send(message); // echo back to simulate peer
    });

    // Inject a burst of 20 rapid cursor-position messages from a simulated peer
    for (let i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
      ws.send(JSON.stringify({ type: 'cursor', userId: 'peer-1', x: i * 10, y: i * 5 }));
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/document/123');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="collab-cursor-peer-1"]');

  const cursors = await page.getByTestId('collab-cursor-peer-1').all();
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'ws-burst-result',
    value: `${cursors.length} cursor element(s) after 20-message burst, ${receivedMessages.length} outbound messages captured`,
  });

  expect(cursors.length).toBe(1); // only one cursor element should exist per peer
});
```
Tradeoff: Injecting a synthetic WebSocket message burst directly via `page.routeWebSocket()` lets the charter exercise high-frequency collaborative scenarios without requiring a real peer client or a live WebSocket server — the tradeoff is that `page.routeWebSocket()` intercepts connections at the protocol level and its `send()` method does not respect the application's WebSocket frame-ordering guarantees; if the application uses a binary sub-protocol (e.g., protobuf-encoded frames), you must encode messages yourself using the same schema, otherwise the application will silently drop frames it cannot parse and the charter will produce false-positive "handles bursts correctly" findings.

---

**Pattern 524** — `test.step({ box: true })`: Boxed Charter Phases for Clean Failure Attribution
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

async function performCheckout(page: import('@playwright/test').Page, cardNumber: string) {
  await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill(cardNumber);
  await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('12/28');
  await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).fill('321');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 8000 });
}

test('charter: checkout error attribution per phase', async ({ page }) => {
  await test.step('Phase 1 — add to cart', { box: true }, async () => {
    await page.goto('/products/42');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /add to cart/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByTestId('cart-count')).toHaveText('1');
  });

  await test.step('Phase 2 — proceed to checkout', { box: true }, async () => {
    await page.getByRole('link', { name: /checkout/i }).click();
    await page.waitForURL('/checkout');
  });

  await test.step('Phase 3 — payment with valid card', { box: true }, async () => {
    await performCheckout(page, '4111111111111111');
  });

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'session-outcome', value: 'checkout charter completed all three phases' });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `{ box: true }` option on each `test.step()` call surfaces failures at the step call site in the HTML report rather than inside the helper function's internals, which makes phase-level failure triage dramatically faster in a charter session where multiple collaborators are reviewing findings — the tradeoff is that boxed steps suppress the internal stack trace that would normally point to the exact failing line inside the helper, so when debugging a new failure discovered during the charter you must temporarily remove `{ box: true }` from the failing step to recover the precise line-level error before filing the bug.

---

**Pattern 525** — `test.fail()` Conditional Platform Annotation: Documenting Known Charter Gaps
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: drag-and-drop reorder in task list', async ({ page, browserName }) => {
  test.fail(
    browserName === 'webkit',
    'webkit does not support synthetic dragstart events via page.dispatchEvent — ' +
      'drag reorder is untested on Safari; add a dedicated manual charter entry',
  );

  await page.goto('/tasks');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="task-item"]');

  const firstTask = page.getByTestId('task-item').first();
  const thirdTask = page.getByTestId('task-item').nth(2);

  const sourceBox = await firstTask.boundingBox();
  const targetBox = await thirdTask.boundingBox();
  if (!sourceBox || !targetBox) throw new Error('task items not visible');

  await page.mouse.move(sourceBox.x + sourceBox.width / 2, sourceBox.y + sourceBox.height / 2);
  await page.mouse.down();
  await page.mouse.move(targetBox.x + targetBox.width / 2, targetBox.y + targetBox.height / 2, { steps: 10 });
  await page.mouse.up();

  const taskItems = await page.getByTestId('task-item').allTextContents();
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'reorder-result', value: taskItems.join(' → ') });
  expect(taskItems[2]).toContain(await firstTask.textContent());
});
```
Tradeoff: Tagging the WebKit path with `test.fail()` and an explanatory message converts a silent test skip into a documented charter gap that appears in the Playwright HTML report with a clear owner note — the tradeoff is that `test.fail()` marks the test as "expected to fail" and inverts the pass/fail logic; if the WebKit drag issue is ever fixed upstream, the test will now report as "unexpectedly passing" and appear red in the report until the `test.fail()` guard is removed, so the team must monitor for unexpected-pass regressions in the CI summary rather than treating all red WebKit results as known.

---

**Pattern 526** — `page.screenshot({ mask: [...] })`: Redacting Dynamic Content in Charter Baselines
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: invoice page visual baseline with dynamic fields masked', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/invoices/INV-2026-001');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Mask dynamic fields: invoice date, total amount, and user avatar
  const masks = [
    page.locator('[data-testid="invoice-date"]'),
    page.locator('[data-testid="invoice-total"]'),
    page.locator('[data-testid="user-avatar"]'),
  ];

  const screenshot = await page.screenshot({
    fullPage: true,
    animations: 'disabled',
    mask: masks,
    maskColor: '#FF00FF', // magenta sentinel so masks are visually obvious in diffs
  });

  await test.info().attach('invoice-baseline-masked', {
    body: screenshot,
    contentType: 'image/png',
  });

  await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('invoice-baseline.png', {
    mask: masks,
    maskColor: '#FF00FF',
    maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.02,
    animations: 'disabled',
  });

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'masked-fields', value: masks.length.toString() });
});
```
Tradeoff: Passing an array of `Locator` objects to `mask` replaces dynamic content with a solid-color rectangle before the pixel comparison, eliminating false-positive visual-regression failures caused by timestamps, running totals, and user-specific avatars without requiring any fixture data normalisation — the tradeoff is that `mask` operates on the rendered screenshot after layout, so if a masked element changes size between baseline capture and regression run (e.g., a longer invoice total overflows its container), the change in surrounding layout will still register as a pixel diff even though the masked content itself is hidden; use `clip` combined with `mask` when the layout stability of the masked region itself must also be asserted.

**Pattern 527** — `page.locator.screenshot()` Per-Component Charter: Isolating Component Visual State
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const STATUS_VARIANTS: Array<{ status: string; label: string }> = [
  { status: 'pending', label: 'Pending' },
  { status: 'processing', label: 'Processing' },
  { status: 'complete', label: 'Complete' },
  { status: 'failed', label: 'Failed' },
];

test('charter: order-status badge renders all variants correctly', async ({ page }) => {
  for (const variant of STATUS_VARIANTS) {
    await page.goto(`/storybook/iframe.html?id=order-status-badge--${variant.status}`);
    await page.waitForSelector(`[data-status="${variant.status}"]`);

    const badge = page.locator(`[data-status="${variant.status}"]`);
    const screenshot = await badge.screenshot({ animations: 'disabled' });

    await test.info().attach(`badge-${variant.status}`, {
      body: screenshot,
      contentType: 'image/png',
    });

    await expect(badge).toHaveScreenshot(`badge-${variant.status}.png`, {
      animations: 'disabled',
      maxDiffPixelRatio: 0.01,
    });

    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'component-charter', value: `${variant.label} badge captured` });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Taking a `locator.screenshot()` per component variant captures each badge state in isolation against a transparent background, which produces cleaner diffs than full-page screenshots because surrounding layout noise (navigation bars, sidebars, unrelated content) is excluded from the comparison — the tradeoff is that `locator.screenshot()` only captures the element's own bounding box; if the component renders floating popups, tooltips, or z-index-elevated overlays that extend beyond the element's bounds, those overlays will be clipped and will not appear in the component screenshot, requiring a separate full-page or `clip`-based capture to cover overflow rendering.

**Pattern 528** — `context.addInitScript()` Locale and Feature-Flag Seed: Multi-Variant Charter in One Run
```typescript
import { test } from '@playwright/test';

const VARIANTS = [
  { locale: 'en-US', flags: { premiumCheckout: false }, label: 'free-en-us' },
  { locale: 'de-DE', flags: { premiumCheckout: true }, label: 'premium-de-de' },
  { locale: 'ja-JP', flags: { premiumCheckout: false }, label: 'free-ja-jp' },
];

for (const variant of VARIANTS) {
  test(`charter: pricing display variant — ${variant.label}`, async ({ browser }) => {
    const context = await browser.newContext({ locale: variant.locale, timezoneId: 'UTC' });

    await context.addInitScript((flags) => {
      (window as any).__FEATURE_FLAGS__ = flags;
    }, variant.flags);

    const page = await context.newPage();
    await page.goto('/pricing');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    const priceDisplay = await page.getByTestId('plan-price').allTextContents();
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'pricing-variant',
      value: `${variant.label}: ${priceDisplay.join(', ')}`,
    });

    await page.screenshot({
      path: `session-artefacts/pricing-${variant.label}.png`,
      fullPage: true,
      animations: 'disabled',
    });

    await context.close();
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Calling `context.addInitScript()` before `page.goto()` and passing variant-specific feature flags as a serialised argument injects the flags into every page load within that context, enabling a single test file to cover locale-and-flag combinations without test data or server-side configuration — the tradeoff is that `context.addInitScript()` scripts are not re-evaluated if the application overwrites `window.__FEATURE_FLAGS__` during its own initialisation (e.g., by fetching a flags config from an API and merging into the same global); in applications that hydrate feature flags from an API response, the `addInitScript` value will be overwritten within milliseconds of page load, making the seeded value ineffective; use `context.route()` to intercept the flags API endpoint and return the desired variant instead.

---

**Pattern 529** — `page.exposeFunction()` with Structured Return: Charter Bug Recorder with Failure Detection
```typescript
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

interface BugReport { charter: string; severity: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'critical'; detail: string; }
interface RecordResult { ok: boolean; id?: number; error?: string; }

const findings: BugReport[] = [];

test.beforeAll(async () => {
  // Reset findings for the session
  findings.length = 0;
});

test('charter: sign-up flow with embedded bug recorder', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.exposeFunction('__recordBug', async (report: BugReport): Promise<RecordResult> => {
    try {
      findings.push(report);
      return { ok: true, id: findings.length };
    } catch (err: unknown) {
      return { ok: false, error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) };
    }
  });

  await page.goto('/signup');

  // Trigger the recorder from the browser side
  await page.evaluate(async () => {
    const result = await (window as any).__recordBug({
      charter: 'signup-flow',
      severity: 'high',
      detail: 'email validation accepts spaces before @',
    });
    if (!result.ok) console.error('Bug record failed:', result.error);
  });

  test.afterAll(() => {
    fs.mkdirSync('session-artefacts', { recursive: true });
    fs.writeFileSync(
      path.join('session-artefacts', 'bug-findings.json'),
      JSON.stringify(findings, null, 2),
    );
  });

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'findings-count', value: String(findings.length) });
});
```
Tradeoff: Returning `{ ok, id, error }` from the `exposeFunction` callback instead of throwing makes all recording failures explicit and detectable by the browser-side caller, preventing silent data loss if the in-memory store or downstream sink rejects a finding — the tradeoff is that `page.exposeFunction()` registers the function on a single page instance only; if the charter spawns popup windows or navigates to a new page via `window.open()`, the new page will not have `window.__recordBug` available unless the function is registered on the browser context level via `context.exposeFunction()` instead; always prefer `context.exposeFunction()` for multi-page charter sessions.

**Pattern 530** — Session-Based Charter with SBTM Ledger: Structured Coverage Accounting
```typescript
import { test } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

interface SBTMEntry {
  charter: string;
  tester: string;
  duration: number;
  bugs: number;
  issues: number;
  setup: number;
}

test('charter: SBTM-instrumented search and filter session', async ({ page }) => {
  const sessionStart = Date.now();
  const ledger: SBTMEntry = {
    charter: 'Explore search + filter interaction under 100-result load',
    tester: process.env.CI_ACTOR ?? 'automated',
    duration: 0,
    bugs: 0,
    issues: 0,
    setup: 0,
  };

  const setupStart = Date.now();
  await page.goto('/search');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="search-input"]');
  ledger.setup = Date.now() - setupStart;

  await page.getByTestId('search-input').fill('widget');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /search/i }).click();
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="result-item"]');

  const resultCount = await page.getByTestId('result-item').count();
  if (resultCount === 0) {
    ledger.bugs++;
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'bug', value: 'search for "widget" returned zero results' });
  }

  await page.getByLabel(/category/i).selectOption('electronics');
  const filteredCount = await page.getByTestId('result-item').count();
  if (filteredCount > resultCount) {
    ledger.issues++;
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'issue', value: 'filter increased result count — unexpected behaviour' });
  }

  ledger.duration = Date.now() - sessionStart;
  fs.mkdirSync('session-artefacts', { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join('session-artefacts', 'sbtm-ledger.json'), JSON.stringify(ledger, null, 2));
});
```
Tradeoff: Structuring charter metadata as an SBTM ledger with explicit `bugs`, `issues`, `setup`, and `duration` fields maps directly to the Session-Based Test Management reporting model used by exploratory testing programs, enabling CI pipelines to aggregate coverage metrics across sessions without manual tester notes — the tradeoff is that bug and issue counts in this pattern are derived from in-test assertions rather than genuine exploratory tester judgment; automated SBTM metrics systematically under-count bugs because the code can only detect conditions it was explicitly programmed to check, whereas a human tester would notice anomalies outside the written assertions; treat automated SBTM ledgers as a lower bound on findings density, not a complete picture.

**Pattern 531** — `page.ariaSnapshot()` Structural Diff with `expect.soft()`: Non-Blocking Accessibility Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

test('charter: ARIA tree structural diff across navigation states', async ({ page }) => {
  const snapshots: Record<string, string> = {};

  const captureSnapshot = async (label: string) => {
    const snapshot = await page.ariaSnapshot();
    snapshots[label] = snapshot;
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'aria-snapshot', value: `${label}: ${snapshot.length} chars` });
    return snapshot;
  };

  await page.goto('/home');
  await captureSnapshot('home-unauthenticated');

  await page.goto('/login');
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('correct-password');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('/dashboard');
  await captureSnapshot('dashboard-authenticated');

  // Non-blocking soft assertion: both snapshots must be non-empty
  expect.soft(snapshots['home-unauthenticated'].length, 'home ARIA snapshot empty').toBeGreaterThan(50);
  expect.soft(snapshots['dashboard-authenticated'].length, 'dashboard ARIA snapshot empty').toBeGreaterThan(50);

  // Confirm role=navigation is present in authenticated state
  expect.soft(snapshots['dashboard-authenticated']).toContain('navigation');

  fs.mkdirSync('session-artefacts', { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join('session-artefacts', 'aria-snapshots.json'), JSON.stringify(snapshots, null, 2));
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `expect.soft()` for all ARIA snapshot assertions allows the charter to continue running and accumulating findings even when individual structural assertions fail, which is essential for accessibility charters that want to catalogue the full set of structural issues in a single run rather than aborting at the first missing landmark — the tradeoff is that `expect.soft()` failures are aggregated and only reported at the end of the test, which means if a critical ARIA regression (e.g., the entire `navigation` landmark disappearing) occurs early in the charter, subsequent assertions that depend on correct navigation structure will also fail with misleading error messages, making the root cause harder to isolate than if a hard `expect()` had aborted the session at the point of the primary failure.
