**Pattern 532** — `browser.newContext()` + Concurrent Role Pair: Admin-and-User Interaction Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: admin moderation action reflects immediately in user view', async ({ browser }) => {
  const adminContext = await browser.newContext({ storageState: 'fixtures/admin.json' });
  const userContext = await browser.newContext({ storageState: 'fixtures/user.json' });

  const adminPage = await adminContext.newPage();
  const userPage = await userContext.newPage();

  try {
    await Promise.all([
      adminPage.goto('/admin/posts'),
      userPage.goto('/feed'),
    ]);
    await Promise.all([
      adminPage.waitForLoadState('networkidle'),
      userPage.waitForLoadState('networkidle'),
    ]);

    const targetPost = userPage.getByTestId('post-item').first();
    const postId = await targetPost.getAttribute('data-post-id');
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-target', value: `post-id: ${postId}` });

    // Admin hides the post
    await adminPage.getByTestId(`post-action-${postId}`).click();
    await adminPage.getByRole('menuitem', { name: /hide post/i }).click();
    await expect(adminPage.getByRole('status')).toContainText(/hidden/i, { timeout: 5000 });

    // User feed should no longer contain the post
    await userPage.reload();
    await userPage.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const postStillVisible = await userPage.getByTestId(`post-${postId}`).isVisible();

    if (postStillVisible) {
      test.info().annotations.push({
        type: 'critical-risk',
        value: `post ${postId} still visible to user after admin hide action`,
      });
    }
    expect(postStillVisible, 'hidden post should not be visible in user feed').toBe(false);
  } finally {
    await adminContext.close();
    await userContext.close();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Running admin and user pages in separate `newContext()` instances with distinct `storageState` files gives each role a fully isolated cookie jar and local storage, preventing credential cross-contamination between the concurrently active sessions — the tradeoff is that two contexts each with their own browser process share the same Playwright worker, so on resource-constrained CI machines (fewer than 4 CPUs, less than 4 GB RAM), spawning two contexts in the same test can cause one context to time out waiting for the browser process to respond; prefer using a single test worker for role-pair charters and set `test.slow()` on the test to triple the default timeout when running in constrained CI environments.

### Community Gotchas

**G90: `page.clock.install()` must be called before any `page.goto()` — calling it after the first navigation is a no-op for the current page's already-registered timers and scheduled microtasks, and Playwright does not warn when the install is too late.**
Why this matters: A charter for a session-expiry banner called `page.goto('/app')`, waited for the app to load, and then called `page.clock.install()` intending to fast-forward the inactivity timer. The banner never appeared. The application registered its inactivity `setTimeout` during the initial page load — before `clock.install()` was called — so that timer remained on the real system clock and fired after the genuine 30-minute wall-clock elapsed, not during the test. Subsequent `page.clock.fastForward('30:00')` calls had no effect on the already-registered real timer. The charter silently missed the expiry flow and reported no finding on the banner.
Fix: Always call `page.clock.install({ time: <initial date> })` before the first `page.goto()`. If the page is already loaded (e.g., in a shared-context fixture), trigger `page.reload()` after installing the clock so the application re-registers all timers under the mocked clock. Document `clock.install()` as a pre-navigation prerequisite in your charter template to catch this ordering mistake during peer review.

---

**G91: `page.coverage.startJSCoverage()` and `startCSSCoverage()` are Chromium-only — calling either method on a Firefox or WebKit page throws `Coverage is only supported on Chromium` synchronously and crashes the charter test without a partial-coverage fallback.**
Why this matters: A team added coverage-gap chartering to their cross-browser test suite by calling `page.coverage.startJSCoverage()` in a shared `beforeEach` hook. The tests passed on Chromium in CI but crashed immediately on Firefox and WebKit with an unhandled error, aborting every test in the suite for those browsers — including tests that had nothing to do with coverage. The error message was logged at the beginning of the test run before any test had a chance to execute, making the CI summary show 100% failure rate for Firefox/WebKit jobs and causing the team to investigate a browser installation problem rather than a coverage API misuse.
Fix: Guard all coverage API calls with a browser-type check: `if (browserName === 'chromium') { await page.coverage.startJSCoverage(); }`. Alternatively, move coverage chartering into a dedicated Chromium-only test project in `playwright.config.ts` using `projects: [{ name: 'coverage', use: { browserName: 'chromium' } }]` so Firefox/WebKit projects never encounter coverage setup code. Never place coverage calls in shared `beforeEach` hooks in multi-browser configurations.

---

**G92: `context.routeFromHAR()` with `update: true` will overwrite the existing HAR file on every test run when the test passes — if a test is accidentally run against a production environment, the HAR is silently refreshed with live production data, replacing carefully curated fixture responses with real user data.**
Why this matters: A developer ran the charter test suite locally with `TEST_ENV=production` set to quickly check a responsive layout fix. The `update: true` HAR setting silently re-recorded all matched routes against live production API responses, replacing the fixture HAR with responses that contained real user PII (names, email addresses, transaction IDs). The developer committed the updated HAR to the repository without noticing the content change, and the PII was present in the git history until a security audit identified it six weeks later.
Fix: Make `update` conditional on an explicit environment variable rather than on HAR file existence: `update: process.env.UPDATE_HAR === 'true'`. Add a `.gitattributes` rule to diff HAR files as text so reviewers see content changes in pull requests. Add a pre-commit hook that greps HAR files for common PII patterns (email regex, credit card patterns) and blocks commits if any are found. Never use `update: true` as the default in fixtures checked into version control.

---

**G93: `test.step()` with `{ box: true }` suppresses the internal stack trace — when a boxed step helper calls a sub-helper that fails, the error is reported only at the `test.step()` call site, making it impossible to identify which line inside the helper tree actually threw without temporarily removing `{ box: true }` from every step in the call chain.**
Why this matters: A team used boxed steps across a 12-step checkout charter. When the charter failed intermittently in CI, the HTML report showed `Step "Phase 6 — apply promo code" failed` but the error pointed to the `test.step()` call in the top-level test body, not to the specific `expect()` inside the `applyPromoCode()` helper that was actually failing. Developers had to clone the CI artefact, temporarily un-box every step, and re-run locally to reproduce the failure before they could identify that a timing issue in `page.waitForResponse()` inside the helper was the root cause. The diagnosis took 4 hours for what turned out to be a 2-line fix.
Fix: Use `{ box: true }` only on stable, fully debugged charter helpers where triage speed matters more than diagnostic depth. During active charter development or when investigating a new failure, remove `{ box: true }` to expose the internal stack. Consider a convention of keeping all charter helpers un-boxed during the current sprint and only adding `{ box: true }` after a helper has been stable for two full sprint cycles without a new failure mode.

---

**G94: `page.locator.screenshot()` clips to the element's own bounding box — CSS `overflow: visible` children, `position: fixed` tooltips, and `transform: translate` animations that render outside the element boundary are silently cropped, producing a screenshot that passes the visual assertion even though the visible UI has rendering defects outside the element bounds.**
Why this matters: A charter for a dropdown menu component used `page.locator('[data-testid="dropdown"]').screenshot()` to capture the menu in its open state. The screenshot showed the dropdown trigger button and the menu panel — but the open menu panel was rendered via `position: absolute` and extended 240 px below the bounding box of the `[data-testid="dropdown"]` element. The locator screenshot captured only the trigger button at the element's registered height of 40 px; the menu panel was entirely cropped. The visual regression suite passed every sprint because the clipped screenshot never changed, while actual rendering bugs in the menu panel (a misaligned caret, incorrect border-radius on the last item) went undetected for three sprints.
Fix: For components that render content outside their own bounding box (dropdowns, tooltips, popovers, cascading menus), use `page.screenshot({ clip: { x, y, width, height } })` with a manually specified clip region that encompasses the full visual extent of the component in its expanded state, rather than relying on the locator's automatic bounding box. Alternatively, wrap the component in a `position: relative` container sized to the full expanded height in your Storybook fixture and screenshot the container locator, ensuring the bounding box includes overflow children.

## Cycle 67 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 533** — `page.addLocatorHandler()` Overlay Auto-Dismissal Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: cookie-banner and survey overlay auto-dismissal during navigation', async ({ page }) => {
  // Register a handler that fires whenever the cookie banner becomes visible
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByRole('dialog', { name: /cookie/i }),
    async (overlay) => {
      test.info().annotations.push({
        type: 'overlay-intercepted',
        value: `cookie dialog appeared at ${new Date().toISOString()}`,
      });
      await overlay.getByRole('button', { name: /accept/i }).click();
    }
  );

  // Register a separate handler for NPS survey modals
  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.getByTestId('nps-survey-modal'),
    async () => {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'overlay-intercepted', value: 'NPS survey dismissed' });
      await page.getByTestId('nps-survey-close').click();
    }
  );

  const criticalPaths = ['/home', '/products', '/checkout', '/account'];
  for (const path of criticalPaths) {
    await page.goto(path);
    await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(new RegExp(path));
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-phase', value: `navigated to ${path}` });
  }

  // Confirm overlays no longer block interaction after handlers ran
  await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.addLocatorHandler()` polls for the registered locator before each Playwright action and invokes the handler when found, which elegantly removes transient overlays without requiring `try/catch` in every step — the tradeoff is that the handler fires asynchronously between action calls and is therefore invisible to assertions that run synchronously inline with navigation (e.g., a `waitForNavigation()` that resolves before the banner appears will not trigger the handler), so overlays that appear during navigation rather than after `domcontentloaded` must still be handled explicitly with a `page.waitForSelector()` + `click()` before the `goto()` call returns.

---

**Pattern 534** — `page.waitForFunction()` Custom Poll-Until State Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: async background job completion reflected in UI within SLA', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard/jobs');

  const jobId = await page.evaluate(async () => {
    const res = await fetch('/api/jobs', {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ type: 'export', format: 'csv' }),
    });
    const data = await res.json();
    return data.jobId as string;
  });

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-artifact', value: `jobId: ${jobId}` });

  // Poll the DOM until the job row shows "completed" or timeout at 30s
  const startMs = Date.now();
  await page.waitForFunction(
    ({ id }) => {
      const row = document.querySelector(`[data-job-id="${id}"]`);
      return row?.getAttribute('data-status') === 'completed';
    },
    { id: jobId },
    { timeout: 30_000, polling: 1_000 }
  );

  const elapsedMs = Date.now() - startMs;
  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'sla-measurement',
    value: `job completed in ${elapsedMs}ms (limit 30000ms)`,
  });

  expect(elapsedMs, 'job must complete within SLA').toBeLessThan(30_000);
  await expect(page.getByTestId(`job-download-${jobId}`)).toBeEnabled();
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.waitForFunction()` with `polling: 1_000` lets the charter observe real async state transitions in the DOM at 1-second resolution without any application-side instrumentation — the tradeoff is that 1-second polling granularity means SLA violations that occur within the last polling interval (e.g., a job that completes at 29.5 s will register as ~30 s elapsed) introduce up to 1 s of measurement error; for sub-second SLA precision, reduce `polling` to 100 or less, but note that tight polling intervals generate significant browser-process CPU overhead in long-running charters with many concurrent `waitForFunction()` calls.

---

**Pattern 535** — `page.route()` + `request.postDataJSON()` Payload Mutation Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: mutated payment payload rejected with 422, UI shows correct error', async ({ page }) => {
  const capturedPayloads: unknown[] = [];

  await page.route('**/api/payments', async (route) => {
    const original = route.request().postDataJSON() as Record<string, unknown>;
    capturedPayloads.push(structuredClone(original));

    // Mutate: replace card number with an invalid Luhn sequence
    const mutated = { ...original, cardNumber: '1234000000000000' };

    await route.continue({
      postData: JSON.stringify(mutated),
      headers: {
        ...route.request().headers(),
        'content-type': 'application/json',
      },
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByLabel('Card number').fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByLabel('Expiry').fill('12/28');
  await page.getByLabel('CVV').fill('123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter-payload',
    value: JSON.stringify(capturedPayloads),
  });

  await expect(page.getByRole('alert')).toContainText(/invalid card/i);
  await expect(page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i })).toBeEnabled();
});
```
Tradeoff: Intercepting and mutating the `postData` inside `route.continue()` lets the charter inject invalid payloads at the network boundary without touching the UI form logic, which exercises server-side validation and error-rendering paths in a single test — the tradeoff is that `route.continue()` with a modified `postData` silently drops any form-encoded body structure (e.g., `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`) and replaces it with the raw string value of the `postData` argument, so callers must manually serialize the payload to match the original `content-type` and set the header explicitly, or the server will reject the request with a 400 before the mutation logic is even evaluated.

---

**Pattern 536** — `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion })` Motion Sensitivity Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: all animated components respect prefers-reduced-motion', async ({ page }) => {
  // Must be set before goto so CSS media query resolves at parse time
  await page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' });
  await page.goto('/components/animated');

  const animatedSelectors = [
    '[data-testid="hero-carousel"]',
    '[data-testid="loading-spinner"]',
    '[data-testid="toast-slide-in"]',
    '[data-testid="accordion-expand"]',
  ];

  for (const selector of animatedSelectors) {
    const el = page.locator(selector);
    if (!(await el.isVisible())) continue;

    const animationDuration = await el.evaluate((node) => {
      const style = window.getComputedStyle(node);
      return parseFloat(style.animationDuration) + parseFloat(style.transitionDuration);
    });

    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'motion-audit',
      value: `${selector}: computed animation+transition = ${animationDuration}s`,
    });

    expect.soft(
      animationDuration,
      `${selector} must have 0s animation+transition under reduced-motion`
    ).toBe(0);
  }

  await page.screenshot({ path: 'session-artefacts/reduced-motion-state.png', fullPage: true });
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` sets the `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` media feature at the browser level, allowing the charter to verify CSS compliance via `getComputedStyle` without requiring a real OS accessibility setting — the tradeoff is that this approach only catches animations controlled by CSS `animation-duration` and `transition-duration` properties; JavaScript-driven animations (e.g., GSAP timelines, Web Animations API sequences, `requestAnimationFrame` loops) are not suppressed by the media feature unless the application explicitly reads `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches` in its animation orchestration code, so charters relying solely on `getComputedStyle` checks will produce false-passing results for JS-animated components.

---

**Pattern 537** — `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'parallel' })` Viewport Matrix Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const VIEWPORTS = [
  { label: 'mobile-xs', width: 375, height: 667 },
  { label: 'mobile-lg', width: 414, height: 896 },
  { label: 'tablet', width: 768, height: 1024 },
  { label: 'desktop', width: 1280, height: 800 },
  { label: 'wide', width: 1920, height: 1080 },
];

test.describe('charter: responsive navigation rendering across breakpoints', () => {
  test.describe.configure({ mode: 'parallel' });

  for (const vp of VIEWPORTS) {
    test(`viewport ${vp.label} (${vp.width}x${vp.height})`, async ({ browser }) => {
      const context = await browser.newContext({ viewport: { width: vp.width, height: vp.height } });
      const page = await context.newPage();

      try {
        await page.goto('/');
        await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

        const hamburger = page.getByTestId('hamburger-menu');
        const desktopNav = page.getByTestId('desktop-nav');

        if (vp.width < 768) {
          await expect(hamburger).toBeVisible();
          await expect(desktopNav).toBeHidden();
        } else {
          await expect(desktopNav).toBeVisible();
          await expect(hamburger).toBeHidden();
        }

        await page.screenshot({
          path: `session-artefacts/nav-${vp.label}.png`,
          fullPage: false,
        });

        test.info().annotations.push({
          type: 'viewport-charter',
          value: `${vp.label}: nav layout confirmed`,
        });
      } finally {
        await context.close();
      }
    });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Setting `test.describe.configure({ mode: 'parallel' })` on the viewport loop runs all five breakpoint subtests concurrently within the same worker, halving wall-clock time compared to sequential execution — the tradeoff is that each subtest creates its own `browser.newContext()` with a distinct viewport rather than reusing the fixture-provided `page`, which means five concurrent browser contexts share the same Playwright worker process and can exhaust OS file-descriptor limits on Linux CI machines (ulimit -n defaults to 1024); on a standard 4-CPU CI runner with more than 8 viewport subtests in the loop, prefer splitting the matrix across two Playwright test projects with different `use: { viewport }` settings rather than spawning all contexts within a single parallel describe block.

**Pattern 538** — `page.evaluate()` + `PerformanceObserver` LCP/CLS Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: Core Web Vitals — LCP and CLS captured via PerformanceObserver injection', async ({ page }) => {
  const webVitals: { lcp?: number; cls?: number } = {};

  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    (window as any).__webVitals = { lcp: null, cls: 0 };

    new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
      for (const entry of list.getEntries()) {
        (window as any).__webVitals.lcp = (entry as PerformanceEntry & { startTime: number }).startTime;
      }
    }).observe({ type: 'largest-contentful-paint', buffered: true });

    new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
      for (const entry of list.getEntries()) {
        const layoutEntry = entry as PerformanceEntry & { value: number; hadRecentInput: boolean };
        if (!layoutEntry.hadRecentInput) {
          (window as any).__webVitals.cls += layoutEntry.value;
        }
      }
    }).observe({ type: 'layout-shift', buffered: true });
  });

  await page.goto('/landing');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Give observers time to flush buffered entries
  await page.waitForTimeout(500);

  const raw = await page.evaluate(() => (window as any).__webVitals);
  webVitals.lcp = raw.lcp ?? undefined;
  webVitals.cls = raw.cls ?? undefined;

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'web-vitals', value: JSON.stringify(webVitals) });

  if (webVitals.lcp !== undefined) {
    expect.soft(webVitals.lcp, 'LCP must be under 2500ms (Good threshold)').toBeLessThan(2500);
  }
  if (webVitals.cls !== undefined) {
    expect.soft(webVitals.cls, 'CLS must be under 0.1 (Good threshold)').toBeLessThan(0.1);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Injecting a `PerformanceObserver` via `page.addInitScript()` captures real browser-side LCP and CLS metrics without any third-party dependency, and `buffered: true` ensures entries that fired before the observer connected are still delivered — the tradeoff is that `page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` alone does not guarantee all `layout-shift` entries have been dispatched, because the browser can emit additional layout shifts up to 5 seconds after the last network request as deferred scripts execute; the 500 ms `waitForTimeout` after `networkidle` is a pragmatic but imprecise flush window that may miss late-occurring CLS contributions from async-rendered content (e.g., lazy-loaded ad slots), causing the charter to undercount CLS and produce false-passing results for pages with significant deferred rendering.

**Pattern 539** — `expect(page).toHaveURL()` Regex Redirect-Chain Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: unauthenticated deep-link redirect chain lands on correct post-login destination', async ({ page }) => {
  const visitedUrls: string[] = [];

  page.on('response', (response) => {
    if ([301, 302, 307, 308].includes(response.status())) {
      visitedUrls.push(`${response.status()} ${response.url()}`);
    }
  });

  // Navigate to a protected resource without authentication
  await page.goto('/account/orders/ORD-9921');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'redirect-chain',
    value: JSON.stringify(visitedUrls),
  });

  // Must land on login with a returnTo parameter preserving the original path
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/login\?returnTo=%2Faccount%2Forders%2FORD-9921/);

  // Simulate login
  await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('user@example.com');
  await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('correct-password');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();

  // After authentication, must redirect back to the original deep-link — not /dashboard
  await page.waitForURL(/\/account\/orders\/ORD-9921/, { timeout: 10_000 });
  await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/account\/orders\/ORD-9921/);

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter-result',
    value: `redirect chain length: ${visitedUrls.length}; final URL verified`,
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Listening to `page.on('response')` to capture 3xx responses and cross-referencing with `expect(page).toHaveURL()` regex assertions gives the charter both a structural audit of the redirect chain length and a precision check on the final destination URL — the tradeoff is that `page.on('response')` fires for all responses including XHR and fetch calls, not just top-level navigation redirects, so the `visitedUrls` array will include API endpoint redirects (e.g., a 301 on `/api/v1/` to `/api/v2/`) that inflate the redirect count and can cause the charter to flag an excessive-redirect finding on the deep-link flow when the actual navigation chain is clean; filter the listener to top-level frame navigation by checking `response.frame() === page.mainFrame()` before pushing to `visitedUrls`.

**Pattern 540** — `page.dragAndDrop()` + Annotation Drag-Interaction Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: kanban card drag-and-drop moves task between columns and persists on reload', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/board/sprint-42');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const sourceCard = page.getByTestId('task-card-1047');
  const targetColumn = page.getByTestId('column-in-review');

  const sourceColumnBefore = await sourceCard.evaluate((el) =>
    el.closest('[data-column]')?.getAttribute('data-column')
  );
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'drag-source', value: `card 1047 in column: ${sourceColumnBefore}` });

  await page.dragAndDrop('[data-testid="task-card-1047"]', '[data-testid="column-in-review"]');

  // Optimistic UI: column should update immediately
  await expect(targetColumn.getByTestId('task-card-1047')).toBeVisible();

  // Confirm the API persisted the move
  const apiResponse = await page.waitForResponse(
    (resp) => resp.url().includes('/api/tasks/1047') && resp.request().method() === 'PATCH'
  );
  expect(apiResponse.status()).toBe(200);

  // Reload and verify persistence
  await page.reload();
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('column-in-review').getByTestId('task-card-1047')).toBeVisible();

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-result', value: 'drag persisted across reload — PASS' });
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.dragAndDrop()` dispatches `dragstart`, `dragover`, and `drop` DOM events at source and target coordinates, covering the majority of drag implementations based on the HTML Drag and Drop API — the tradeoff is that `page.dragAndDrop()` does not synthesize intermediate `pointermove` or `mousemove` events between the source and destination, so applications that use pointer-event-based drag libraries (e.g., react-dnd with PointerSensor, dnd-kit, or Sortable.js with `forceFallback: true`) will not enter the dragging state at all and the test will silently pass without any drag occurring; for pointer-event-based drag implementations, use `page.mouse.move()` + `page.mouse.down()` + multiple intermediate `page.mouse.move()` steps + `page.mouse.up()` to synthesize a realistic pointer drag path.

**Pattern 541** — `page.pdf()` Printable-View Charter (Chromium)
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

test('charter: invoice printable-view renders correct totals and no UI chrome', async ({ page, browserName }) => {
  test.skip(browserName !== 'chromium', 'page.pdf() is Chromium-only');

  await page.goto('/invoices/INV-2026-0042/print');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Inject print media before PDF generation
  await page.emulateMedia({ media: 'print' });

  // Confirm that navigation sidebar is hidden under print media
  const sidebarVisible = await page.locator('[data-testid="sidebar"]').isVisible();
  expect.soft(sidebarVisible, 'sidebar must be hidden in print layout').toBe(false);

  const pdfBuffer = await page.pdf({
    format: 'A4',
    printBackground: true,
    margin: { top: '20mm', right: '15mm', bottom: '20mm', left: '15mm' },
  });

  expect(pdfBuffer.byteLength, 'PDF must not be empty').toBeGreaterThan(1024);

  const outDir = 'session-artefacts/invoices';
  fs.mkdirSync(outDir, { recursive: true });
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, 'INV-2026-0042.pdf'), pdfBuffer);

  test.info().attachments.push({
    name: 'INV-2026-0042.pdf',
    contentType: 'application/pdf',
    body: pdfBuffer,
  });

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'charter-artifact',
    value: `PDF generated: ${pdfBuffer.byteLength} bytes`,
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.pdf()` with `page.emulateMedia({ media: 'print' })` renders the page under print media queries and captures the result as a PDF buffer that can be attached directly to the Playwright HTML report — the tradeoff is that `page.pdf()` always renders using the `print` CSS media type regardless of whether `page.emulateMedia({ media: 'screen' })` was set beforehand, because the PDF renderer internally overrides the media type to `print`; calling `page.emulateMedia({ media: 'print' })` before `page.pdf()` is therefore redundant for the PDF output but is still necessary for the `isVisible()` DOM checks that precede it, which run under the currently emulated media type rather than the PDF rendering context.

**Pattern 542** — `worker` Fixture + Shared Database Seeding for Multi-Test Charter Isolation
```typescript
import { test as base, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import { createTestDatabase, dropTestDatabase } from './helpers/db';

type WorkerFixtures = { testDbUrl: string };

const test = base.extend<{}, WorkerFixtures>({
  testDbUrl: [
    async ({}, use, workerInfo) => {
      const dbName = `charter_worker_${workerInfo.workerIndex}`;
      const dbUrl = await createTestDatabase(dbName);
      await use(dbUrl);
      await dropTestDatabase(dbName);
    },
    { scope: 'worker' },
  ],
});

test('charter: concurrent order creation does not produce duplicate order IDs', async ({ page, testDbUrl }) => {
  process.env.TEST_DB_URL = testDbUrl;

  await page.goto('/orders/new');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const orderIds = new Set<string>();

  for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
    await page.getByLabel('Product').selectOption({ index: i % 3 });
    await page.getByLabel('Quantity').fill(String(i + 1));
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /place order/i }).click();

    const response = await page.waitForResponse((r) => r.url().includes('/api/orders') && r.status() === 201);
    const body = await response.json();
    orderIds.add(body.orderId);

    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'order-created', value: body.orderId });
    await page.goto('/orders/new');
  }

  expect(orderIds.size, 'all 5 orders must have unique IDs').toBe(5);
});
```
Tradeoff: Scoping the database fixture to `{ scope: 'worker' }` means each Playwright worker process gets exactly one isolated database that is created once and torn down after all tests in that worker complete, which avoids the overhead of per-test database creation — the tradeoff is that all tests within the same worker share the same database instance, so if one test leaves uncommitted transactions or fails mid-write, subsequent tests in that worker will observe corrupted state; mitigate by wrapping each test's database operations in a transaction that is rolled back in an `afterEach` hook, or use a per-test `{ scope: 'test' }` fixture when strict test isolation is more important than provisioning overhead.

**Pattern 543** — `page.getByRole('table')` + `.filter()` Data-Grid Accessibility Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: data-grid table exposes correct ARIA roles, column headers, and row counts', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports/transactions');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const table = page.getByRole('table', { name: /transactions/i });
  await expect(table).toBeVisible();

  // Every column header must have a non-empty accessible name
  const headers = table.getByRole('columnheader');
  const headerCount = await headers.count();
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-audit', value: `column headers found: ${headerCount}` });
  expect(headerCount, 'table must have at least 3 column headers').toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(3);

  for (let i = 0; i < headerCount; i++) {
    const name = await headers.nth(i).textContent();
    expect.soft(name?.trim().length, `column header ${i} must not be empty`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
  }

  // Row count must match the pagination summary text
  const rows = table.getByRole('row').filter({ hasNot: page.getByRole('columnheader') });
  const rowCount = await rows.count();

  const summary = await page.getByTestId('pagination-summary').textContent();
  const summaryMatch = summary?.match(/Showing \d+-\d+ of (\d+)/);
  if (summaryMatch) {
    const totalOnPage = parseInt(summaryMatch[1]);
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-audit', value: `DOM rows: ${rowCount}, summary total: ${totalOnPage}` });
    expect.soft(rowCount, 'DOM row count must match pagination summary page size').toBeLessThanOrEqual(totalOnPage);
  }

  await page.screenshot({ path: 'session-artefacts/data-grid-audit.png' });
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `page.getByRole('table')` with `.filter()` to isolate data rows from header rows leverages Playwright's ARIA-aware locator API, which correctly handles `<thead>` / `<tbody>` structures and accessible table names without brittle CSS selectors — the tradeoff is that virtualized data grids (e.g., AG Grid, TanStack Virtual) only render the visible rows in the DOM, so `getByRole('row').count()` returns the viewport-window row count rather than the total dataset size, making the row-count cross-reference against the pagination summary unreliable; for virtualized grids the charter must scroll to the last row using `locator.scrollIntoViewIfNeeded()` in a loop and accumulate the total row count across scroll positions rather than reading the DOM count once.

**Pattern 544** — `test.describe.serial()` Ordered Phase Gate for Stateful Workflow Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';

test.describe.serial('charter: end-to-end SaaS trial onboarding flow — ordered phase gate', () => {
  const STATE_FILE = 'session-artefacts/onboarding-state.json';
  let accountEmail: string;

  test('Phase 1 — signup and email verification', async ({ page }) => {
    accountEmail = `charter+${Date.now()}@mailinator.com`;
    await page.goto('/signup');
    await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(accountEmail);
    await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('Charter@2026!');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /create account/i }).click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/verify-email/);
    fs.writeFileSync(STATE_FILE, JSON.stringify({ accountEmail }));
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-phase', value: 'Phase 1 complete — email registered' });
  });

  test('Phase 2 — workspace setup wizard', async ({ page }) => {
    const state = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(STATE_FILE, 'utf-8'));
    accountEmail = state.accountEmail;

    await page.goto('/login');
    await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(accountEmail);
    await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('Charter@2026!');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
    await page.waitForURL(/\/onboarding\/workspace/);
    await page.getByLabel('Workspace name').fill('Charter Corp');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue/i }).click();
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/onboarding\/invite/);
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-phase', value: 'Phase 2 complete — workspace created' });
  });

  test('Phase 3 — dashboard first-run state validation', async ({ page }) => {
    await page.goto('/login');
    await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(accountEmail);
    await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('Charter@2026!');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
    await page.waitForURL(/\/dashboard/);
    await expect(page.getByTestId('empty-state-prompt')).toBeVisible();
    await expect(page.getByText(/Charter Corp/)).toBeVisible();
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-phase', value: 'Phase 3 complete — dashboard first-run state confirmed' });
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: `test.describe.serial()` guarantees that the three onboarding phases execute in strict order with a shared outer scope, making it possible to pass state (the registered email) forward from Phase 1 to Phase 3 without an external database fixture — the tradeoff is that `test.describe.serial()` skips all remaining tests in the block if any earlier test fails, so a flaky Phase 1 (e.g., a timing issue in the email-field animation) will suppress Phase 2 and Phase 3 results and report them as skipped rather than failed, masking whether the downstream phases would have passed independently; when `retries` is configured globally, Playwright retries the entire serial block from Phase 1 on each retry attempt rather than from the failing phase, which can triple or quadruple CI time on flaky serial charters.

**Pattern 545** — `page.keyboard.press()` Sequence Keyboard-Only Navigation Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('charter: checkout form is fully completable using keyboard only — no mouse required', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded');

  // Focus the first focusable element
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab');

  const tabStops: string[] = [];
  let previousActiveElement = '';

  for (let i = 0; i < 30; i++) {
    const activeInfo = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const el = document.activeElement as HTMLElement | null;
      if (!el) return null;
      return {
        tag: el.tagName.toLowerCase(),
        role: el.getAttribute('role'),
        label: el.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? el.getAttribute('placeholder') ?? el.textContent?.trim().slice(0, 40),
        testId: el.getAttribute('data-testid'),
      };
    });

    if (!activeInfo) break;
    const key = `${activeInfo.tag}[${activeInfo.role ?? ''}] "${activeInfo.label ?? ''}"`;
    if (key === previousActiveElement) break; // Focus trap detected
    tabStops.push(key);
    previousActiveElement = key;

    await page.keyboard.press('Tab');
  }

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'keyboard-charter', value: JSON.stringify(tabStops, null, 2) });

  const hasPayButton = tabStops.some((s) => /pay|submit|place order/i.test(s));
  expect(hasPayButton, 'keyboard tab order must reach the submit/pay button').toBe(true);

  // No focus trap in the main form (all 30 iterations must advance focus)
  const uniqueStops = new Set(tabStops);
  expect(uniqueStops.size, 'tab order must not cycle before reaching pay button').toBeGreaterThan(3);
});
```
Tradeoff: Iterating `page.keyboard.press('Tab')` in a loop and capturing `document.activeElement` metadata after each keypress produces a precise tab-order transcript that reveals focus traps, skipped interactive elements, and missing `aria-label` attributes in a single charter pass — the tradeoff is that `page.evaluate()` for each tab stop introduces a round-trip between the browser context and the Node.js test runner for every iteration, making the charter noticeably slow (approximately 50–100 ms per tab stop) on forms with 20+ interactive elements; for performance-sensitive charter suites, batch the entire tab traversal inside a single `page.evaluate()` call that programmatically tabs through all elements using `element.focus()` and collects their metadata in one array, then return the array to the test runner in a single round-trip.

---

**Pattern 546** — `test.setTimeout()` Adaptive + `page.route()` Network Throttle Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const THROTTLE_PROFILES = [
  { label: 'fast-3g', downloadKbps: 1600, uploadKbps: 750, latencyMs: 150 },
  { label: 'slow-3g', downloadKbps: 400, uploadKbps: 200, latencyMs: 400 },
  { label: 'offline', downloadKbps: 0, uploadKbps: 0, latencyMs: 0 },
];

for (const profile of THROTTLE_PROFILES) {
  test(`charter: app loads and remains interactive under ${profile.label}`, async ({ page, context }) => {
    // Extend timeout proportional to simulated latency
    test.setTimeout(30_000 + profile.latencyMs * 10);

    if (profile.label === 'offline') {
      await context.setOffline(true);
    } else {
      await context.route('**', async (route) => {
        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, profile.latencyMs));
        await route.continue();
      });
    }

    const navigationStart = Date.now();
    try {
      await page.goto('/dashboard', { timeout: 20_000 });
      await page.waitForLoadState('domcontentloaded', { timeout: 20_000 });
    } catch {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-finding', value: `${profile.label}: navigation failed or timed out` });
      if (profile.label === 'offline') return; // Expected — offline should show error UI
      throw new Error(`Navigation failed under ${profile.label} — unacceptable`);
    }

    const ttid = Date.now() - navigationStart;
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'performance-charter', value: `${profile.label}: TTID=${ttid}ms` });

    if (profile.label === 'offline') {
      await expect(page.getByRole('alert', { name: /no internet/i })).toBeVisible();
    } else {
      await expect(page.getByRole('main')).toBeVisible();
      expect.soft(ttid, `TTID under ${profile.label} must be < 10s`).toBeLessThan(10_000);
    }
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Simulating network throttle via `context.route()` with a `setTimeout` delay is portable across all operating systems and does not require CDP (Chrome DevTools Protocol) `Network.emulateNetworkConditions`, which is Chromium-only — the tradeoff is that injecting a uniform per-request delay is a coarse approximation that applies the same latency to every request including sub-resource requests, which inflates the total page load time non-linearly (a page with 40 assets at 400 ms latency experiences 16 s of added delay from the route middleware alone), making TTID measurements incomparable to real-world 3G performance where TCP/IP congestion window growth and browser request pipelining produce qualitatively different loading patterns than uniform per-request synthetic delays.

---

**Pattern 547** — `browser.newContext({ recordVideo: { dir } })` Video Artefact Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

test('charter: multi-step file upload wizard — video evidence of full user journey', async ({ browser }) => {
  const videoDir = 'session-artefacts/video-charters';
  fs.mkdirSync(videoDir, { recursive: true });

  const context = await browser.newContext({
    recordVideo: {
      dir: videoDir,
      size: { width: 1280, height: 720 },
    },
  });

  const page = await context.newPage();

  try {
    await page.goto('/files/upload');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Step 1 — select file
    const fileChooserPromise = page.waitForEvent('filechooser');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /choose files/i }).click();
    const fileChooser = await fileChooserPromise;
    await fileChooser.setFiles([{ name: 'charter-sample.pdf', mimeType: 'application/pdf', buffer: Buffer.alloc(1024) }]);

    // Step 2 — set metadata
    await page.getByLabel('Document title').fill('Charter Sample Q2 2026');
    await page.getByLabel('Category').selectOption('reports');

    // Step 3 — submit and confirm
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /upload/i }).click();
    await expect(page.getByRole('status')).toContainText(/upload complete/i, { timeout: 15_000 });

    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-phase', value: 'upload wizard completed successfully' });
  } finally {
    await context.close(); // Finalizes the video file

    const videoFiles = fs.readdirSync(videoDir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.webm'));
    for (const vf of videoFiles) {
      const vBuf = fs.readFileSync(path.join(videoDir, vf));
      test.info().attachments.push({ name: vf, contentType: 'video/webm', body: vBuf });
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `browser.newContext({ recordVideo: { dir } })` records the charter session as a `.webm` video and attaches it to the Playwright HTML report, providing unambiguous visual evidence of the exact UI state at each step for both passing and failing charter runs — the tradeoff is that `context.close()` must be called explicitly (not relying on the test teardown) to trigger Playwright's video finalizer, because if the test process is killed or times out before `close()` completes, the `.webm` file on disk will be a partial, unreadable video (missing the EBML end-of-segment marker); always wrap the page interactions in a `try/finally` block with `context.close()` in the `finally` clause, and be aware that video recording increases per-test memory usage by approximately 30–60 MB per concurrent context on a 1280x720 viewport.

### Community Gotchas

**G95: `page.addLocatorHandler()` does not intercept modals that block `page.waitForNavigation()` — if a modal appears during the browser's navigation commit phase, the navigation promise rejects before the handler has a chance to dismiss the modal.**
Why this matters: A team registered a `locatorHandler` for a GDPR consent modal that occasionally appeared mid-navigation on their staging environment. During most test runs the modal appeared after `waitForNavigation()` resolved and the handler correctly dismissed it. On slower CI machines, the modal appeared during the navigation commit, causing `waitForNavigation()` to reject with `net::ERR_ABORTED` before the handler could fire. The charter reported navigation errors and was marked as infrastructure flakiness for three sprints before a network trace revealed the modal was triggering a navigation abort, not a real network error.
Fix: For modals that can appear during navigation commit, register a `page.route()` handler that intercepts the URL triggering the modal (e.g., a `/consent` endpoint) and fulfills it immediately with an empty `200` response to suppress the modal entirely during the charter session. Reserve `page.addLocatorHandler()` for post-navigation overlays that are purely DOM-rendered and do not involve network requests.

---

**G96: `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` must be called before the first `page.goto()` — calling it after the page loads does not retroactively apply `prefers-reduced-motion` to already-parsed CSS transitions on existing elements.**
Why this matters: A charter for a hero carousel called `page.goto('/landing')`, waited for `networkidle`, and then called `page.emulateMedia({ reducedMotion: 'reduce' })` expecting the carousel to freeze. The carousel continued animating. The browser had already computed `transition-duration` for `.carousel-track` as `0.6s` when the stylesheet was first parsed — before the media emulation changed the environment. Subsequent `getComputedStyle` reads after emulation returned the new value of `0s` (because the computed style reflects the current media query state), but the CSS transition engine had already committed the animation timeline on the existing element and did not re-evaluate the transition for the already-running animation.
Fix: Always call `page.emulateMedia()` before `page.goto()` so that CSS is parsed and `getComputedStyle` is computed under the emulated media environment from the first render. If the page is already loaded (e.g., in a shared context fixture), call `page.reload()` after `emulateMedia()` to force a full style recalculation before asserting computed animation properties.

---

**G97: `page.pdf()` ignores `page.emulateMedia({ media: 'screen' })` — the PDF renderer always uses `print` media type regardless of the currently emulated media setting, so `@media screen` styles are never reflected in the generated PDF.**
Why this matters: A charter for a report page called `page.emulateMedia({ media: 'screen' })` to check that the screen layout rendered correctly, then called `page.pdf()` expecting to capture the screen layout as a PDF for an audit trail. The generated PDF showed the `@media print` layout (single-column, no sidebar, grey background) rather than the screen layout the charter had visually verified. The audit team accepted the PDF artefact as representative of the screen layout for three weeks before a design review identified that the captured PDF did not match the UI in production.
Fix: Understand that `page.pdf()` is exclusively a print-layout capture tool. If a screen-layout audit trail is required, use `page.screenshot({ fullPage: true })` instead. If both a screen screenshot and a print PDF are needed, call `page.screenshot()` first (under `emulateMedia: 'screen'`), then switch to `emulateMedia: 'print'` and call `page.pdf()`, and attach both artefacts to the test report clearly labelled as `screen-layout.png` and `print-layout.pdf`.

---

**G98: `test.describe.serial()` combined with `retries: N` retries the entire serial block from the first test — a retry triggered by a flaky final test re-executes all earlier tests in the block, creating duplicate side effects (duplicate user accounts, duplicate database rows) that can corrupt shared state and cause subsequent retry attempts to fail for a completely different reason.**
Why this matters: A serial charter for a SaaS onboarding flow created a new user account in Phase 1 and used that account through Phase 3. With `retries: 2` configured globally, a flaky Phase 3 network assertion caused Playwright to retry the entire block from Phase 1. The Phase 1 retry attempted to create a user account with the same email address (derived from `Date.now()` but within the same second), which the API rejected with `409 Conflict`. The Phase 1 test then failed with an account-creation error, and Playwright retried the block a second time with the same outcome. The root cause (a flaky Phase 3 assertion) was never re-executed and the CI run reported Phase 1 as the failing test, misdirecting a 90-minute debugging session.
Fix: In serial blocks that create side effects, always generate uniquely seeded identifiers that cannot collide across retry attempts (e.g., use `workerInfo.workerIndex + '_' + Date.now() + '_' + Math.random().toString(36).slice(2)` as the email seed). Alternatively, add an idempotency check at the start of Phase 1 that skips account creation if the account already exists, treating the conflict as a resumable state rather than a fatal error.

---

**G99: `page.dragAndDrop()` does not synthesize `pointermove` events between source and target — drag-and-drop libraries that use the Pointer Events API with a `PointerSensor` (e.g., dnd-kit, react-beautiful-dnd with `forceTouch`, SortableJS with `forceFallback: true`) will not enter the dragging state at all, and the drop target assertion will pass vacuously because the card never left the source column.**
Why this matters: A team migrated their kanban board from react-beautiful-dnd (HTML DnD API) to dnd-kit (Pointer Events API) as part of a mobile-compatibility initiative. Their existing drag-and-drop charter tests continued to pass in CI after the migration. The `page.dragAndDrop()` calls silently fired `dragstart` and `drop` events that dnd-kit's `PointerSensor` does not listen to, so the dragged card stayed in its original column. The `expect(targetColumn.getByTestId('task-card')).toBeVisible()` assertion passed because the test ID matched a different card already present in the target column. The regressions were only discovered six weeks later during a manual QA sprint.
Fix: For Pointer Events-based drag libraries, replace `page.dragAndDrop()` with a manual mouse simulation: `await page.mouse.move(srcX, srcY); await page.mouse.down(); for (const [x, y] of intermediatePoints) { await page.mouse.move(x, y, { steps: 5 }); } await page.mouse.move(tgtX, tgtY); await page.mouse.up();`. Verify which drag API the library uses before writing charters and add a comment in the test documenting whether it requires HTML DnD events or Pointer Events.

## Cycle 65 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 533** — `page.clock.setFixedTime()` + Date-Dependent UI Snapshot Diffing
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('dashboard shows correct fiscal-quarter label at quarter boundary', async ({ page }) => {
  // Pin time to the last millisecond of Q1 before the boundary
  await page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date('2026-03-31T23:59:59.999Z'));
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  const q1Label = await page.locator('[data-testid="fiscal-quarter-badge"]').textContent();
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'clock-anchor', value: '2026-03-31T23:59:59.999Z' });

  // Advance one millisecond into Q2
  await page.clock.setFixedTime(new Date('2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z'));
  await page.reload();
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  const q2Label = await page.locator('[data-testid="fiscal-quarter-badge"]').textContent();

  expect(q1Label).toMatch(/Q1/i);
  expect(q2Label).toMatch(/Q2/i);
  expect(q1Label).not.toBe(q2Label);
});
```
Tradeoff: `setFixedTime` freezes `Date.now()` while leaving `setTimeout`/`setInterval` on the real system clock, so this pattern is correct for pure date-rendering assertions but will silently fail to advance any timer-driven state machines (polling intervals, session-keep-alive pings) that run alongside the date display — for those scenarios use `page.clock.install()` + `page.clock.fastForward()` instead.

**Pattern 534** — `page.clock.install()` + `page.clock.runFor()` Tick-Granular Debounce Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('search input debounce fires exactly once after 300 ms of idle input', async ({ page }) => {
  // Clock must be installed before navigation to capture all registered timers
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z') });
  await page.goto('/search');

  const apiCalls: string[] = [];
  await page.route('**/api/search**', async route => {
    apiCalls.push(new URL(route.request().url()).searchParams.get('q') ?? '');
    await route.fulfill({ json: { results: [] } });
  });

  const input = page.locator('[data-testid="search-input"]');
  await input.pressSequentially('hello', { delay: 0 });

  // Advance 299 ms — debounce should not have fired yet
  await page.clock.runFor(299);
  expect(apiCalls).toHaveLength(0);

  // Advance 1 ms more — debounce threshold crossed
  await page.clock.runFor(1);
  expect(apiCalls).toHaveLength(1);
  expect(apiCalls[0]).toBe('hello');
});
```
Tradeoff: `runFor()` advances the mocked clock synchronously in the Node process but Playwright dispatches the resulting timer callbacks asynchronously into the browser context via CDP, so very tight tick sequences (< 5 ms between `runFor` calls) can occasionally reorder if the browser's event loop has unprocessed microtasks queued — use `await page.clock.runFor(0)` between assertions to flush pending microtasks before checking side effects.

**Pattern 535** — HAR Zip Bundle with Per-Endpoint Manual Override
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

test('product detail page renders mocked inventory badge', async ({ context, page }) => {
  // Route all API traffic through the committed HAR bundle
  await context.routeFromHAR(
    path.resolve(__dirname, '../fixtures/product-detail.har.zip'),
    {
      url: '**/api/**',
      // Fallback to real network for any unmatched routes so charter
      // does not silently miss new endpoints added after HAR was recorded
      notFound: 'fallback',
    }
  );

  // Override a single endpoint with a controlled low-stock response
  await page.route('**/api/inventory/42', async route => {
    await route.fulfill({
      contentType: 'application/json',
      body: JSON.stringify({ productId: 42, stock: 2, lowStockThreshold: 5 }),
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/products/42');
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="inventory-badge"]')).toContainText(/low stock/i);
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="inventory-badge"]')).toHaveCSS('background-color', /rgb\(220/);
});
```
Tradeoff: Layering a `page.route()` override on top of `context.routeFromHAR()` works because page-level routes take precedence over context-level routes, but the ordering guarantee only holds within the same Playwright version — if the team upgrades Playwright and the route precedence rules change, the manual override could silently stop taking effect while the HAR version of the endpoint is served instead, making the charter appear to pass while actually testing stale fixture data; pin the Playwright version in `package.json` and add an assertion that verifies the response body contains the controlled stock value.

**Pattern 536** — `context.routeFromHAR({ update: 'missing' })` Incremental HAR Hydration
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import path from 'path';

// Fixture: re-used across the charter file
const harPath = path.resolve(__dirname, '../fixtures/checkout-flow.har.zip');

test.use({
  contextOptions: async ({ contextOptions }, use) => {
    await use({
      ...contextOptions,
    });
  },
});

test('checkout flow — new shipping-estimate endpoint auto-hydrates HAR', async ({ context, page }) => {
  // 'missing' mode: replay known routes from HAR, record only new routes
  // This is safer than update:true which overwrites all entries
  await context.routeFromHAR(harPath, {
    url: '**/api/**',
    update: process.env.HYDRATE_HAR === 'true' ? 'missing' : false,
    notFound: process.env.HYDRATE_HAR === 'true' ? 'passthrough' : 'abort',
  });

  await page.goto('/checkout');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /calculate shipping/i }).click();
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="shipping-estimate"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 8000 });

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'har-mode',
    value: process.env.HYDRATE_HAR === 'true' ? 'hydrating-missing' : 'replay-only',
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: The `update: 'missing'` strategy prevents overwriting existing HAR entries with live data while still capturing new endpoints, but it requires a human reviewer to inspect the diff of the HAR zip before merging, because `'missing'` mode will record any unmatched route regardless of whether the test environment points at staging or production — a misconfigured `TEST_BASE_URL` can silently pollute the HAR with staging-specific response bodies that differ from the production schema.

**Pattern 537** — `route.fulfill()` with Delayed Response Body for Progress-Bar Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('file upload progress bar appears before server response completes', async ({ page }) => {
  let resolveBody!: (value: string) => void;
  const bodyReady = new Promise<string>(res => { resolveBody = res; });

  // Intercept the upload endpoint and simulate a slow response
  await page.route('**/api/upload', async route => {
    // Artificial first-byte delay simulates network latency
    await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200));
    await route.fulfill({
      status: 200,
      headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json', 'x-upload-id': 'test-42' },
      body: JSON.stringify({ uploadId: 'test-42', bytesReceived: 1048576, status: 'complete' }),
    });
    resolveBody('fulfilled');
  });

  await page.goto('/upload');
  const fileInput = page.locator('input[type="file"]');
  await fileInput.setInputFiles({ name: 'sample.pdf', mimeType: 'application/pdf', buffer: Buffer.alloc(1024) });
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /upload/i }).click();

  // Progress bar should appear before upload completes
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="upload-progress"]')).toBeVisible();
  await bodyReady;
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="upload-progress"]')).toContainText(/100%|complete/i);
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'upload-stub', value: 'route.fulfill 200ms delay' });
});
```
Tradeoff: Faking the upload response with `route.fulfill()` validates that the UI correctly interprets the response and updates the progress bar, but it completely bypasses the actual multipart form encoding and network chunking logic — if the application calculates upload progress from `XHR.upload.onprogress` events (which depend on real bytes being transmitted), the mocked route will fire the `100%` event immediately on response receipt, never exercising the intermediate progress states; for intermediate-progress chartering, use `page.evaluate()` to dispatch synthetic `ProgressEvent` objects on the XHR upload object directly.

**Pattern 538** — `page.route()` Fault-Injection Matrix for Resilience Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const faultMatrix = [
  { label: '503 Service Unavailable', status: 503, body: '{"error":"service_unavailable"}' },
  { label: '429 Rate Limited',        status: 429, body: '{"error":"rate_limit","retryAfter":60}' },
  { label: 'Network timeout abort',   status: null, abort: 'timedout' as const },
  { label: 'Empty body 200',          status: 200, body: '' },
] as const;

for (const fault of faultMatrix) {
  test(`dashboard handles ${fault.label} from recommendations API`, async ({ page }) => {
    await page.route('**/api/recommendations', async route => {
      if ('abort' in fault && fault.abort) {
        await route.abort(fault.abort);
      } else {
        await route.fulfill({ status: fault.status!, body: fault.body });
      }
    });

    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // The fallback empty-state card must render regardless of the fault type
    await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="recommendations-fallback"]'))
      .toBeVisible({ timeout: 6000 });
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'fault-injected', value: fault.label });
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Iterating `faultMatrix` with a `for...of` loop at module level generates test titles and registrations at collection time, which means adding a new fault entry to the array immediately appears in the test plan without any test body changes — the tradeoff is that parameterized tests generated this way cannot be individually retried by test title in the Playwright UI `--grep` filter unless the fault label is unique and grep-safe (no special regex characters), so always ensure `label` values avoid parentheses, asterisks, and pipe characters.

**Pattern 539** — `page.coverage.startJSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false })` Multi-Page SPA Bundle Audit
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('checkout SPA route transitions cover payment module entry point', async ({ page }) => {
  // Chromium-only: guard required in multi-browser projects
  const isCoverage = test.info().project.name === 'coverage-chromium';
  if (!isCoverage) test.skip();

  await page.coverage.startJSCoverage({ resetOnNavigation: false });

  // Navigate through multiple SPA routes to accumulate cross-route coverage
  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /proceed to checkout/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/checkout/shipping');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue to payment/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/checkout/payment');

  const coverageReport = await page.coverage.stopJSCoverage();

  const paymentBundle = coverageReport.find(entry => entry.url.includes('payment'));
  expect(paymentBundle, 'payment bundle must be loaded by payment step').toBeDefined();

  const totalBytes = paymentBundle!.text.length;
  const usedBytes = paymentBundle!.ranges.reduce((sum, r) => sum + (r.end - r.start), 0);
  const coveragePct = (usedBytes / totalBytes) * 100;

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'bundle-coverage',
    value: `payment.js: ${coveragePct.toFixed(1)}% (${usedBytes}/${totalBytes} bytes)`,
  });
  expect(coveragePct).toBeGreaterThan(40);
});
```
Tradeoff: Setting `resetOnNavigation: false` accumulates coverage across all SPA route changes into a single report, which is essential for lazy-loaded route bundles that only execute after navigation — the tradeoff is that accumulated coverage inflates apparent code execution because any byte range executed at any point during the session is marked used, even if that code path was only reachable during an error condition triggered on an earlier route; always reset coverage and re-measure per route when you need accurate per-route dead-code metrics rather than session-wide reachability.

**Pattern 540** — `page.coverage.startCSSCoverage()` Unused-Selector Density Heatmap
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('landing page CSS does not load more than 60% unused selectors', async ({ page }) => {
  if (test.info().project.name !== 'coverage-chromium') test.skip();

  await page.coverage.startCSSCoverage();
  await page.goto('/');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Expand interactive states to exercise hover/focus selector coverage
  await page.locator('[data-testid="primary-cta"]').hover();
  await page.keyboard.press('Tab'); // trigger :focus-visible selectors

  const cssReport = await page.coverage.stopCSSCoverage();

  for (const sheet of cssReport) {
    if (!sheet.url.includes('/static/')) continue; // skip CDN third-party sheets
    const totalChars = sheet.text!.length;
    const usedChars = sheet.ranges.reduce((sum, r) => sum + (r.end - r.start), 0);
    const unusedPct = ((totalChars - usedChars) / totalChars) * 100;
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'css-unused',
      value: `${new URL(sheet.url).pathname}: ${unusedPct.toFixed(1)}% unused`,
    });
    expect(unusedPct, `${sheet.url} has excessive unused CSS`).toBeLessThan(60);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: CSS coverage byte-ranges measure character positions within the raw stylesheet text, not the number of CSS rules or selectors — a single highly-verbose `@keyframes` block that is never triggered during the session counts as a large unused byte range and can inflate the unused percentage dramatically even when nearly all meaningful layout rules are exercised; supplement byte-range coverage with a selector-count audit using `document.styleSheets` iteration via `page.evaluate()` to get an accurate picture of how many distinct rules are dead versus active.

**Pattern 541** — `test.info().annotations` Charter Evidence Trail with Severity Tagging
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

async function recordFinding(
  severity: 'critical' | 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' | 'observation',
  title: string,
  detail: string
) {
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: `finding:${severity}`, value: `[${title}] ${detail}` });
}

test('CHARTER: account settings data persistence under rapid navigation', async ({ page }) => {
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter', value: 'Account Settings — Persistence Under Rapid Navigation' });
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-duration', value: '45min' });

  await page.goto('/settings/profile');
  await page.locator('[data-testid="display-name"]').fill('Rapid Nav Test User');

  // Rapid navigation away before save
  await page.goto('/dashboard');
  await page.goBack();

  const displayName = await page.locator('[data-testid="display-name"]').inputValue();
  if (displayName !== 'Rapid Nav Test User') {
    await recordFinding('high', 'unsaved-input-cleared', `display-name input value lost on back-navigation: got "${displayName}"`);
  }

  // Check for a browser-native "unsaved changes" dialog
  page.on('dialog', async dialog => {
    await recordFinding('observation', 'native-unsaved-dialog', `dialog appeared: "${dialog.message()}"`);
    await dialog.dismiss();
  });

  await page.goto('/settings/notifications');
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="notifications-heading"]')).toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: Annotating findings directly onto `test.info()` makes them visible in the Playwright HTML report without any external tooling, but annotations are appended at runtime and are therefore only present in the report if the test runs to completion — a test that crashes mid-charter due to an unhandled selector error will produce an incomplete annotation trail that silently omits any findings that would have been recorded after the crash point; wrap charter exploration blocks in `try/catch` and always call `recordFinding('critical', ...)` inside the `catch` block before rethrowing.

**Pattern 542** — `page.exposeFunction()` Real-Time Console Error Classifier
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('CHARTER: no unhandled promise rejections during full checkout flow', async ({ page }) => {
  const errors: Array<{ level: string; message: string; url: string }> = [];

  // Expose a Node-side collector that the browser calls on every console error
  await page.exposeFunction('__qaCollectError', (level: string, msg: string, url: string) => {
    errors.push({ level, message: msg, url });
  });

  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    const original = console.error.bind(console);
    console.error = (...args: unknown[]) => {
      window.__qaCollectError('error', args.map(String).join(' '), window.location.href);
      original(...args);
    };
    window.addEventListener('unhandledrejection', ev => {
      window.__qaCollectError('unhandledrejection', String(ev.reason), window.location.href);
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/cart');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /checkout/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/checkout/**');
  await page.locator('[data-testid="card-number"]').fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.locator('[data-testid="card-expiry"]').fill('12/28');
  await page.locator('[data-testid="card-cvc"]').fill('123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /place order/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/order-confirmation/**');

  errors.forEach(e => test.info().annotations.push({ type: `js-${e.level}`, value: `${e.url}: ${e.message}` }));
  const criticalErrors = errors.filter(e => e.level === 'unhandledrejection');
  expect(criticalErrors, 'No unhandled promise rejections during checkout').toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.exposeFunction()` serializes arguments through the CDP protocol as JSON, so Error objects passed to `console.error` are coerced to their `.toString()` representation (`"Error: message"`) before reaching Node — stack traces, `cause` chains, and non-enumerable properties on the Error are silently dropped, meaning the collected error messages may not contain the stack context needed to locate the bug; supplement the exposed function collector with `page.on('pageerror', ...)` which receives the full Error object with stack trace preserved by Playwright's CDP error event handling.
