**Pattern 543** — SBTM Session Sheet Metadata Injection via `test.info().annotations`
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface SBTMSession {
  charter: string;
  tester: string;
  build: string;
  startTime: string;
  area: string;
  durationMinutes: number;
}

function openSBTMSession(session: SBTMSession) {
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'sbtm:charter', value: session.charter });
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'sbtm:tester', value: session.tester });
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'sbtm:build', value: session.build });
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'sbtm:area', value: session.area });
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'sbtm:start', value: session.startTime });
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'sbtm:planned-duration', value: `${session.durationMinutes}m` });
}

test('SBTM: password-reset flow — token expiry boundary exploration', async ({ page }) => {
  openSBTMSession({
    charter: 'Explore password-reset token expiry: does UI handle expired, already-used, and malformed tokens gracefully?',
    tester: process.env.TESTER_ID ?? 'ci-agent',
    build: process.env.BUILD_ID ?? 'local',
    area: 'Authentication / Password Reset',
    startTime: new Date().toISOString(),
    durationMinutes: 45,
  });

  // Expired token charter
  await page.goto('/reset-password?token=expired-token-fixture');
  const heading = page.locator('h1, [role="heading"]');
  await expect(heading).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });
  const headingText = await heading.first().textContent();
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'sbtm:note', value: `expired-token heading: "${headingText}"` });

  // Already-used token charter
  await page.goto('/reset-password?token=used-token-fixture');
  const usedText = await heading.first().textContent();
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'sbtm:note', value: `used-token heading: "${usedText}"` });

  // Malformed token charter
  await page.goto('/reset-password?token=!!!invalid!!!');
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="error-message"], [role="alert"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'sbtm:coverage', value: 'expired, used, malformed token paths explored' });
});
```
Tradeoff: Embedding SBTM session metadata as annotations makes charter sheets queryable in the Playwright HTML report and extractable by `playwright/reporter` plugins, but Playwright's annotation key-value pairs are both plain strings with no type enforcement — the `sbtm:` prefix convention is purely by agreement and any contributor who omits the prefix or misspells a key will silently create orphaned annotations that do not aggregate with the rest of the session data in downstream reporting scripts; enforce annotation key conventions with a custom ESLint rule or a `afterEach` hook that validates the presence of all required `sbtm:` keys before the test result is emitted.

---

**Pattern 544** — `page.waitForResponse()` + Response Body Assertion for Silent API Contract Drift
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('CHARTER: user profile API contract — required fields present after save', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/settings/profile');

  // Arm the response watcher before triggering the action
  const saveResponsePromise = page.waitForResponse(
    resp => resp.url().includes('/api/profile') && resp.request().method() === 'PUT'
  );

  await page.locator('[data-testid="display-name"]').fill('Contract Test User');
  await page.locator('[data-testid="bio"]').fill('Testing API contract consistency.');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /save changes/i }).click();

  const saveResponse = await saveResponsePromise;
  const body = await saveResponse.json().catch(() => null);

  // Explicit contract assertions surfaced as charter findings
  const requiredFields = ['id', 'displayName', 'bio', 'updatedAt', 'avatarUrl'];
  for (const field of requiredFields) {
    const present = body !== null && field in body;
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: present ? 'contract:pass' : 'contract:missing-field',
      value: field,
    });
    expect(present, `API response missing required field: ${field}`).toBe(true);
  }

  expect(saveResponse.status()).toBe(200);
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'api-contract-version', value: saveResponse.headers()['x-api-version'] ?? 'unknown' });
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.waitForResponse()` matches on the first response whose URL and method match the predicate, so if the UI fires multiple `PUT /api/profile` calls in rapid succession (e.g., auto-save debounce plus manual save), only the first response is captured — the second response, which may differ in status or body, is silently ignored; use `page.on('response', ...)` listener accumulation with `Promise.all` to capture all matching responses when the charter needs to verify every response in a multi-call sequence.

---

**Pattern 545** — `context.addInitScript()` + `window.__flags` Charter-Controlled Feature Toggle
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

type FeatureFlags = {
  newCheckoutFlow: boolean;
  experimentalRecommendations: boolean;
  betaAccessibilityEnhancements: boolean;
};

async function withFlags(flags: Partial<FeatureFlags>, page: import('@playwright/test').Page) {
  await page.addInitScript((injectedFlags: Partial<FeatureFlags>) => {
    // Override the application's flag resolution before any app code runs
    Object.defineProperty(window, '__featureFlags', {
      get: () => ({
        newCheckoutFlow: false,
        experimentalRecommendations: false,
        betaAccessibilityEnhancements: false,
        ...injectedFlags,
      }),
      configurable: true,
    });
  }, flags);
}

test('CHARTER: new checkout flow — payment step renders without legacy fallback', async ({ page }) => {
  await withFlags({ newCheckoutFlow: true }, page);
  await page.goto('/cart');

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'feature-flags', value: JSON.stringify({ newCheckoutFlow: true }) });

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /checkout/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/checkout/**');

  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="new-payment-step"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 6000 });
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="legacy-payment-step"]')).not.toBeVisible();
});
```
Tradeoff: Injecting flags via `addInitScript()` with `Object.defineProperty` guarantees the override is in place before any application JavaScript executes, making it reliable for flags read during module initialisation — the tradeoff is that `configurable: true` is required to allow re-definition across page reloads within the same test, but if application code itself calls `Object.defineProperty(__featureFlags, ...)` to lock flags as non-configurable, the init script's override will throw a `TypeError: Cannot redefine property` that crashes the page silently and causes the charter test to fail with a misleading `page crashed` error rather than a flag-injection diagnostic.

---

**Pattern 546** — `page.ariaSnapshot()` Pre/Post Mutation Semantic Diff Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('CHARTER: modal open/close cycle preserves surrounding page ARIA tree', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/products');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Capture baseline ARIA snapshot before modal interaction
  const baselineSnapshot = await page.ariaSnapshot();
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'aria-baseline-length', value: String(baselineSnapshot.length) });

  // Open modal
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /filter products/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 4000 });
  const modalOpenSnapshot = await page.ariaSnapshot();

  // Close modal
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /close/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 4000 });
  const afterCloseSnapshot = await page.ariaSnapshot();

  // The dialog role must appear in open snapshot and not in closed snapshot
  expect(modalOpenSnapshot).toContain('dialog');
  expect(afterCloseSnapshot).not.toContain('dialog');

  // Structural parity: post-close tree should match baseline within acceptable variance
  const baselineLines = baselineSnapshot.split('\n').length;
  const afterCloseLines = afterCloseSnapshot.split('\n').length;
  const drift = Math.abs(baselineLines - afterCloseLines);
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'aria-tree-drift', value: `${drift} lines` });
  expect(drift, 'ARIA tree line count should be stable after modal close').toBeLessThanOrEqual(3);
});
```
Tradeoff: Comparing ARIA snapshots by line count is a lightweight proxy for structural parity but is brittle when the page renders dynamic content (live regions, notification badges, unread counts) that changes independently of the modal interaction — a single new notification arriving between baseline capture and post-close capture will add one line to `afterCloseSnapshot` and cause the drift assertion to fail with no indication that the failure is a false positive; use `expect.soft()` for the drift assertion and annotate the failure rather than aborting the charter, then manually review the annotation trail to distinguish structural regressions from expected dynamic-content churn.

---

**Pattern 547** — Charter Coverage Matrix via `test.info().annotations` + Reporter Aggregation
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

// Coverage matrix cell: each combination of (area x risk) is a charter cell
const charterMatrix = [
  { area: 'auth',     risk: 'session-fixation',   path: '/login',             method: 'POST /api/auth/login' },
  { area: 'auth',     risk: 'concurrent-sessions', path: '/settings/security', method: 'GET /api/sessions' },
  { area: 'payments', risk: 'idempotency',         path: '/checkout/payment',  method: 'POST /api/orders' },
  { area: 'payments', risk: 'currency-rounding',   path: '/cart',              method: 'GET /api/cart' },
] as const;

for (const cell of charterMatrix) {
  test(`CHARTER CELL [${cell.area}/${cell.risk}]: ${cell.path}`, async ({ page }) => {
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'matrix:area', value: cell.area });
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'matrix:risk', value: cell.risk });
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'matrix:path', value: cell.path });
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'matrix:method', value: cell.method });
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'matrix:status', value: 'exploring' });

    await page.goto(cell.path);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Baseline: page must load without JS errors for the cell to be charterable
    const errors: string[] = [];
    page.on('pageerror', e => errors.push(e.message));
    await page.waitForTimeout(500); // allow any deferred initialization errors to surface

    if (errors.length > 0) {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'matrix:blocker', value: errors.join('; ') });
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'matrix:status', value: 'blocked' });
    } else {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'matrix:status', value: 'explored' });
    }

    expect(errors, `JS errors on ${cell.path} block charter coverage`).toHaveLength(0);
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Generating charter matrix tests from a static array at module load time makes the full coverage matrix visible in the Playwright test list immediately (enabling coverage gap reporting without running any tests), but the matrix array is defined in TypeScript source and must be edited to add or remove cells — if a product manager maintains the risk register in a separate spreadsheet, the matrix array and spreadsheet will drift out of sync silently; eliminate the drift by reading the charter matrix from a JSON file at test collection time using `require()` and treating the JSON as the single source of truth, regenerating it from the spreadsheet in CI before the test run.

### Community Gotchas

**G95: `page.clock.setFixedTime()` does not affect `performance.now()` — timer-based animations and CSS transitions that use `performance.now()` as their internal clock source continue running against the real system monotonic clock, causing animation-state assertions to fail non-deterministically even after the date is frozen.**
Why this matters: A charter for a countdown-timer component called `page.clock.setFixedTime(targetDate)` to pin the displayed date and then used `expect(locator).toHaveText('00:00:00')` to assert the timer had expired. The test passed in isolation but failed intermittently in parallel CI runs. The countdown component rendered its initial value from `new Date()` (correctly frozen by `setFixedTime`) but drove the visual tick animation using a `requestAnimationFrame` loop that read `performance.now()` for smooth interpolation. Because `setFixedTime` does not mock `performance.now()`, the animation continued advancing on the real monotonic clock, and the text node was updated by the rAF loop to reflect the real elapsed time rather than the frozen date, producing values like `23:47:32` instead of `00:00:00`.
Fix: Use `page.clock.install()` instead of `page.clock.setFixedTime()` when the component under test uses `performance.now()`, `requestAnimationFrame`, or Web Animations API timing. `page.clock.install()` mocks all time sources including `performance.now()` and rAF callbacks. After installing, call `page.clock.pauseAt(targetTime)` to freeze all time sources simultaneously, then use `page.clock.runFor(0)` to flush pending rAF frames before asserting animation state.

---

**G96: `context.routeFromHAR()` silently falls through to real network when the HAR file path does not exist — there is no error thrown, and Playwright continues to make live requests, meaning a missing fixture file causes the test to make real network calls in CI without any indication that the HAR replay was not active.**
Why this matters: A team renamed their HAR fixtures directory from `fixtures/har/` to `fixtures/network/` during a file structure refactor. The `routeFromHAR()` calls still referenced the old path. Playwright did not throw an error — it silently fell through to real network for all matched routes. The tests continued to pass in local environments (because developers had local API servers running) and in staging CI (because the staging API was accessible), but failed only in the air-gapped production CI environment with timeout errors on network requests. The root cause took two days to identify because there were no warnings in the Playwright output about the missing HAR file.
Fix: Always verify HAR file existence before calling `context.routeFromHAR()` using `fs.existsSync(harPath)` and throw a descriptive error if the file is missing: `if (!fs.existsSync(harPath)) throw new Error('HAR fixture not found: ' + harPath)`. Add a CI lint step that greps test files for `routeFromHAR` calls and verifies each referenced path exists in the repository. Set `notFound: 'abort'` (the default) rather than `'fallback'` in all CI configurations so that unmatched routes cause the test to fail loudly rather than silently hitting real endpoints.

---

**G97: `test.info().annotations.push()` called inside a `page.on('request', ...)` or `page.on('response', ...)` event listener executes asynchronously and may not be flushed to the test report if the test completes before all pending CDP events have been processed — annotations added inside event callbacks can silently disappear from the HTML report.**
Why this matters: A charter used `page.on('response', async resp => { if (resp.status() >= 400) { test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'api-error', value: resp.url() }); } })` to record all error responses during a charter session. After the test completed, the HTML report showed zero `api-error` annotations even though the developer could see 404 responses in the browser's network tab. The event listener's callback was async and included an `await resp.json()` call to extract the error body — by the time the callback resumed after the `await`, the test had already finished and Playwright had serialized the test result, discarding any annotations pushed after result serialisation.
Fix: Collect annotations synchronously (without `await`) inside `page.on()` callbacks, or accumulate raw data into a local array and push to `test.info().annotations` in a synchronous block after `await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')` before the test's final assertions. If you must await inside the listener (e.g., to read the response body), track the promise in an array and `await Promise.all(pendingAnnotations)` before the test assertion phase.

---

**G98: `page.addInitScript()` registered on a `BrowserContext` does not re-run on iframes that are navigated independently after the main page load — cross-origin iframes that load after the initial page navigation, or iframes whose `src` is changed dynamically by JavaScript, will not have the init script injected and will run with the unpatched globals.**
Why this matters: A charter for an embedded payment iframe injected a `window.__qaPaymentStub` object via `context.addInitScript()` to intercept card tokenization calls. The payment iframe was loaded dynamically into the page 2 seconds after the main page load (triggered by a user clicking "Proceed to Payment"). Because the iframe was navigated after the init script had already run on the main frame, the iframe's `window` object was never patched — `window.__qaPaymentStub` was `undefined` inside the iframe, and all tokenization calls went to the real Stripe endpoint. The charter silently tested against the live payment API instead of the stub, and the test passed only because Stripe's test mode was active.
Fix: Register `page.addInitScript()` on the `Frame` object of the target iframe rather than on the context: obtain the frame with `page.frameLocator('[data-testid="payment-iframe"]').owner()` after the iframe has loaded, then call `frame.addInitScript(...)` and trigger a `frame.reload()` to re-run initialization with the script injected. Alternatively, intercept the iframe's source URL via `context.route()` and inject the stub as a script tag into the HTML response body, ensuring injection happens at parse time regardless of when the iframe is loaded.

---

**G99: `expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot()` baseline images are stored per test title and per `--project` name — if a test title contains dynamic content (timestamps, IDs, or counter values interpolated into the test name), every run generates a new baseline filename, causing the fixture directory to accumulate unlimited baseline files that are never cleaned up and can exhaust disk space on long-lived CI agents.**
Why this matters: A team parameterized a visual regression charter using a loop over product IDs fetched from an API at test collection time. The product IDs changed between sprints as products were added and retired. Each new product ID generated a new baseline screenshot filename (`charter-product-{id}-1.png`), and old IDs were never deleted because `toHaveScreenshot()` only creates new baselines — it never removes stale ones. After four sprints, the `__screenshots__` directory contained 847 PNG files totalling 2.3 GB. The CI agent's disk filled during a nightly run, causing unrelated tests to fail with `ENOSPC` errors that had no obvious connection to the screenshot accumulation.
Fix: Never interpolate runtime-variable values (fetched IDs, timestamps, random seeds) directly into test titles used with `toHaveScreenshot()`. Use a fixed, semantically meaningful test title and pass variant data as a `toHaveScreenshot(name)` argument with a controlled naming scheme (e.g., `toHaveScreenshot('product-slot-' + slotIndex + '.png')`). Add a CI maintenance step that runs `find __screenshots__ -name "*.png" -mtime +30 -delete` weekly to remove baselines older than 30 days, and commit baseline cleanup as part of the sprint-close checklist.

## Cycle 66 — 2026-05-14

### Patterns

**Pattern 548** — `page.routeWebSocket()` Frame-Order Injection for Chat Message Sequencing
```typescript
test('charter: out-of-order WebSocket frames expose race condition in chat renderer', async ({ page }) => {
  const frames: string[] = [];
  const DELAY_MS = 80;

  await page.routeWebSocket('wss://chat.example.com/ws', (ws) => {
    ws.onmessage = async (message) => {
      const data = JSON.parse(message.toString());
      frames.push(data.id);
      if (data.type === 'chat' && frames.length % 3 === 0) {
        // Inject a synthetic duplicate before forwarding to stress the deduplication logic
        const duplicate = { ...data, injected: true };
        ws.send(JSON.stringify(duplicate));
      }
      // Introduce artificial reorder: delay every second frame
      if (frames.indexOf(data.id) % 2 === 1) {
        await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, DELAY_MS));
      }
      ws.send(message);
    };
  });

  await page.goto('/chat/room/42');
  await page.getByRole('textbox', { name: /message/i }).fill('hello');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /send/i }).click();

  // Verify the message list renders in insertion order despite injected reordering
  const messages = page.locator('[data-testid="message-list"] [data-testid^="msg-"]');
  await expect(messages.nth(0)).toBeVisible();
  const count = await messages.count();
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'ws-frames', value: `received: ${frames.length}, rendered: ${count}` });
  // Duplicate injection should NOT produce extra rendered rows
  expect(count, 'renderer must deduplicate injected frames').toBeLessThanOrEqual(frames.length / 2 + 1);
});
```
Tradeoff: Routing at the WebSocket level with `page.routeWebSocket()` intercepts all frames globally for the page, so injecting artificial delays via `setTimeout` inside the route handler blocks the same Node.js event-loop tick that processes real frames — if the delay exceeds the server's keep-alive ping interval (commonly 30 s but often as low as 5 s on mobile gateways), the server will close the socket before the delayed frames are forwarded, converting a reorder charter into an unexpected disconnect charter; keep injected delays below 500 ms and verify that the target gateway's keep-alive interval is at least 2× the maximum injected delay before using this pattern in CI.

---

**Pattern 549** — `context.setGeolocation()` + `context.grantPermissions()` Location-Boundary Charter
```typescript
test('charter: store-locator proximity boundary returns correct result sets', async ({ browser }) => {
  // Coordinates spanning inside, on-boundary, and outside a 50 km radius from San Francisco centre
  const BOUNDARY_COORDS: Array<{ label: string; coords: { latitude: number; longitude: number } }> = [
    { label: 'inside-1m',     coords: { latitude: 37.7749,  longitude: -122.4194 } },   // city centre
    { label: 'boundary-50km', coords: { latitude: 37.3387,  longitude: -121.8853 } },   // ~49.8 km
    { label: 'outside-51km',  coords: { latitude: 37.3300,  longitude: -121.8700 } },   // ~51.2 km
  ];

  for (const { label, coords } of BOUNDARY_COORDS) {
    const context = await browser.newContext({
      permissions: ['geolocation'],
      geolocation: coords,
    });
    const page = await context.newPage();

    await page.goto('/stores');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /use my location/i }).click();
    await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="store-list-item"]', { state: 'visible', timeout: 8000 })
      .catch(() => null); // may not appear for outside-boundary case

    const storeCount = await page.locator('[data-testid="store-list-item"]').count();
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'geo-boundary', value: `${label}: ${storeCount} stores` });

    if (label === 'outside-51km') {
      await expect(page.getByText(/no stores found/i)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });
    } else {
      expect(storeCount, `${label} should show at least one store`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
    await context.close();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Creating a fresh `browser.newContext()` per coordinate set guarantees each geolocation is active before `page.goto()` executes — the alternative of calling `context.setGeolocation()` mid-session after navigation is unreliable because the Geolocation API caches the last-granted position for the lifetime of a `getCurrentPosition()` call already in flight; the per-context approach costs ~120 ms of context spin-up overhead per coordinate, so chartering 50+ boundary points in a loop doubles total suite time compared to reusing a single context, making this pattern unsuitable for wide geographic fuzzing beyond ~20 boundary cases.

---

**Pattern 550** — `page.on('pageerror')` Continuous JavaScript Error Accumulation Across Multi-Step Charter
```typescript
test('charter: multi-step checkout accumulates zero unhandled JS errors end-to-end', async ({ page }) => {
  const jsErrors: Array<{ message: string; step: string }> = [];
  let currentStep = 'init';

  // Register before first navigation to catch module-initializer errors
  page.on('pageerror', (error) => {
    jsErrors.push({ message: error.message, step: currentStep });
  });

  await page.goto('/checkout');

  currentStep = 'cart-review';
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /proceed to checkout/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/checkout/address');

  currentStep = 'address-entry';
  await page.getByLabel(/street address/i).fill('123 Main St');
  await page.getByLabel(/city/i).fill('Springfield');
  await page.getByLabel(/zip/i).fill('62701');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /continue to payment/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/checkout/payment');

  currentStep = 'payment';
  await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4111111111111111');
  await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('12/27');
  await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).fill('123');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /place order/i }).click();
  await page.waitForURL('**/checkout/confirmation');

  currentStep = 'confirmation';
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /order confirmed/i })).toBeVisible();

  if (jsErrors.length > 0) {
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'js-errors', value: JSON.stringify(jsErrors, null, 2) });
  }
  expect(jsErrors, 'no unhandled JS errors during checkout charter').toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Attaching `page.on('pageerror')` before the first navigation captures every unhandled error for the full lifetime of the page, making the listener a reliable cross-step accumulator without polling — however, `pageerror` fires for errors on all frames including sandboxed third-party iframes (payment widgets, analytics scripts), so a charter testing only first-party code will see unrelated vendor errors and must filter by `error.stack` origin before asserting; failing to filter converts a first-party clean run into a noisy failure caused by a transient third-party CDN error outside the team's control.

---

**Pattern 551** — `AxeBuilder.include()` Focused WCAG 2.2 Component-Level Accessibility Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';
import AxeBuilder from '@axe-core/playwright';

test('charter: modal dialog meets WCAG 2.2 AA — focus trap, role, and label', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/components/modal-demo');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('dialog')).toBeVisible();

  // Scope axe to the modal only; exclude known third-party badge rendered inside the dialog
  const results = await new AxeBuilder({ page })
    .include('[role="dialog"]')
    .exclude('[data-testid="third-party-badge"]')
    .withTags(['wcag2a', 'wcag2aa', 'wcag21aa', 'wcag22aa'])
    .analyze();

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'axe-violations',
    value: JSON.stringify(
      results.violations.map((v) => ({ id: v.id, impact: v.impact, nodes: v.nodes.length })),
      null, 2
    ),
  });

  // Verify keyboard focus is trapped inside the dialog after open
  const activeTag = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.tagName ?? '');
  expect(['BUTTON', 'INPUT', 'A', 'TEXTAREA', 'SELECT']).toContain(activeTag);

  // Verify dialog carries an accessible name via labelledby or label attribute
  const labelledby = await page.getByRole('dialog').getAttribute('aria-labelledby');
  const label      = await page.getByRole('dialog').getAttribute('aria-label');
  expect(labelledby ?? label, 'dialog must have accessible name').not.toBeNull();

  expect(results.violations, 'no WCAG 2.2 AA violations inside modal dialog').toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Scoping `AxeBuilder.include()` to `[role="dialog"]` reduces axe rule evaluation time from ~800 ms for a full-page scan to ~120 ms — the tradeoff is that violations on elements outside the modal boundary (e.g., the trigger button's color contrast in the parent page) are invisible to the scoped scan; always pair a component-level charter with at least one full-page scan in the same suite to catch cross-boundary violations.

---

**Pattern 552** — `context.tracing.start/stop` On-Demand Trace Capture Keyed to Charter Phase Outcome
```typescript
test('charter: payment retry flow — trace capture gates on decline-card detection', async ({ context, page }) => {
  let traceActive = false;

  await context.tracing.start({ screenshots: true, snapshots: true, sources: true });
  traceActive = true;

  await page.goto('/checkout/payment');
  await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4000000000000002'); // Stripe test decline card
  await page.getByLabel(/expiry/i).fill('12/26');
  await page.getByLabel(/cvv/i).fill('456');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();

  const declineVisible = await page
    .getByRole('alert').filter({ hasText: /declined/i })
    .isVisible({ timeout: 6000 }).catch(() => false);

  if (!declineVisible) {
    // Unexpected success — dump trace immediately for investigation
    await context.tracing.stop({ path: `traces/unexpected-success-${Date.now()}.zip` });
    traceActive = false;
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'unexpected-path', value: 'decline card accepted payment' });
  }

  expect(declineVisible, 'test card 4000000000000002 must trigger decline notice').toBe(true);

  // Retry with an approved card
  await page.getByLabel(/card number/i).fill('4242424242424242');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /pay now/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByRole('heading', { name: /payment successful/i })).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10000 });

  if (traceActive) {
    await context.tracing.stop({ path: `traces/payment-retry-${Date.now()}.zip` });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Starting a trace with `screenshots: true` and `snapshots: true` produces 15–40 MB artefacts for a 20-action checkout charter — this is acceptable for targeted charters, but unconditional tracing across a 50-test suite can exceed 2 GB of CI artefact storage per run; adopt a convention of explicitly calling `context.tracing.start()` only in tests tagged `@charter` while using `trace: 'on-first-retry'` as the project default for regression tests.

---

**Pattern 553** — `locator.dragTo()` vs `mouse.down/move/up` Gap Charter for HTML5 Drag Events
```typescript
test('charter: kanban card move — detect HTML5 drag API vs pointer-event API mismatch', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/kanban');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="kanban-board"]', { state: 'visible' });

  const card = page.locator('[data-testid="kanban-card"]').first();
  const targetColumn = page.locator('[data-testid="kanban-column"]').nth(2);
  const cardText = await card.textContent();

  // Strategy 1: high-level locator.dragTo() — dispatches pointer events only
  await card.dragTo(targetColumn);
  const movedViaHighLevel =
    (await targetColumn.locator('[data-testid="kanban-card"]').filter({ hasText: cardText ?? '' }).count()) > 0;
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'drag-high-level', value: movedViaHighLevel ? 'SUCCESS' : 'FAIL' });

  if (!movedViaHighLevel) {
    // Strategy 2: low-level mouse events — triggers HTML5 dragstart / dragover / drop
    const src = await card.boundingBox();
    const dst = await targetColumn.boundingBox();
    if (src && dst) {
      await page.mouse.move(src.x + src.width / 2, src.y + src.height / 2);
      await page.mouse.down();
      for (let i = 1; i <= 10; i++) {
        await page.mouse.move(
          src.x + (dst.x - src.x) * (i / 10) + dst.width / 2,
          src.y + (dst.y - src.y) * (i / 10) + dst.height / 2,
          { steps: 1 }
        );
      }
      await page.mouse.up();
    }
    const movedViaLowLevel =
      (await targetColumn.locator('[data-testid="kanban-card"]').filter({ hasText: cardText ?? '' }).count()) > 0;
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'drag-low-level', value: movedViaLowLevel ? 'SUCCESS' : 'FAIL' });
    expect(movedViaLowLevel || movedViaHighLevel, 'card must be movable via at least one drag strategy').toBe(true);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `locator.dragTo()` dispatches pointer events but NOT the HTML5 `dragstart/dragover/drop/dragend` event set — applications built on React DnD or native `draggable="true"` handlers silently ignore `locator.dragTo()` and the test completes without the card moving; the low-level `mouse.*` approach fires HTML5 events but moves in a straight line, failing to trigger auto-scroll behaviors in oversized boards; both strategies leave auto-scroll charter coverage incomplete.

**Pattern 554** — `page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme })` Dark-Mode Visual Regression Charter
```typescript
test('charter: dashboard renders correctly under both light and dark color schemes', async ({ page }) => {
  for (const scheme of ['light', 'dark'] as const) {
    await page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: scheme });
    await page.goto('/dashboard');
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

    // Wait for any scheme-change toast to clear before screenshotting
    const toast = page.getByRole('status');
    if (await toast.isVisible()) {
      await toast.waitFor({ state: 'hidden', timeout: 3000 });
    }

    await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot(`dashboard-${scheme}.png`, {
      fullPage: true,
      animations: 'disabled',
      maxDiffPixels: 50,
    });

    // Spot-check: dark mode body must not be white
    if (scheme === 'dark') {
      const bg = await page.evaluate(() => getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor);
      expect(bg, 'dark mode body background must not be white').not.toBe('rgb(255, 255, 255)');
    }

    const headingColor = await page.getByRole('heading', { level: 1 }).evaluate(
      (el) => getComputedStyle(el).color
    );
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: `heading-color-${scheme}`, value: headingColor });
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.emulateMedia({ colorScheme: 'dark' })` correctly triggers CSS `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` rules — but applications that persist theme choice in `localStorage` and apply `data-theme="dark"` to the `<html>` element will NOT respond because their JS reads storage, not the media query; for such apps the charter must also inject `localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark')` via `context.addInitScript()` before navigation, otherwise the emulation has no visible effect and the dark-mode screenshot silently captures the light theme.

**Pattern 555** — `page.on('console')` Structured Console-Error Accumulator with Severity Bucketing
```typescript
test('charter: SPA navigation accumulates no console errors or CSP violations across 5 routes', async ({ page }) => {
  type Bucket = { errors: string[]; warnings: string[]; forbidden: string[] };
  const log: Bucket = { errors: [], warnings: [], forbidden: [] };

  const FORBIDDEN = [/Content Security Policy/i, /Cross-Origin/i, /Failed to load resource/i];

  page.on('console', (msg) => {
    const text = msg.text();
    if (msg.type() === 'error')   log.errors.push(text);
    if (msg.type() === 'warning') log.warnings.push(text);
    if (FORBIDDEN.some((re) => re.test(text))) log.forbidden.push(`[${msg.type()}] ${text}`);
  });

  for (const route of ['/dashboard', '/profile', '/settings', '/reports', '/help']) {
    await page.goto(route);
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
  }

  test.info().annotations.push({
    type: 'console-summary',
    value: `errors:${log.errors.length} warnings:${log.warnings.length} forbidden:${log.forbidden.length}`,
  });

  expect(log.errors,   'no console errors across navigation charter').toHaveLength(0);
  expect(log.forbidden, 'no CSP/CORS/resource violations').toHaveLength(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.on('console')` captures messages from the main frame and all same-origin iframes — when running against a development build, React prop-type warnings are emitted as `console.error()` calls that are stripped in production; these inflate the error count and produce false failures on dev builds; always run console-error charters against a `NODE_ENV=production`-equivalent build, or add a `msg.location().url` filter to skip messages originating from `webpack-internal://` and `react-dom` module paths.

**Pattern 556** — `locator.setInputFiles()` with In-Memory Buffer for File-Type Boundary Charter
```typescript
test('charter: file upload enforces size limit and MIME-type allowlist', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/documents/upload');

  const cases = [
    { label: 'valid-pdf',    name: 'report.pdf',  mime: 'application/pdf',          bytes: 512_000,   reject: false },
    { label: 'oversized',    name: 'large.pdf',   mime: 'application/pdf',          bytes: 6_000_000, reject: true  },
    { label: 'exe-as-pdf',   name: 'bad.pdf',     mime: 'application/x-msdownload', bytes: 1_024,     reject: true  },
    { label: 'allowed-svg',  name: 'chart.svg',   mime: 'image/svg+xml',            bytes: 2_048,     reject: false },
    { label: 'blocked-heic', name: 'photo.heic',  mime: 'image/heic',               bytes: 3_000_000, reject: true  },
  ];

  for (const { label, name, mime, bytes, reject } of cases) {
    const buffer = Buffer.alloc(bytes, 0xaa); // uniform fill — no disk I/O required

    await page.locator('input[type="file"]').setInputFiles({ name, mimeType: mime, buffer });
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /upload/i }).click();

    if (reject) {
      await expect(
        page.getByRole('alert').filter({ hasText: /(too large|unsupported|not allowed)/i })
      ).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });
    } else {
      await expect(
        page.getByRole('status').filter({ hasText: /uploaded/i })
      ).toBeVisible({ timeout: 8000 });
    }

    test.info().annotations.push({ type: `upload-${label}`, value: reject ? 'rejected' : 'accepted' });
    await page.reload();
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: `Buffer.alloc(bytes, 0xaa)` avoids disk I/O and makes 6 MB boundary tests fast in CI — however, the uniform-fill buffer contains no valid magic bytes, so a server that performs content-based MIME sniffing will reject the synthetic PDF as an unrecognized binary even on the happy path; for magic-byte-sniffing servers the charter must prepend the correct file signature (e.g., `%PDF-1.4` for PDF, `\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n` for PNG) to the buffer, otherwise false rejections obscure the actual MIME-type boundary behavior under test.

**Pattern 557** — `expect(page).toHaveScreenshot()` + `page.addStyleTag()` Deterministic Visual Charter
```typescript
test('charter: pricing table renders consistently with volatile content suppressed', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/pricing');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  // Suppress animations and hide runtime-volatile elements before capture
  await page.addStyleTag({
    content: `
      *, *::before, *::after { animation: none !important; transition: none !important; }
      [data-testid="live-user-count"],
      [data-testid="last-updated-timestamp"],
      [data-testid="ad-banner"],
      iframe { visibility: hidden !important; }
    `,
  });

  // Wait for all lazy images to finish loading
  await page.waitForFunction(() =>
    Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img')).every((i) => (i as HTMLImageElement).complete)
  );

  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="plan-card"]')).toHaveCount(3);

  await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('pricing-table-baseline.png', {
    clip: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 1280, height: 900 },
    maxDiffPixels: 0,
    animations: 'disabled',
  });

  // Expand Enterprise accordion and capture expanded state
  await page.locator('[data-testid="plan-card"]').last()
    .getByRole('button', { name: /see features/i }).click();
  await expect(
    page.locator('[data-testid="plan-card"]').last().locator('[data-testid="feature-list"]')
  ).toBeVisible();

  await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('pricing-table-enterprise-expanded.png', {
    clip: { x: 0, y: 0, width: 1280, height: 1200 },
    maxDiffPixels: 0,
    animations: 'disabled',
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Injecting a `<style>` tag inside the test keeps suppression logic version-controlled alongside the charter without affecting other tests — the tradeoff is that `page.addStyleTag()` inserts a DOM element captured by traces and `page.content()`, so any assertion on raw HTML that runs after the tag insertion will see the injected styles; if the same page instance is reused for subsequent structural assertions, remove the tag explicitly via `page.evaluate(() => document.querySelector('style:last-of-type')?.remove())` before those assertions.

**Pattern 558** — `context.route()` Artificial Latency Injection via `setTimeout` Inside `fulfill`
```typescript
test('charter: data table shows skeleton loader under simulated 3G latency (~400 ms)', async ({ context, page }) => {
  const LATENCY_MS = 400;
  const hit: string[] = [];

  await context.route('**/api/v1/table-data**', async (route) => {
    hit.push(route.request().url());
    const response = await route.fetch();
    const json = await response.json();
    await new Promise<void>((r) => setTimeout(r, LATENCY_MS));
    await route.fulfill({
      status: response.status(),
      headers: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(response.headers())),
      body: JSON.stringify(json),
    });
  });

  await page.goto('/data-table');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /load data/i }).click();

  // Skeleton must appear within 200 ms of the button click
  const skeleton = page.getByTestId('table-skeleton-loader');
  await expect(skeleton).toBeVisible({ timeout: 200 });

  // Skeleton must disappear and real rows appear after the injected delay resolves
  await expect(skeleton).toBeHidden({ timeout: LATENCY_MS + 2000 });
  await expect(page.locator('[data-testid="table-row"]').first()).toBeVisible({ timeout: 1000 });

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'intercepted', value: `${hit.length} request(s)` });
  expect(hit.length, 'table-data route must be intercepted').toBeGreaterThan(0);
});
```
Tradeoff: Fetching the real response with `route.fetch()` and then re-fulfilling with added delay avoids fixture maintenance — the tradeoff is that total effective latency is `real_network_RTT + LATENCY_MS`; on remote CI runners with variable server latency, this can cause total timeout of `test.timeout()` to be exceeded; set `test.slow()` on all latency-injection charters and confirm that `test.timeout()` is at least `3 × (LATENCY_MS + worst-case_server_RTT)` to prevent flaky CI failures.

**Pattern 559** — `page.keyboard.press()` Modifier-Key Combination Charter for Shortcut Accessibility
```typescript
test('charter: editor keyboard shortcuts trigger correct actions and pass hard-assert on save', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/editor');
  await page.waitForSelector('[data-testid="editor-canvas"]', { state: 'visible' });
  await page.getByTestId('editor-canvas').click();

  const shortcuts = [
    { keys: 'Control+z',       action: 'undo',       selector: '[data-testid="undo-indicator"]'      },
    { keys: 'Control+Shift+z', action: 'redo',       selector: '[data-testid="redo-indicator"]'      },
    { keys: 'Control+s',       action: 'save',       selector: '[data-testid="save-toast"]'          },
    { keys: 'Control+a',       action: 'select-all', selector: '[data-testid="selection-count"]'     },
    { keys: 'Escape',          action: 'deselect',   selector: '[data-testid="editor-canvas"]'       },
    { keys: 'Control+/',       action: 'open-help',  selector: '[role="dialog"][aria-label*="help"]' },
  ];

  for (const { keys, action, selector } of shortcuts) {
    await page.keyboard.press(keys);
    const appeared = await page.locator(selector).first().isVisible({ timeout: 2000 }).catch(() => false);
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: `shortcut-${action}`, value: appeared ? 'OK' : 'NOT-TRIGGERED' });
    if (!appeared) {
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter-finding', value: `"${keys}" (${action}) not triggered` });
    }
  }

  // Hard assert only on the save shortcut — business-critical path
  await page.keyboard.press('Control+s');
  await expect(page.getByTestId('save-toast')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.keyboard.press('Control+s')` dispatches a native keyboard event that the OS/browser may intercept before the application handler fires — on macOS, `Meta+s` triggers the browser's native Save Page As dialog, stealing the event from the application's `keydown` listener; always branch on `process.platform === 'darwin'` and substitute `Meta` for `Control` in the shortcut table, or the macOS CI job will crash with an unexpected OS dialog.

**Pattern 560** — `page.addInitScript()` + `PerformanceObserver` LCP Timing Capture During Charter
```typescript
test('charter: landing page LCP remains under 2.5 s on simulated 4G connection', async ({ page, context }) => {
  // Simulate 4G: ~30 ms per-resource base latency
  await context.route('**/*', async (route) => {
    await new Promise<void>((r) => setTimeout(r, 30));
    await route.continue();
  });

  // Install PerformanceObserver before navigation to capture LCP from the first paint
  await page.addInitScript(() => {
    (window as unknown as Record<string, unknown[]>)['__lcpEntries'] = [];
    const obs = new PerformanceObserver((list) => {
      for (const e of list.getEntries()) {
        (window as unknown as Record<string, unknown[]>)['__lcpEntries'].push(e.toJSON());
      }
    });
    obs.observe({ type: 'largest-contentful-paint', buffered: true });
  });

  const t0 = Date.now();
  await page.goto('/', { waitUntil: 'networkidle' });
  const wallMs = Date.now() - t0;

  const entries = await page.evaluate(
    () => (window as unknown as Record<string, unknown[]>)['__lcpEntries'] ?? []
  ) as Array<{ startTime?: number }>;

  const lcpMs = entries.at(-1)?.startTime ?? wallMs;
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'lcp-ms', value: `LCP: ${lcpMs.toFixed(0)} ms, wall: ${wallMs} ms` });

  expect(lcpMs, 'LCP must be under 2500 ms on simulated 4G').toBeLessThan(2500);
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.addInitScript()` registers the observer before page scripts run, ensuring no LCP entries are missed — but injecting 30 ms latency per resource via `context.route()` creates O(n) overhead where n is the total resource count (a page with 80 resources adds 2,400 ms of artificial latency on top of real server time); run performance-charter tests in a dedicated `workers: 1` Playwright project with `test.setTimeout(45_000)` to prevent contention and timeout failures.

---

**Pattern 561** — `page.waitForResponse()` with Predicate for GraphQL Operation Name Charter
```typescript
test('charter: product search GraphQL query handles valid, empty, and no-match inputs', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/search');

  const cases = [
    { q: 'laptop',       expectHits: true  },
    { q: '',             expectHits: false  },
    { q: '   ',          expectHits: false  },
    { q: 'zzzzzzzzzz',   expectHits: false  },
  ];

  for (const { q, expectHits } of cases) {
    const responsePromise = page.waitForResponse(
      (resp) => {
        if (!resp.url().includes('/graphql')) return false;
        try {
          const body = resp.request().postDataJSON() as { operationName?: string } | null;
          return body?.operationName === 'SearchProducts';
        } catch { return false; }
      },
      { timeout: 8000 }
    );

    await page.getByRole('searchbox').fill(q);
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /search/i }).click();
    const resp = await responsePromise;
    const json = await resp.json() as { data?: { searchProducts?: { total?: number } } };
    const total = json.data?.searchProducts?.total ?? 0;
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: `gql-${q || 'empty'}`, value: `total: ${total}` });

    if (expectHits) {
      expect(total, `query "${q}" should return results`).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    } else {
      await expect(page.getByText(/no results/i)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });
    }
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Matching `page.waitForResponse()` by `operationName` in the POST body enables precise per-operation interception without matching every `/graphql` request — the tradeoff is that `postDataJSON()` parses the full request body on every `/graphql` response (including background mutations and subscriptions), adding CPU overhead proportional to request frequency; mitigate with a fast pre-filter `resp.url().includes('/graphql') && resp.request().method() === 'POST'` before invoking `postDataJSON()`, and add an early-exit `body?.operationName?.startsWith('Search')` check before the full equality test.

---

**Pattern 562** — `context.clearPermissions()` + Re-Grant Permission State Reset for Consent-Flow Charter
```typescript
test('charter: notification permission prompt re-appears after browser-level revocation', async ({ browser }) => {
  const ctx = await browser.newContext({ permissions: ['notifications'] });
  const page = await ctx.newPage();

  // Phase 1: grant and verify subscription flow
  await page.goto('/notifications/setup');
  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /enable notifications/i }).click();
  await expect(page.getByText(/notifications enabled/i)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'phase1', value: 'granted-OK' });

  // Phase 2: simulate user revoking in browser settings
  await ctx.clearPermissions();
  await page.reload();
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const reEnablePrompt = page
    .getByRole('dialog').filter({ hasText: /re-enable notifications/i })
    .or(page.getByRole('alert').filter({ hasText: /permission revoked/i }));

  const promptShown = await reEnablePrompt.isVisible({ timeout: 5000 }).catch(() => false);
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'phase2', value: promptShown ? 'prompt-shown' : 'prompt-missing' });

  // Phase 3: re-grant and verify recovery without sign-out
  await ctx.grantPermissions(['notifications']);
  await page.reload();
  await expect(page.getByText(/notifications enabled/i)).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'phase3', value: 'recovered-OK' });

  await ctx.close();
  expect(promptShown, 'app must prompt user to re-enable after permission revocation').toBe(true);
});
```
Tradeoff: `context.clearPermissions()` resets all browser-level permissions to the default "prompt" state without navigating — however, applications that cache `notifications: granted` in `localStorage` or `IndexedDB` at grant time will not detect the revocation because they never re-query `Notification.permission` after reload; the charter must separately assert `page.evaluate(() => Notification.permission)` to distinguish the browser state from the application's cached state, and the architectural fix is to re-query `Notification.permission` on every page-focus event rather than relying solely on the stored grant flag.

---

### Community Gotchas

**G100: `context.setGeolocation()` is silently ignored when the `geolocation` permission has not been granted — the Geolocation API returns `PositionError.code === 1` (PERMISSION_DENIED) to the application regardless of the coordinates set, and Playwright emits no warning.**
Why this matters: A charter for a store-locator feature called `await context.setGeolocation({ latitude: 37.77, longitude: -122.41 })` immediately before clicking "Use My Location". The app's `navigator.geolocation.getCurrentPosition()` error callback fired with `PERMISSION_DENIED` silently, and the store list never populated. The charter logged no assertion failure because the list container element (`[data-testid="store-list"]`) was already present in the DOM from the server-rendered static state — it was never cleared on a permission error. The charter reported a false pass for three sprints while the feature was broken for all users who had not pre-granted the permission.
Fix: Always pair `context.setGeolocation()` with `await context.grantPermissions(['geolocation'])` before the first navigation, or set `permissions: ['geolocation']` in the `browser.newContext()` options. Add an assertion that verifies the geolocation-dependent UI element actually changes state (e.g., the dynamic store count increases above the static server-rendered baseline of zero) rather than simply checking for the container's existence.

---

**G101: `page.on('pageerror')` fires asynchronously via CDP and can miss JavaScript exceptions thrown synchronously during `page.goto()` if the listener is attached after the navigation promise settles.**
Why this matters: A charter test attached `page.on('pageerror', ...)` on line 3, then called `page.goto('/app')` on line 4. A critical `TypeError` was thrown in the application's module initializer during the early page-load phase. Because the error was delivered to Playwright via the CDP `Runtime.exceptionThrown` event during the same microtask queue flush that resolved the `goto()` promise, the listener missed the error on approximately 30% of CI runs depending on event-loop scheduling — making the charter flaky rather than reliably detecting the initialization bug.
Fix: Attach `page.on('pageerror', ...)` before calling `page.goto()`. For errors that occur before the CDP `Runtime.enable` acknowledgement (very early module initializer errors), also install a `window.onerror` capture via `context.addInitScript()` that pushes into a `window.__earlyErrors` array, then read that array after navigation with `await page.evaluate(() => window.__earlyErrors)`. This two-layer approach closes the window between page creation and the first CDP event.

---

**G102: `locator.dragTo()` does not dispatch HTML5 `dragstart`, `drag`, `dragenter`, `dragover`, `drop`, or `dragend` events — applications built on the native HTML5 Drag and Drop API silently ignore `locator.dragTo()` and the drag completes without moving anything, while the test passes with no error.**
Why this matters: A team used `locator.dragTo()` on a sortable list backed by native `draggable="true"` and `ondrop` handlers. The call completed without error, the `await` resolved, and the subsequent assertion `expect(items.first()).toHaveText('Item B')` passed because the unchanged list still had "Item A" first — the assertion was checking the wrong index. The regression was discovered only in a manual QA session two sprints later after the draggable feature had shipped broken to production.
Fix: Before writing a drag charter, determine the drag implementation: `draggable="true"` + `ondragstart/ondrop` = HTML5 API (requires `page.dispatchEvent()` or `mouse.down/move/up`); CSS `cursor: grab` + pointer-event listeners = Pointer Events API (`locator.dragTo()` works). Document the confirmed API type in `test.info().annotations` so future maintainers know which strategy to use. Never rely on a silent `locator.dragTo()` success as evidence that the drag actually moved the element.

---

**G103: `expect(page).toHaveScreenshot()` baselines are stored per OS because font rendering, anti-aliasing, and subpixel hinting differ between Linux, macOS, and Windows — baselines generated on macOS will always fail on Linux CI even for pixel-perfect identical HTML.**
Why this matters: A developer ran `npx playwright test --update-snapshots` locally on macOS to generate the initial visual baselines, then committed the `.png` files. The first Linux CI run failed every visual assertion with `Screenshot comparison failed` and a diff highlighting subtle font-weight differences — FreeType on Linux renders text with different subpixel hinting than CoreText on macOS. Because every visual assertion in the suite failed simultaneously, the team assumed a catastrophic rendering regression and spent six hours bisecting commits before tracing the root cause to the OS mismatch.
Fix: Always generate and update snapshot baselines on the same OS as CI (typically Linux/Ubuntu). Configure `snapshotPathTemplate` in `playwright.config.ts` to embed `{platform}` in the path (e.g., `{testDir}/__screenshots__/{platform}/{testFilePath}/{arg}{ext}`) so macOS and Linux baselines are stored in separate directories and never compared cross-platform. Alternatively, run `--update-snapshots` exclusively inside a Docker container matching the CI image to guarantee identical rendering conditions.

---

**G104: `page.evaluate()` closures cannot capture `const`/`let` variables from the outer Node.js test scope — variables referenced inside the callback are `undefined` in the browser context, and Playwright throws no error, silently producing wrong results.**
Why this matters: A charter test declared `const expectedUserId = 'user-42'` in the test body, then wrote `await page.evaluate(() => document.querySelector('[data-user-id="' + expectedUserId + '"]') !== null)`. This always returned `false` because `expectedUserId` was `undefined` in the browser's V8 context — `page.evaluate()` serialises the function as a string and re-evaluates it in the browser, where the outer Node.js variable does not exist. The charter silently reported the user-ID element as absent for every run, and the team spent a sprint investigating a non-existent rendering bug.
Fix: Always pass outer-scope values via the second argument of `page.evaluate()`: `await page.evaluate((uid) => document.querySelector('[data-user-id="' + uid + '"]') !== null, expectedUserId)`. The argument is JSON-serialised and injected as the first callback parameter. Add the `eslint-plugin-playwright` `no-eval` lint rule (or a custom `no-restricted-syntax` rule) to detect `page.evaluate()` calls with closures over outer-scope `const`/`let` at lint time before they reach CI.

**Pattern 563** — `page.route()` Conditional Chaos Injection per Charter Scenario
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

type FaultProfile = { url: string; status: number; body: Record<string, unknown>; delayMs: number };

const faultProfiles: Record<string, FaultProfile> = {
  'cart-timeout':    { url: '**/api/cart/**',    status: 503, body: { error: 'service unavailable' }, delayMs: 6000 },
  'payment-reject':  { url: '**/api/payments/**', status: 402, body: { error: 'card_declined' },       delayMs: 200  },
  'inventory-stale': { url: '**/api/inventory**', status: 200, body: { available: false, qty: 0 },     delayMs: 0    },
};

for (const [scenario, fault] of Object.entries(faultProfiles)) {
  test(`CHARTER: checkout resilience — ${scenario}`, async ({ page }) => {
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'fault-scenario', value: scenario });

    await page.route(fault.url, async (route) => {
      if (fault.delayMs > 0) await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, fault.delayMs));
      await route.fulfill({ status: fault.status, contentType: 'application/json', body: JSON.stringify(fault.body) });
    });

    await page.goto('/checkout');
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /place order/i }).click();

    const alertOrError = page.locator('[role="alert"], [data-testid="error-banner"]');
    await expect(alertOrError).toBeVisible({ timeout: 10_000 });

    const errorText = await alertOrError.textContent();
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'fault-ui-response', value: errorText ?? '(empty)' });
  });
}
```
Tradeoff: Parameterising fault profiles as a static dictionary makes every scenario visible in the Playwright test list before any test runs and lets CI selectively re-run only failing fault scenarios by name with `--grep`, but the dictionary lives in the test file — if the API URL patterns change (e.g., a versioning migration from `/api/` to `/api/v2/`), all fault routes silently stop matching and the tests pass with zero fault injection; centralise URL patterns in a shared `api-routes.ts` constant that both app code and test fault profiles import, and add a route-match assertion (`expect(interceptedCount).toBeGreaterThan(0)` after the action) to detect silent route-miss regressions.

**Pattern 564** — `test.step()` Hierarchical Charter Tree for Multi-Phase Sessions
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('CHARTER: onboarding flow — new-user end-to-end exploration', async ({ page }) => {
  await test.step('Phase 1: Registration boundary exploration', async () => {
    await test.step('1a: duplicate email rejection', async () => {
      await page.goto('/register');
      await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('existing@example.com');
      await page.getByLabel('Password').fill('ValidPass1!');
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: /create account/i }).click();
      await expect(page.locator('[role="alert"]')).toContainText(/already.*registered|email.*taken/i);
      test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:finding', value: '1a: duplicate email error present' });
    });

    await test.step('1b: password complexity boundary', async () => {
      await page.goto('/register');
      await page.getByLabel('Email').fill('newuser+pw@example.com');
      for (const pw of ['short', 'alllowercase1', 'ALLUPPERCASE1', 'NoSpecialChar1']) {
        await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(pw);
        await page.getByRole('button', { name: /create account/i }).click();
        const hint = await page.locator('[data-testid="pw-strength"]').textContent().catch(() => null);
        test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:pw-boundary', value: `${pw} → ${hint}` });
      }
    });
  });

  await test.step('Phase 2: Email verification flow exploration', async () => {
    await page.goto('/verify-email?token=valid-fixture-token');
    await expect(page).toHaveURL(/dashboard|welcome/);
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:finding', value: 'Phase 2: email verify redirects to dashboard' });
  });

  await test.step('Phase 3: Profile completion nudge exploration', async () => {
    const nudge = page.locator('[data-testid="profile-completion-banner"]');
    const nudgeVisible = await nudge.isVisible().catch(() => false);
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:profile-nudge', value: nudgeVisible ? 'present' : 'absent' });
    if (nudgeVisible) await expect(nudge).toContainText(/complete.*profile|add.*photo/i);
  });
});
```
Tradeoff: Nesting charter phases inside `test.step()` blocks produces a structured timeline in the Playwright HTML report with per-phase pass/fail indicators and step-level screenshot attachment points, which dramatically accelerates post-session triage compared to a flat test; but each `test.step()` that throws halts all subsequent phases in the same test, meaning a blocking bug in Phase 1 prevents Phase 2 and Phase 3 from running at all — split independent charter phases into separate `test()` blocks sharing state via a `storageState` fixture when phase independence is more valuable than the unified session view.

**Pattern 565** — `page.accessibility.snapshot()` Pre/Post Action ARIA Tree Diff
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

async function captureAriaTree(page: import('@playwright/test').Page, label: string): Promise<string> {
  const snapshot = await page.accessibility.snapshot({ interestingOnly: true });
  const serialised = JSON.stringify(snapshot, null, 2);
  test.info().attachments.push({
    name: `aria-tree-${label}.json`,
    contentType: 'application/json',
    body: Buffer.from(serialised),
  });
  return serialised;
}

test('CHARTER: modal dialog — ARIA tree mutation on open/close', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/dashboard');

  const before = await captureAriaTree(page, 'before-modal-open');

  await page.getByRole('button', { name: /open settings/i }).click();
  const modalLocator = page.getByRole('dialog');
  await expect(modalLocator).toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });
  const during = await captureAriaTree(page, 'during-modal-open');

  await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
  await expect(modalLocator).not.toBeVisible({ timeout: 3000 });
  const after = await captureAriaTree(page, 'after-modal-close');

  // Charter finding: focus management — focus must return to trigger button
  const focusedAfterClose = await page.evaluate(() => document.activeElement?.getAttribute('aria-label') ?? 'unknown');
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:focus-return', value: focusedAfterClose });

  // Structural diff: modal role must appear during and disappear after
  expect(during).toMatch(/"role":\s*"dialog"/);
  expect(after).not.toMatch(/"role":\s*"dialog"/);

  // Aria tree must be identical before and after (no leaked ARIA nodes)
  expect(before).toEqual(after);
});
```
Tradeoff: Attaching serialised ARIA trees as JSON report artifacts creates a permanent, diff-able accessibility audit trail for each charter session and surfaces leaked ARIA nodes (orphaned `role="dialog"` after close) that visual snapshots miss entirely, but `page.accessibility.snapshot({ interestingOnly: true })` prunes nodes Playwright deems uninteresting — custom components using non-semantic `<div>` elements with manually managed `aria-*` attributes may be silently excluded from the snapshot, making the diff appear clean while real accessibility regressions exist; supplement with `page.ariaSnapshot()` (the string-based format added in Playwright 1.44) for full-fidelity tree capture when testing custom ARIA implementations.

**Pattern 566** — `browser.newContext()` Session Fork for Concurrent-User Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('CHARTER: shared document — concurrent edit conflict exploration', async ({ browser }) => {
  const [authorCtx, reviewerCtx] = await Promise.all([
    browser.newContext({ storageState: 'fixtures/auth/author.json' }),
    browser.newContext({ storageState: 'fixtures/auth/reviewer.json' }),
  ]);

  const [authorPage, reviewerPage] = await Promise.all([
    authorCtx.newPage(),
    reviewerCtx.newPage(),
  ]);

  try {
    await Promise.all([
      authorPage.goto('/documents/doc-fixture-001'),
      reviewerPage.goto('/documents/doc-fixture-001'),
    ]);

    const authorEditor = authorPage.locator('[data-testid="editor-body"]');
    await authorEditor.click();
    await authorEditor.fill('Author draft v1');

    const reviewerEditor = reviewerPage.locator('[data-testid="editor-body"]');
    await reviewerEditor.click();
    await reviewerEditor.fill('Reviewer concurrent edit');

    await authorPage.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).click();
    await expect(authorPage.locator('[data-testid="save-confirmation"]')).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5000 });

    await reviewerPage.getByRole('button', { name: /save/i }).click();
    const conflictBanner = reviewerPage.locator('[data-testid="conflict-banner"], [role="alert"]');
    const conflictVisible = await conflictBanner.isVisible({ timeout: 5000 }).catch(() => false);
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: 'charter:conflict-ui',
      value: conflictVisible ? 'conflict banner shown' : 'silent overwrite — RISK',
    });
  } finally {
    await Promise.all([authorCtx.close(), reviewerCtx.close()]);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Using `browser.newContext()` with separate `storageState` files to simulate concurrent users in a single Playwright test eliminates the need for a multi-process test harness and lets the charter observe race conditions in a deterministic single run, but both contexts share the same Playwright CDP connection pool — very high-frequency concurrent interactions (100+ events/second) can create CDP backpressure that serialises actions which should be truly parallel, masking race conditions that only surface under genuine concurrent load; for true concurrency stress, run the same charter with `--workers 2` and coordinate via a shared HTTP fixture server rather than in-process context forking.

**Pattern 567** — `page.evaluate()` Heap Memory Sampler for Long-Session Leak Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

interface HeapSample { label: string; usedMB: number; totalMB: number; timestamp: number }

async function sampleHeap(page: import('@playwright/test').Page, label: string): Promise<HeapSample> {
  const memory = await page.evaluate(() => ({
    used:  (performance as unknown as { memory?: { usedJSHeapSize: number } }).memory?.usedJSHeapSize  ?? 0,
    total: (performance as unknown as { memory?: { totalJSHeapSize: number } }).memory?.totalJSHeapSize ?? 0,
  }));
  const sample: HeapSample = {
    label,
    usedMB:  Math.round(memory.used  / 1_048_576 * 100) / 100,
    totalMB: Math.round(memory.total / 1_048_576 * 100) / 100,
    timestamp: Date.now(),
  };
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'heap', value: JSON.stringify(sample) });
  return sample;
}

test('CHARTER: data-grid — heap growth across 50 page-navigation cycles', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto('/reports/grid');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const baseline = await sampleHeap(page, 'baseline');
  const samples: HeapSample[] = [baseline];

  for (let i = 0; i < 50; i++) {
    await page.getByRole('button', { name: /next page/i }).click();
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    if (i % 10 === 9) samples.push(await sampleHeap(page, `cycle-${i + 1}`));
  }

  const finalSample = await sampleHeap(page, 'final');
  samples.push(finalSample);

  const growthMB = finalSample.usedMB - baseline.usedMB;
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:heap-growth-mb', value: String(growthMB) });

  // Charter heuristic: >50 MB growth across 50 cycles is a leak candidate
  expect(growthMB, `Heap grew by ${growthMB} MB across 50 pagination cycles — suspected leak`).toBeLessThan(50);
});
```
Tradeoff: Sampling `performance.memory` via `page.evaluate()` provides a zero-dependency heap growth signal that works in any Chromium-based browser without enabling CDP directly, and per-cycle annotations make trends visible in the HTML report timeline; but `performance.memory` is a non-standard V8 API available only in Chrome/Edge (not Firefox or WebKit) and its values are quantised by GC reporting granularity — gradual leaks of 1–5 MB per cycle may appear as a flat line until the GC decides to report; complement with `--enable-precise-memory-info` in Chromium launch args and invoke `page.evaluate(() => gc())` (requires `--js-flags="--expose-gc"`) before each sample to force a collection cycle and eliminate GC noise from the heap delta.

**Pattern 568** — `page.addLocatorHandler()` Interstitial Dismissal During Free-Form Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

test('CHARTER: pricing page — feature exploration with auto-dismissal of overlays', async ({ page }) => {
  const dismissedOverlays: string[] = [];

  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.locator('[data-testid="cookie-consent"], #onetrust-accept-btn-handler, .cc-dismiss'),
    async (locator) => {
      await locator.click();
      dismissedOverlays.push('cookie-consent');
    }
  );

  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.locator('[data-testid="promo-modal"] button[aria-label*="close" i]'),
    async (locator) => {
      await locator.click();
      dismissedOverlays.push('promo-modal');
    }
  );

  await page.addLocatorHandler(
    page.locator('[data-testid="survey-nudge"]'),
    async () => {
      await page.keyboard.press('Escape');
      dismissedOverlays.push('survey-nudge');
    }
  );

  await page.goto('/pricing');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  for (const tier of ['starter', 'pro', 'enterprise']) {
    await page.locator(`[data-testid="tier-${tier}"]`).click();
    await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');
    const price = await page.locator('[data-testid="tier-price"]').textContent();
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:tier-price', value: `${tier}: ${price}` });
  }

  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:dismissed-overlays', value: dismissedOverlays.join(', ') || 'none' });
});
```
Tradeoff: `page.addLocatorHandler()` (introduced in Playwright 1.44) allows interstitial overlays to be dismissed automatically whenever Playwright's auto-waiting encounters them blocking an action, preventing charter tests from aborting on cookie banners or promotional modals; but handlers run asynchronously outside the test's action flow — if a handler dismisses a modal that is itself the feature under charter (e.g., an intentionally triggered upsell modal), the handler silently swallows it before the assertion runs, producing a false-negative; scope all handler selectors exclusively to non-content overlays using `data-testid` values controlled by the QA team, and log every dismissal to annotations so post-session review can confirm no chartered interactions were intercepted.

**Pattern 569** — `page.clock.runFor()` SLA Timer Boundary Charter
```typescript
import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';

const SLA_THRESHOLDS_MS = [
  { label: 'warning',  ms:  30_000 },
  { label: 'critical', ms:  60_000 },
  { label: 'breach',   ms: 120_000 },
];

test('CHARTER: support ticket — SLA countdown boundary states', async ({ page }) => {
  await page.clock.install({ time: new Date('2026-01-01T10:00:00Z') });
  await page.goto('/support/tickets/fixture-ticket-001');
  await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle');

  const slaIndicator = page.locator('[data-testid="sla-indicator"]');
  await expect(slaIndicator).toBeVisible({ timeout: 5_000 });
  const baseline = await slaIndicator.getAttribute('data-sla-status');
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:sla-baseline', value: baseline ?? 'unknown' });

  let elapsed = 0;
  for (const threshold of SLA_THRESHOLDS_MS) {
    await page.clock.runFor(threshold.ms - elapsed);
    elapsed = threshold.ms;

    const status = await slaIndicator.getAttribute('data-sla-status');
    const colour = await slaIndicator.evaluate(el => getComputedStyle(el).color);
    test.info().annotations.push({
      type: `charter:sla-${threshold.label}`,
      value: `status="${status}" color="${colour}"`,
    });
    await expect(slaIndicator).toHaveAttribute('data-sla-status', threshold.label);
  }
});
```
Tradeoff: Advancing synthetic time through SLA thresholds with `page.clock.runFor()` enables deterministic, millisecond-precise boundary testing of timer-driven UI states in under a second regardless of the SLA duration; but `page.clock.runFor()` only advances the browser-side synthetic clock — server-rendered SLA data computed at request time will reflect the real server time rather than the synthetic time, so `data-sla-status` attributes set by server-side rendering will not change; verify the SLA countdown is driven entirely by client-side JS reading `Date.now()` before relying on this pattern, and stub the SLA endpoint response to return a countdown value consistent with the synthetic clock's starting point.

**Pattern 570** — Worker-Scoped Fixture for Shared Authentication State Across Charter Suite
```typescript
import { test as base, BrowserContext } from '@playwright/test';
import * as fs from 'fs';
import * as path from 'path';

const test = base.extend<object, { authedContext: BrowserContext }>({
  authedContext: [async ({ browser }, use) => {
    const stateFile = path.join('fixtures', 'auth', `worker-state-${process.env.TEST_WORKER_INDEX ?? '0'}.json`);
    let ctx: BrowserContext;

    if (fs.existsSync(stateFile)) {
      ctx = await browser.newContext({ storageState: stateFile });
    } else {
      ctx = await browser.newContext();
      const page = await ctx.newPage();
      await page.goto('/login');
      await page.getByLabel('Email').fill(process.env.QA_USER_EMAIL ?? 'qa@example.com');
      await page.getByLabel('Password').fill(process.env.QA_USER_PASSWORD ?? 'QaPassword1!');
      await page.getByRole('button', { name: /sign in/i }).click();
      await page.waitForURL(/dashboard/, { timeout: 10_000 });
      await ctx.storageState({ path: stateFile });
      await page.close();
    }

    await use(ctx);
    await ctx.close();
  }, { scope: 'worker' }],
});

test('CHARTER: billing settings — invoice download exploration', async ({ authedContext }) => {
  const page = await authedContext.newPage();
  await page.goto('/settings/billing');

  const invoiceRows = page.locator('[data-testid="invoice-row"]');
  const count = await invoiceRows.count();
  test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:invoice-count', value: String(count) });

  if (count > 0) {
    const [download] = await Promise.all([
      page.waitForEvent('download'),
      invoiceRows.first().getByRole('button', { name: /download/i }).click(),
    ]);
    test.info().annotations.push({ type: 'charter:invoice-download', value: download.suggestedFilename() });
    expect(download.suggestedFilename()).toMatch(/\.pdf$/i);
  }
  await page.close();
});
```
Tradeoff: A worker-scoped `authedContext` fixture amortises login cost from O(n-tests) to O(n-workers), and the per-worker `storageState` file enables session reuse across retries; but the shared context means any test mutating account state (password change, resource deletion, billing modification) corrupts the context for all subsequent tests in the same worker — restrict the worker context to read-only charter exploration and create fresh `browser.newContext()` instances inside any mutating test, or add an `afterEach` hook that reloads the storage state from the original fixture file to reset session mutations between tests.
